negative_cases.description: An accepted durable Circle-scoped Event (e.g. ck.message.create whose Flow scope_circle_id is set) MUST carry the reducer-stamped effective_scope on its envelope. An offline validator / cotest MUST reject an accepted event whose object is Circle-scoped but whose effective_scope is absent, otherwise the §9.3 'Circle scoped event not delivered to non-members' invariant cannot be deterministically replayed. event-envelope.schema.json carries effective_scope as a reducer-stamped field; this vector pins that accepted (post-reducer) Circle events MUST populate it.

negative_cases.description: The reducer-stamped effective_scope MUST be derived from the object's scope_circle_id: scope_circle_id=null -> {kind:realm}; scope_circle_id=C -> {kind:circle, circle_id:C}. A materialized object / accepted event whose effective_scope.circle_id disagrees with its scope_circle_id is corrupt; reducer MUST schema_violation (effective_scope_reducer_managed) on write and a validator MUST reject on read.
negative_cases.name: effective_scope_mismatches_scope_circle_id

negative_cases.description: effective_scope is part of an Event's canonical bytes, so event_digest = H(canonical bytes) binds it directly. If a Seal later reports the DataEvent inside data_event_set_root, that root is an observational availability/projection proof, not control-plane finality. Mutating effective_scope after signing changes event_digest, so the recomputed digest no longer matches the signed event. Receivers MUST reject with digest_mismatch; this forbids silently re-scoping an accepted event and is why no separate scope field is added to seal.schema.json (the binding is the digest).
negative_cases.name: seal_leaf_effective_scope_tamper

negative_cases.description: Realm.content_encryption_floor=e2ee_required requires every Flow/Message/Morph/Blob content effective_scope to be MLS-backed (Realm-default MLS or Circle MLS). cases.name: or_set_dedup_double_add_same_actor
cases.notes: Two add events from the same actor with the same key collapse to one OR-Set membership entry; the per-event audit log retains both.

cases.name: or_set_concurrent_add_remove_remove_wins_in_default_view
cases.notes: Two events from the same actor with no causal_refs between them; default view applies per-actor causal closure — concurrent (add, remove) collapses to the remove because the remove is itself a tombstone for the actor's adds in the concurrent past per OR-Set semantics chosen for ck.reaction.

cases.name: dangling_reaction_before_target_arrives
cases.notes: Reaction whose target_ref has not been observed yet MUST be held in pending; reducer materialises the OR-Set entry only after the target message becomes available.

cases.name: target_redacted_drops_default_view_keeps_audit
cases.notes: When the target message is redacted, the default view summary MUST NOT expose reaction members; the audit view retains the reaction events under the redaction stub.

cases.name: e2ee_routing_digest_dedup
cases.notes: In an E2EE realm the plaintext key is the v1 keyed-HMAC routing tag: HMAC-SHA256(key = MLS-Exporter("cokret-reaction-routing-v1", context = realm_id), data = NFC(canonical_emoji)); see zh/crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md §2.9. The 32-byte tag is carried in `key` as a 256-bit hex digest (the sha256: prefix below denotes the digest wire-encoding, not the derivation). Two adds with the same routing tag from the same actor in the same epoch collapse to one OR-Set membership; the tag differs in a different epoch because the MLS exporter secret rotates on every commit, so it does not dedup across epochs. realm_id is bound via the exporter context, providing defense-in-depth even if mls_group_id is reused across deployments.

cases.name: e2ee_epoch_rotation_breaks_dedup
cases.notes: Same canonical emoji yields a different routing hash after MLS epoch rotation; the new add is a fresh OR-Set entry, not a duplicate of the pre-rotation one.

cases.name: capability_revoked_blocks_subsequent_add
cases.notes: After ck.capability.revoke removes the actor's ck.reaction.add capability, the next add MUST be rejected before reducer state changes; in-flight events accepted before the revoke causal frontier remain in OR-Set state.

cases.name: rate_limit_high_rate_reaction_burst
cases.notes: Servers MAY rate-limit ck.reaction.add per actor; the reducer MUST treat rate-limited events as either rate_limited or quarantine, never as accepted-then-silently-dropped.

parser_tier_definitions.current_parser: Sync service, federation peer, snapshot consumer, reducer, conformance test runner — anything that processes live or persisted v1 wire bytes. MUST treat every entry in this file as forbidden in input; MUST NOT do payload-shape disambiguation; reject with the schema's standard unknown_kind / unknown_field / schema_violation error.
parser_tier_definitions.migration_tool: Offline batch tool that reads pre-v1 / pre-inversion bytes and rewrites them to canonical v1 form. May consult migration_tool_only entries (those carrying the explicit flag) and apply their disambiguation_payload_shape rule. MUST NOT be embedded in a real-time parser surface (no inline transform; no 'auto-accept legacy and quietly rewrite'). This tier-only allowance is expressed by the `legacy_migration` allowed_context plus, where applicable, the `migration_tool_only` flag — never by a reader-facing tolerance window.

rejection_levels.compat_only: MUST appear only on explicitly opt-in interop / compatibility surfaces (e.g., MIMI interop module).
rejection_levels.docs_only: Removed from wire / code; references survive only in CHANGELOG, glossary deprecation notices, or migration guides.
rejection_levels.hard_reject: MUST be rejected at parse/reducer time. No legitimate occurrence on current wire or in current code.
rejection_levels.migration_only: Tolerated only inside offline migration / replay tools, NEVER in current v1 wire parsers. Current parsers (sync, federation, snapshot consumers, reducer, conformance runner) MUST reject the old identifier without inspecting payload shape; migration_tool_only entries carry the `migration_tool_only: true` flag to make this enforceable. There is no in-band reader tolerance window; the prior 'bounded migration window readers MAY tolerate' language has been retired.

migration_group_definitions.agent_applet_interop_session_rename: Agent and applet session surfaces renamed from the ambiguous `protocol_session` (which reads as the ambient Cokret protocol) to `interop_session`, naming the external agent-to-agent interop relationship. Event kinds ck.{agent,applet}.protocol_session.* -> ck.{agent,applet}.interop_session.*; the agent capability action namespace ck.agent.session.* (start/cancel/stream_status/attach_artifact/read_transcript) -> ck.agent.interop_session.*; the typed id and schema payload defs use the agent_interop_session_* / applet_interop_session_* short form. Single design decision.
migration_group_definitions.agent_key_imperative_verbs: Event kind verbs use imperative action names, not past participles. cx.agent.key.{authorized,revoked,rotated} → cx.agent.key.{authorize,revoke,rotate} (3 entries).
migration_group_definitions.agent_session_namespace_collapse: Superseded by agent_applet_interop_session_rename: the agent capability action namespace and the agent/applet session event kinds now both use the interop_session form.
migration_group_definitions.blob_reference_naming: Blob references use <noun>_blob_ref when the role noun is not already blob.
migration_group_definitions.brand_namespace_cx_to_ck: Wire/brand namespace renamed from the legacy `contrix` brand to `cokret`. Every wire token prefix `cx.` becomes `ck.` and every typed-id prefix `cx:` becomes `ck:` across operation_id, event_kind, schema_id, capability action, id_kind, error code, vector id, and profile id. The bare brand strings `contrix` / `Contrix` and the token prefixes `cx.` / `cx:` are hard_reject on the current wire and in current identifiers (allowed only in CHANGELOG / migration docs / negative drift fixtures). HTTP paths additionally moved to the versionless trust-circle namespace `/_cokret/<segment>/...` (see sync/service-http-binding.md §2.1); the legacy flat paths and `/api/v1` / `/cokret/v1` prefixes are recorded in removed-operation-ids.json. Mechanical, single design decision; the entries below are representative seals, the rule applies to the whole token space.
migration_group_definitions.cba_notary_seal_rename: CBA terminology family rename (2026-06-11): the Anchor/Anchorer word family is replaced by Seal/Notary across wire fields, typed-id prefixes, cell families, enum values and model names; the Seal cumulative-coverage frontier[] enumeration is retired in favor of predecessor_refs + delta recursion (no direct field successor; the snapshot manifest's boundary `frontier` object and the streaming `frontier` frame kind are true-frontier semantics and keep their names); proposal-era interim spellings (governance_ref, Checkpoint) are forbidden. See authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md and overview/glossary.md.
migration_group_definitions.claim_kind_discriminator: Closed protocol-level claim discriminators use claim_kind; external credential taxonomy selectors may continue to use claim_type.
migration_group_definitions.conformance_verifier_neutralization: ServiceDescribe.verified_profiles neutralized away from the downstream tool name cotest: claim_kind enum value cotest_verified → conformance_verified, wire fields cotest_run_id → verification_run_id and cotest_issuer_did → verifier_did. The wire contract binds to the neutral Conformance Verifier role (conformance-suite.md §6.2); cotest survives only as an informative reference-implementation name in prose (3 entries).
migration_group_definitions.crdt_lattice_snake_case: CRDT lattice enum values use snake_case (5 entries).
migration_group_definitions.device_imperative_verbs: Same rule as agent_key_imperative_verbs but for device key events (2 entries).
migration_group_definitions.did_id_suffix: Protocol responsibility subjects use the _id suffix even when the value is a DID. actor_did / principal_did / subject_did renamed to actor_id / principal_id / subject_id, and the bare wire fields `actor` (policy check request, bound_to, capability vector request; MIMI consent update request) and `requester` (MIMI consent request) renamed to actor_id / requester_id (6 entries).
migration_group_definitions.duration_iso8601: Human-readable policy duration wire strings use ISO 8601 (^P...) as the single v1 format; the self-invented compact ^[0-9]+(ms|s|m|h|d)$ mini-DSL is forbidden. Machine timing fields keep integer _ms / _seconds. See common-fields.md §3.0.2.
migration_group_definitions.frank_to_franking_proof_noun: Moderation franking objects use the full franking_proof noun (4 entries).
migration_group_definitions.full_word_field_names: Protocol wire fields use full nouns for signature/public_key/base64url material rather than sig/pubkey/b64 abbreviations.
migration_group_definitions.grant_constraint_single_kind_ids: Grant constraint fields that carry one concrete protocol identifier kind use `_ids`; `_refs` remains reserved for causal/proof/schema/content-addressed or polymorphic reference material.
migration_group_definitions.hash_to_digest_vocabulary: Wire fields carrying hash output bytes use _digest with self-describing <alg>:<hex>; algorithm selectors use _algorithm; tree roots use _root. _hash is forbidden as wire field-name suffix (~50 entries).
migration_group_definitions.key_backup_kdf_hash_to_digest_algorithm: Key backup KDF parameter algorithm selectors use digest_algorithm; hash is reserved for actual digest material and internal JSON Schema defs.
migration_group_definitions.metadata_encryption_floor_rename: Wire field metadata_encryption_profile renamed to metadata_encryption_floor.
migration_group_definitions.operation_id_trust_surface_segment: Scheme B: operation_id now encodes its trust-surface classifier as the mandatory leading segment (ck.<surface>.<resource>.<action>, surface in {self,peer,edge,root,find,gate,open}), matching the HTTP path's first segment 1:1. 108 operations gain the surface prefix; peer.* were already compliant and ck.server.describe (pre-auth root meta, no surface segment) is the sole exception. grpc service names gain the PascalCase surface prefix and mq topics the lowercase surface segment in lockstep. Single design decision; entries are mechanical applications.
migration_group_definitions.realm_lifecycle_segment_realignment: Realm lifecycle capability actions flattened from 4 segments (cx.realm.lifecycle.<verb>) to 3 segments (cx.realm.<verb>) to match the corresponding event kind (4 entries). target_event_kinds preserved.
migration_group_definitions.signature_algorithm_vocabulary: Signature and key algorithm selector fields use the full _algorithm suffix; JOSE/JWK nested headers may still use standard alg.
migration_group_definitions.status_axis_timestamp: Status-axis transition timestamps use status_changed_at instead of a bare changed_at.
migration_group_definitions.typed_id_prefix_unabbreviation: Abbreviated typed-id prefixes expanded to full snake_case kind. Single rule: ck:<abbrev>: → ck:<full_kind>: (9 entries).
migration_group_definitions.verb_noun_bridge_collapse: Capability actions converged back to noun form matching their target event kind. The earlier verb-form action names (.manage / .modify / create_*) are forbidden; new IAM tools can use the event kind string verbatim as the action token. 6 entries; v3 (2026-05-24). See authz/capabilities.md §5.0a.

parser_tier_definitions.current_parser: Sync service, federation peer, snapshot consumer, reducer, conformance test runner — anything that processes live or persisted v1 wire bytes. MUST treat every entry in this file as forbidden in input; MUST NOT do payload-shape disambiguation; reject with the schema's standard unknown_kind / unknown_field / schema_violation error.
parser_tier_definitions.migration_tool: Offline batch tool that reads pre-v1 / pre-inversion bytes and rewrites them to canonical v1 form. May consult migration_tool_only entries (those carrying the explicit flag) and apply their disambiguation_payload_shape rule. MUST NOT be embedded in a real-time parser surface (no inline transform; no 'auto-accept legacy and quietly rewrite').

rejection_levels.compat_only: Old form retained only on explicit interop surfaces.
rejection_levels.docs_only: Old form survives in CHANGELOG / migration docs only.
rejection_levels.hard_reject: After replacement, the old identifier MUST NOT appear in current code or wire bytes. Current v1 parsers MUST reject the old identifier without inspecting payload shape.
rejection_levels.migration_only: Tolerated only inside offline migration / replay tools, NEVER in current v1 wire parsers. Current parsers (sync, federation, snapshot consumers, reducer) MUST reject the old identifier without inspecting payload shape; migration_tool_only entries below carry the `migration_tool_only: true` flag to make this enforceable. The 'mechanical replacement window' language has been retired — there is no in-band tolerance.

additional_requirements.canonical_reducer_output_must: Reducer MUST stamp tagged effective_scope on accepted Event envelope and materialized object cell. effective_scope is immutable per-event; later scope_circle_id rebinds MUST NOT re-interpret historical events.
additional_requirements.circle_content_encryption_floor_must: Circle.content_encryption_floor (allow_plaintext | e2ee_required) is optional and symmetric with Circle.metadata_encryption_floor: when omitted it inherits the parent Realm content_encryption_floor, and the effective floor = max(parent Realm content_encryption_floor, Circle content_encryption_floor). Reducer MUST reject a Circle floor below the effective floor and MUST reject content_encryption_floor=e2ee_required on an encryption_profile=none Circle (reason=circle_encryption_below_realm_floor). See zh/models/circle.md §7.
additional_requirements.circle_encryption_profile_floor_must: Circle.encryption_profile may be none or mls_rfc9420. Reducer MUST reject plaintext Circle creation or update when the parent Realm encryption_profile is mls_rfc9420 or the effective content_encryption_floor is e2ee_required (reason=circle_encryption_below_realm_floor).
additional_requirements.circle_membership_subset_must: Circle.members MUST be a strict subset of parent Realm.members; reducer MUST reject ck.circle.member.state -> join when the target actor is not a `join` member of the parent Realm (reason=circle_member_must_be_realm_member).
additional_requirements.encryption_floor_ratchet_must: The effective content_encryption_floor and effective metadata encryption floor of any scope (Realm-default or Circle) are one-way ratchets: monotonically non-decreasing over time. A ck.realm.policy_components or ck.circle.update that lowers the effective content floor from e2ee_required to allow_plaintext MUST be rejected (reason=content_encryption_floor_downgrade); one that lowers the effective metadata floor MUST be rejected (reason=metadata_encryption_floor_downgrade). Tightening is always allowed. Vectors: ck.vector.e2ee.content_floor_downgrade_rejected.v1, ck.vector.e2ee.metadata_floor_downgrade_rejected.v1, ck.vector.circle.content_floor_below_realm_rejected.v1, ck.vector.e2ee.in_place_enable.v1.
additional_requirements.scope_invariant_must: Sync Service MUST NOT deliver events with effective_scope.kind=circle to actors not in that Circle's member frontier at the event's causal frontier (see zh/models/circle.md §9.3 scope-delivery invariant).
additional_requirements.scope_rebind_default_reject_must: Default reducer MUST reject scope_circle_id rebind (None<->Some, Some(A)->Some(B)) with failed_precondition reason=scope_rebind_forbidden. Profile-declared audit-paired rebind MAY be permitted, but MUST emit ck.audit.accessed pairing.
additional_requirements.submit_payload_must: Submit payload for ck.flow.create / ck.message.create / ck.morph.create / ck.relation.create / ck.space.create / ck.space.parent MUST carry only scope_circle_id (id:circle | null). Reducer MUST reject any submit payload that also carries effective_scope (reason=effective_scope_reducer_managed).

ck.profile.cross_signing.reset.v1.description: Hardening profile for high-risk cross-signing reset. Claimants MUST accept ck.cross_signing.reset only with one valid reset proof family, enforce generation monotonicity, clock skew, and replay rejection, and require a successor ck.cross_signing.publish within the recovery window. Verification rules and reason codes are normative in zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §14.4.

max_clock_skew_seconds.rationale: Maximum allowed deviation between `ck.cross_signing.reset.issued_at` and receiver local clock. Default 300s mirrors policy-decision freshness windows; receivers MAY tighten down to 60s for high-assurance deployments or relax up to 900s for federated peers with documented clock skew. Beyond the configured value receivers MUST emit cross_signing_reset_clock_skew_exceeded.

publish_recovery_window_seconds.rationale: Maximum interval after an accepted reset within which the successor ck.cross_signing.publish MUST be observed; receivers MUST otherwise enter the 'no usable SSK/USK' state from §14.2 step 5. Default 24h matches the §14.1 normative requirement.

reset_replay_cache_min_retention_seconds.rationale: Minimum retention for the (principal_id, previous_generation) replay-rejection cache used by §14.4 通用规则. MUST be at least `publish_recovery_window_seconds + 3600` so that no late-arriving duplicate reset can bypass the cache before the successor publish window closes. Default = 24h + 1h slack.

ck.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1.description: Degraded E2EE profile. Allows `mls_send_pause="advisory"` (cf. §2.4.1) so that low-latency interactive scenarios (real-time AV, collaborative editing, in-game chat) do not block message send on MLS commit completion. Cost: removed members can continue decrypting a small window of subsequent messages. NOT for general chat / collaboration / compliance use. MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with ck.profile.mls_governance_binding.full.v1.

downgrade_window_constraint.compliance_profile_disabled: Profiles in the compliance / audited tier (ck.profile.attested_audit.e2ee.v1, ck.profile.disclosed_audit.e2ee.v1, and any deployment with active Audit Applet Binding) MUST NOT enable ck.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1. Reducer MUST reject the combination with reason_code `e2ee_relaxed_disallowed_in_compliance_profile`. Rationale: compliance assurance presumes the kick-out semantic is cryptographically immediate; the relaxed window contradicts that presumption.
downgrade_window_constraint.rationale: Receiving client refuses to admit a message into verified timeline if the gap between receive_at and the most recent membership_change_at exceeds this window with old-epoch decryption.
downgrade_window_constraint.receiver_enforcement: Receiver MUST enforce the hard ceiling independently of any declared deployment value: if a Realm policy event sets relaxed_window_max_ms > absolute_hard_ceiling_ms (300000 ms / 5 min), the reducer MUST reject the policy update with reason_code `relaxed_window_exceeds_ceiling` (mapped from `schema_violation`), and the receiver MUST treat the policy event as failed_precondition. Receivers MUST NOT silently clamp the value to the ceiling, because a silent clamp would let a deployment publish a longer window than receivers honor and split visible policy state across implementations. Negative vector: `ck.vector.e2ee_relaxed.window_exceeds_ceiling.v1` covers (a) reducer reject on policy write > 300000 ms, (b) receiver reject on old-epoch decrypt admission when the gap exceeds the per-policy declared window, and (c) reject when any deployment tries to redefine the ceiling via an unrelated profile.

They MUST NOT silently accept the advisory string without honoring the relaxed semantics.

additional_requirements.stable_identifier_ban_must: Provider payload MUST NOT contain principal DID, sender DID / handle, Realm id / name, Flow id / name, Message id, event id, device DID URL, reaction emoji, attachment filename, IP, geolocation, or any cross-Realm stable correlation key.

ck.profile.push_gateway.blind_wakeup.v1.description: Default push gateway privacy baseline. Every implementation claiming ck.profile.push_gateway.v1 MUST also claim this profile. Provider-facing payloads MUST NOT carry stable identifying fields (principal DID, sender DID, Realm id / name / avatar, Flow id / name, Message id, event id, device DID URL, reaction value, or any cross-Realm stable correlation key). Payloads MUST be restricted to per-(recipient_service_did, principal, device, push_route) pairwise pseudonym push_target_id + closed-enum wakeup hint fields (wakeup_kind, badge_count, unread_increment, l10n_key). See zh/discovery/push-notifications.md §2.2 / §4.5 / §5.1 and zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §5a.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: MUST fail closed; gateways unable to enforce blind wakeup MUST NOT claim ck.profile.push_gateway.v1

additional_requirements.interop_only_must: This profile is interop-only; it MUST NOT be used as a substitute for ck.profile.push_gateway.blind_wakeup.v1 in default Cokret deployments.
additional_requirements.no_default_mixing_must: Implementations MUST NOT advertise both ck.profile.push_gateway.blind_wakeup.v1 and ck.profile.push_gateway.matrix_passthrough.v1 as applying to the same (recipient_service_did, device) tuple.
additional_requirements.partition_must: Bridges MUST partition push traffic so that Cokret v1 default-baseline peers (ck.profile.push_gateway.blind_wakeup.v1) NEVER receive matrix_passthrough-shaped payloads.

ck.profile.push_gateway.matrix_passthrou.description: Interop compatibility profile for Matrix push gateway passthrough. Implementations claiming this profile MAY accept Matrix-shaped push gateway payloads as an external interop bridge to Matrix push gateways but MUST NOT mix this profile with ck.profile.push_gateway.blind_wakeup.v1 on the same notify path: the Matrix push gateway shape carries identifying fields incompatible with the default Cokret privacy baseline. Bridges MUST partition traffic so that any peer or device negotiated under ck.profile.push_gateway.blind_wakeup.v1 (i.e. the default v1 baseline) NEVER receives a matrix_passthrough payload. See zh/discovery/push-notifications.md §5.1 and zh/conformance/conformance-profiles.md §11.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: omit profile claim; bridges that cannot partition traffic MUST NOT claim this profile

ck.profile.push_gateway.v1.description: Push gateway base profile. Provides the device registration / notify operation surface. ck.profile.push_gateway.visible_notifica.description: Opt-in push gateway profile for deployments that require visible notification fields (e.g. titles, sender labels) in provider payloads. profiles/conformance-profiles.json.profile_roles_rule: Every profile id MUST be annotated with exactly one role from the enum {client, server, gateway, directory, admin, interop}. Roles partition the profile namespace so that an implementation MUST NOT mistake e.g. a gateway profile (push_gateway, blob_node) for a client profile, or a deployment / hardening / vector profile (admin role) for a wire-conformance client / server profile. SDK manifests, client-side feature negotiation, and conformance harness loaders MUST consult `profile_roles` before claiming a profile as locally implemented. Roles in spec layer metadata; the per-profile object in `profile_requirements` MAY ALSO carry a `role` field for convenience, but `profile_roles` is the canonical source.

tier_rules.extension_profile_implementation: Optional. Tracks implementation profiles outside the v1 minimal interop floor, including evolving external standards (MIMI Internet-Drafts; A2A/ACP/MCP unstandardized agent protocols; Applet registry/audit SLA) and opt-in product/privacy features such as productivity, disappearing messages, calendar events, pins, and search. Implementations claiming v1 core MAY omit these entirely; implementations MUST claim only entries they actually support. When an underlying external standard matures, a replacement profile with stable version pinning can supersede that entry.
tier_rules.v1_minimal_interop_floor: Minimum profile for claiming v1 Event Store interop. Higher-level client, service, federation, blob, push, identity, and sovereign profiles remain independently claimable.
tier_rules.v1_profile_catalog: Profiles that belong to the v1 stable catalog. This is not a bundle requirement; implementations MUST claim only the profiles, event kinds, schemas, and operations they actually support.

account_data_types.description: Private per-Realm tags and ordering hints.
Principal-private notification and push rule configuration.
Principal-private do-not-disturb schedule used by notification routing.
Principal-private custom emoji and sticker collection metadata.
Private client UI state such as sidebar, recent realms (canonical key recent_realms), language, and layout preferences.
Holder-private personal blocklist. It affects only the holder's local projection, notifications, contact handling, and trusted holder-side filtering.
Private local remark, note, tag, and pin metadata for an actor, organization, device, or service DID.
Private local remark, note, tag, and pin metadata for a Realm.
Private read-receipt send/display defaults and per-Realm or per-Flow overrides.
Principal-private reminders keyed by opaque id; target_ref and note remain inside encrypted value.
Principal-private scheduled-send plan. planned_message_id is later reused as ck.message.create.payload.message_id.
Principal-private snooze state keyed by HMAC-derived target_key.
Principal-private saved item in an HMAC-derived collection; each item is an independent account-data value.
Principal-private cross-device draft sync key. Raw target_ref MUST NOT appear in the account-data key.

Principal-private cross-device file transfer record keyed by an HMAC-derived transfer_key. Blob bytes are stored through ck.self.blob.*; raw blob_ref, filename, target device ids, and plaintext hashes MUST NOT appear in the account-data key.
Encrypted client search-index manifest keyed by an HMAC-derived realm_key.

Controller-owned encrypted draft created when Principal Server materializes an agent's ck.agent.draft.propose / ck.agent.action_request after capability / policy / accountability / risk check. Draft MUST NOT enter shared Realm history; publishing produces a new shared event referencing only an opaque digest. See CKP-0008 §4.8 / private-objects.md §4.1.

MUST NOT modify target Flow tracks map or write any target-side metadata / Relation / watch / unread / search / notification state. See CKP-0009 §4.14 / private-objects.md §4.1.

Effective participation = effective_ceiling ∩ selection, where the ceiling is the monotone deployment ⊇ Realm ⊇ Circle ⊇ Flow fold. accept_third_party_mention drives the dispatcher mention gate; reply / act_on_behalf materialize into ck.capability.grant. Effective Realm/Circle policy MUST allow the audience and declare finite max_recipients/quota before notification fanout.

event_mapping_kind_definitions.aggregate_admin: Action intentionally covers a bounded administrative family of event kinds.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.non_event_surface: Action authorizes read/projection/signaling behavior that does not emit a durable reducer event.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.operation_verb: Action token names an operation/command verb that does not match its target event kind name(s); reducer admission resolves the resulting event kind(s) via target_event_kinds. Literal action matching per the actions[] rule applies; carries no aggregate-admin family semantics.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.polymorphic_object: Action covers the same object-lifecycle verb across multiple object event kinds.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.same_name: Action maps one-to-one to an identically named durable event kind.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.scope_suffix_variant: Action adds actor/scope/role qualifiers while reducer admission targets a shared event kind.

registry_rules: Wire capability grant.actions[] entries MUST be drawn from this registry; wildcards / segment globs are statically rejected by capability-grant.schema.json.

Receivers MUST default to risk_tier=high when an action submitted in a grant or evaluated in policy is not present in this registry; this is the freshness fail-closed default required by capabilities.md §18.

required_constraints lists typed-constraint shorthand names that the capability evaluator MUST enforce for the action regardless of the grant author's declarations; absence in this list does NOT disable other declared constraints.

required_evaluator_checks lists non-grant-field invariants (for example actor_eq_target_author or audit_pair_required) that admission control MUST enforce from Event context, reducer state, or paired audit evidence. These are not grant-constraint schema fields.

target_event_kinds links the action to one or more ck.* event_kinds in event_kind_registry. Empty array means the action authorizes a read / projection / signaling path that does not produce a durable reducer-input event. Reducer admission for a listed event_kind MUST verify the actor holds at least one matching action grant.

profile is null for v1 core actions, or a ck.profile.*.v<n> id when the action is only meaningful inside that profile. Receivers without the named profile MUST treat the action as unknown (risk_tier=high default).

Every action MUST declare event_mapping_kind. action == single target_event_kind uses same_name; empty target_event_kinds uses non_event_surface; any other mapping MUST use one of the allowed deviation categories.

risk_tier_definitions.medium: Object create / update / delete, message authoring, invite issuance, MLS proposal, audit query. Freshness requires recent frontier within freshness_required_ms.

admission_class_definitions.capability_gated: Gated by one or more named capability actions listed in admission_capabilities. Reducer MUST verify the actor holds a matching action grant per capability-action-registry. Fail-closed.
admission_class_definitions.crypto_verifiable: Admitted by cryptographic verification of the payload against group/key state (MLS epoch, key material, franking) and its policy preconditions. Reducer MUST verify the cryptographic binding; not a user capability. Fail-closed.
admission_class_definitions.self_authored_proof: Admitted by a self-authored proof bound to the subject principal's identity (DID-bound signature / proof of possession with bounded freshness). Reducer MUST verify actor == subject and a fresh, replay-protected proof; no capability grant is consulted. Fail-closed: missing or stale proof MUST be rejected.
admission_class_definitions.service_attested: Written by a protocol service component (Auth/Gate server, Events node, applet host, agent runtime) under its service-DID attestation as part of operating the protocol. Reducer MUST verify the issuing service's authority and its binding to the subject/scope; not a user capability. Fail-closed.

event_kinds.payload: Realm official or sponsoring organization statement

Typed Realm link graph edge. link_kind declares governance / discoverability / import-export / confidential-extension semantics; it is never generic parent/child containment and never implicitly propagates membership, capabilities, history, E2EE keys, retention, or federation policy.
Realm preview / peek policy for directory card, stripped state, history stub, and plaintext history snippet projections
Enabled Realm policy components set. Payload MUST carry monotonic policy_revision; reducer rejects rollback or gaps and policy_frontier_digest MUST cover policy_revision.

Constraints on member delivery_binding: which binding_source values are admissible, which recipient services are allowed, which endorsers are required, whether DID Document fallback / unroutable membership are permitted, who may sign rebind. Governs reducer acceptance of ck.member.state{membership=join}.delivery_binding (see governance/join-policy.md §5.1).

Realm read receipt disclosure policy (disclosure / visibility / scope_overrides_allowed / allow_child_privacy_tightening_against_required); see zh/discovery/read-receipts.md §2.5 for the compliance-floor escape switch
Realm moderation policy (blocklists, allowlists, content filters)
Plaintext-visible services declaration outside E2EE boundary
Per-parent inheritance policy; one entry per source Realm
Realm tombstone lifecycle facet (terminal pointer to successor)
Realm destroy lifecycle facet (terminal decommission marker)
Circle create (intra-Realm scoped event/message boundary). Initializes independent MLS group and epoch-0 governance binding only when encryption_profile=mls_rfc9420. See zh/models/circle.md §3, §5.
Circle patch (ck.patch.v1 with path NOT containing realm_id / encryption_profile). Modifies title / summary / display / directory_visibility / join_rule / history_visibility.
Circle tombstone (terminal). Triggers lifecycle cascade per zh/models/circle.md §9.2.

Circle membership state. Uses the same membership_state enum as ck.member.state (invite/join/knock/leave/ban), scoped to a Circle. Reducer MUST first validate the target actor is a parent Realm `join` member, otherwise failed_precondition reason=circle_member_must_be_realm_member. See zh/models/circle.md §9.1.

Reducer-derived: Circle sub-seal commits opaque sub_seal_head_digest to the Realm Seal stream at the Circle's profile-defined cadence. MUST use time-based ticks + empty-batch commitment to avoid leaking activity frequency. See zh/models/circle.md §10.2.

Issuer-signed endorsement that a subject DID (typically an agent / service / hosted actor) is accountable_principal_ids the issuer for a declared scope (employment / contracted_service / agent_operator / etc.). Required to verify `Actor Profile.accountable_principal_ids[]` entries; reducer strips unverified DIDs from accountable_principal_ids. See zh/models/actor.md §3.3.1.

Notary equivocation evidence (Control Move). Payload carries signer_id plus the two conflicting Seal wire objects: same (realm_id, notary_seq) slot with different canonical bytes, or a notary_seq=k+1 Seal that does not descend from the same signer's notary_seq=k Seal (authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 7.1). Admission is verification-only: any Realm member MAY submit and the two conflicting notary signatures are the complete authorization; no capability grant is consulted and reducer MUST NOT require one. Reducer MUST re-verify both signatures and the slot rule, then add a per-signer fault record to the notary_fault cell. Once a fault record is accepted: receivers MUST reject later Seals signed by the fault signer, the two conflicting Seals and their descendants enter fork_quarantine, and Realm-wide pause applies only when no eligible signer remains.

Notary censorship evidence (Control Move). Payload carries signer_id, the signed control-plane receipt, the seal_ref of the Seal that was obliged to include / signed-reject / defer the pending Control Move, a control_event_set_root non-membership proof for the censored event digest, and the missing rejection-or-defer proof (authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 7.2). Admission is verification-only: the receipt holder MAY submit; the receipt signature plus the non-membership proof are the complete authorization. This evidence does NOT automatically disqualify the notary: reducer adds an audit fault record that MUST raise governance alarms, feeds inclusion-list / recovery obligations, and is evaluated by governance or the genesis recovery path.

Realm-scoped MemberIdentity segment replacement event. Append-only log entry that may supersede prior ck.member.identity.update events via payload.replaces[] without overloading ck.profile.update patch semantics.

Flow business-progression stage transition. Single source of truth for mutating Flow.stage / Flow.stage_changed_at; ck.flow.update patch on those paths MUST be rejected (forbidden-wire). The payload intentionally carries no reason / note / explanation field — rationale belongs in a Message on the Flow's discussion track that 'references' this event, and the event log's own actor_id / created_at is the audit source. Reducer enforces hard invariants from zh/models/common-fields.md §5.3.3: state=redacted yields failed_precondition reason=flow_already_terminal; state=archived yields flow_not_active; same-value self-transition is accepted but does NOT update stage_changed_at; reducer overwrites any wire-supplied stage_changed_at with the event's created_at. A per-Realm workflow profile MAY narrow which transitions are legal beyond these hard invariants.

Unified Flow tracks patch. payload.patch uses ck.patch.v1 against the Flow.tracks map: keys are track names (e.g. `synthesis`, `discussion`), values are patch ops that may toggle enabled, set is_primary, or modify profile / metadata on a track entry. Atomic across multiple tracks.

Flow move between Spaces (target_space_id in payload). Writes a cas_register cell keyed by (board_space_id, flow_id); the contains Relation list_space_id->flow_id is derived from cell value, not a separate truth source. Plane ruling (CBA): ck.component.flow.position.v1 defaults to sealed=true (control plane), so ck.flow.move is a Control Move carrying seal_basis; Realm schema MAY redeclare the cell family as data-plane mv_register + user-pick or per-object sequencer per authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 9.4 and models/realm-and-space.md section 3.6.

Flow reorder within Space. Writes the same cell as ck.flow.move; effect.list_space_id MUST equal head_eq.list_space_id (rank-only update). Plane ruling follows ck.flow.move: same cell family, same default sealed=true control-plane declaration (models/realm-and-space.md section 3.6).

Set or clear a per-(flow, actor) watch subscription. Writes a cas_register cell keyed by (flow_id, watcher_actor_id). Payload carries level in {mentions_only, participating, all, muted} (or null to clear, equivalent to mentions_only). Default invariant: payload.watcher_actor_id MUST equal envelope actor_id, unless writer holds ck.flow.watch.set.others. Cross-actor writes MUST carry refs[role=audit_pair] to a same-batch ck.audit.accessed event with access_kind=watch_set_others. The watches Relation (actor --watches--> flow) is a derived projection of this cell, not a separate truth source — direct ck.relation.create relation_kind=watches MUST schema_violation. See models/flow-and-message.md §8.
Space create (board / list / swimlane / calendar bucket / etc.)
Space metadata update (title, rank, kind-specific fields)

Space parent declaration. Parent is another ck:space: or null; cross-Realm parent is navigation only and never propagates Realm membership, capabilities, history, E2EE keys, retention, or federation policy.
Space archive (UI-level grouping archive; contained Flows MUST be relocated or follow archive)
Space restore (transition state archived -> active; only valid when current state == archived; tombstoned Spaces MUST NOT be restored)
Space tombstone (irreversible; contained Flows MUST be relocated before)
Message-scoped redaction; does not grant generic redaction authority
Generic redaction envelope for non-message objects/events and profile-declared content trimming

Morph schema_refs[] migration. First-class event for evolving a Morph's schema_refs[] without bypassing audit / capability gates. Carries (from_schema_refs[], to_schema_refs[], compatibility_class, migration_evidence?). Required capability ck.morph.schema_migrate (high risk tier; see capability-action-registry.json). compatibility_class = additive | breaking | transformation; core reducers MUST reject breaking/transformation unless the Realm declares ck.profile.morph.schema_migration_transformations.v1. See zh/models/morph.md §4.1 S3.

Morph business-progression stage transition. Single source of truth for mutating Morph.stage / Morph.stage_changed_at; ck.morph.update / ck.morph.schema_migrate patches on those paths MUST be rejected (forbidden-wire). The payload intentionally carries no reason / note / explanation field — rationale belongs in a Message on an associated discussion track that 'references' this event. Reducer enforces hard invariants from zh/models/common-fields.md §5.3.3: state=redacted yields failed_precondition reason=morph_already_terminal; state=archived yields morph_not_active; same-value self-transition is accepted but does NOT update stage_changed_at; reducer overwrites any wire-supplied stage_changed_at with the event's created_at.

Agent signing key authorization. Payload MUST validate as event-payload.schema.json#/$defs/agent_key_authorize_payload and bind agent_principal_id, key_id, verification_method, accountable_principal_id, agent_key_scope, audience, issued_at, expires_at, and approval_evidence.

Agent signing key revocation. Payload MUST validate as event-payload.schema.json#/$defs/agent_key_revoke_payload and bind agent_principal_id, key_id, revoked_at, and revoked_by; the revocation's control-plane basis is the Control Move envelope seal_basis, and its cutoff is the accepted Seal covering the Move.

Agent signing key rotation. Payload MUST validate as event-payload.schema.json#/$defs/agent_key_rotate_payload; key_id names the retiring key and replacement_key_id names the new key under the same accountable_principal_id with equivalent or narrower agent_key_scope.

Agent lifecycle transition to paused state (CKP-0008 §4.11). Auth Server MUST reject new agent session grants for this principal; existing tokens fail closed within the revocation freshness window. Reversible via ck.agent.resume.

Agent lifecycle transition from paused to active (CKP-0008 §4.11). Reducer MUST re-validate controller, agent, key, capability, Realm policy, and accountability_grant freshness; any failure rejects the resume.

Agent lifecycle terminal state (CKP-0008 §4.11). MUST fan-out ck.agent.key.revoke for all active agent keys, ck.capability.revoke for all active grants, and runtime endpoint revocation. Terminal — no transition out.

Agent-initiated draft proposal (CKP-0008 §4.8). Submitted by agent runtime; Principal Server materializes accepted drafts into controller-owned ck.agent.draft.v1 account-data after capability / policy / accountability / risk check. MUST NOT enter shared Realm history.
Agent-initiated action request (CKP-0008 §4.8). Carries proposed_action, target descriptor, and content digest. Awaits controller approval before generating shared event.

Controller approval of a draft / action request (CKP-0008 §4.8.1). Binds draft_id, content digest, target descriptor, proposed_action, approved payload digest, approval expiry, and single-use nonce. Publish executor MUST atomic-consume the nonce; reuse fails closed (reason=approval_already_consumed).
Controller rejection of a draft / action request (CKP-0008 §4.8.1). Draft transitions to rejected; agent runtime MUST NOT continue publish attempts.
Holder-private consent declaration: 'I consent to receive <consent_scope> from <peer>'
Revoke a previously granted consent (shares the ck.consent.grant cell; semantically a remove on the consent or_set)
Principal-scoped contact request fact. Issuer is requester; target holder must respond with accepted/rejected.
Principal-scoped contact acceptance fact. Issuer is original request target and MUST reference target-controlled consent grants.
Principal-scoped contact rejection fact. Issuer is original request target and does not write consent.
Principal-scoped contact tombstone fact. Issuer ends their own side of a contact and may revoke contact-managed consent dots.
Principal-scoped binding from unordered participant pair to canonical DM Realm and main Flow.
Realm-scoped profile override. payload.target_realm_id is the target Realm and no Space boundary is created.
Key backup active series selection for one principal and backup_class.

Push route binding for a (recipient_service_did, principal, device, push_route) tuple. Carries push_target_id, push_gateway_did, encryption_key, capabilities. Stored as actor-private state on the recipient Principal Server only; MUST NOT be replicated to Principal Servers outside the binding's recipient_service_did context.
MLS commit or Welcome processing failure diagnostic

Auditable access marker for privileged reads or privacy-sensitive paired writes. E2EE compliance release uses ck.audit.release; ck.audit.accessed remains for non-release audit pairs such as Circle metadata audit, watch_set_others, late recovery, and policy reads.

Audit Applet Binding. Declares that an audit applet/service may request staged historical release sessions for a specific Realm or Circle effective_scope. Binding is control-plane only: it does not add the applet to MLS, does not subscribe it to realtime sync, and does not grant plaintext/history keys. Bindings are non-retroactive: activation_frontier_digest / first_auditable_epoch define the earliest eligible material, and later policy changes MUST NOT expand eligibility for already encrypted messages.
Audit release session request. Must reference an active ck.audit.applet_binding and a bounded historical target range or target_refs.
Audit release session authorization by a scoped approver. Approves only the intersection of request, binding, policy, and effective_scope.
Member-visible notice for an audit release session. Circle-scoped notices are visible only to the target Circle audience and authorized moderators/admins.

Sealed audit release manifest. Records exactly which historical target_refs or sealed epochs were released, to whom, under which binding/session/notice/policy. Current active epoch release is forbidden; sealed epoch releases must reference sealed_by_commit_ref.
Close an audit release session and freeze its final release_refs.
Signed hard-erasure receipt. Attests deletion outcome and retained verification stub within an issuer-declared storage boundary; does not prove independent third-party copies disappeared.

Range-bound completeness attestation. Distinct from ck.audit.ryw_receipt (per-event read-your-writes hint) and ck.event_batch_receipt (set-bound integrity hint): this attestation asserts completeness over an explicit (from_frontier, to_frontier) + per-actor seq interval range. Issuer commits to having observed every reducer-input event in scope; witness quorum or independent seal backing is required for non-self-attested deployments. See zh/sync/operations-sync.md §4.2.
Lift a previously sealed moderation decision

Submit an appeal against an existing ck.moderation.decision. Writes the appeal cell to state=submitted. Schema: ck.schema.moderation_appeal.v1. See zh/governance/content-moderation.md §5.5 (appeal flow).
Reviewer acknowledges the appeal and transitions cell state submitted → under_review. Identifies the reviewing actor and target appeal. Schema: ck.schema.moderation_appeal.v1.

Reviewer's verdict on the appeal: uphold (decision stands) / overturn (decision reversed, emits ck.moderation.decision.lift) / modify (decision adjusted). Transitions cell state under_review → decided. Schema: ck.schema.moderation_appeal.v1.

Closes the appeal from submitted / under_review / decided via reviewer close, appellant withdrawal, or timer auto-close. Locks against re-appeal of the same target by the same appellant during the cool-off window. Schema: ck.schema.moderation_appeal.v1.

Read cursor advance event (actor-private). Writes the actor's latest read position for a given (realm_id, read_scope) tuple. Was historically named ck.read.cursor; renamed to align the event_kind, capability action, schema id and typed ID prefix on a single noun root read_cursor.

Invite create. Directed v1 invite payloads carry invitee plus invite_delivery_target and introduction_evidence_digest; raw locator tokens and invite_receive_policy state are private and MUST NOT enter the durable Realm event.

payload_schema_contract.non_critical_extension_rule: Unknown non-critical payload fields are preserved in canonical bytes and MAY be ignored by reducers. Unknown critical payload semantics MUST be declared in Event.requirements.critical_extensions and fail closed when unsupported.
payload_schema_contract.validation_rule: Every active standard ck.* event kind MUST be validated by the Event Envelope schema and one payload class selected by kind. Unknown standard kind, unmatched active kind, or payload class failure is schema_violation before reducer execution.

registry_rules: Standard ck.* effect kinds MUST appear in this registry when used by a DataEvent effect, Control Move effect, or Event Envelope payload router.

Events API, Sync durable history, Federation, and canonical reducers MUST accept only active entries with wire_scope=durable_event unless an implementation profile explicitly defines a private channel for actor_private_event.
Entries with wire_scope=ephemeral_event MUST be carried only on ephemeral channels and MUST NOT advance Seal coverage, governance state_root, or reducer state.

Entries with wire_scope=actor_private_event MAY be persisted in encrypted account data or an actor-private stream, but MUST NOT be inserted into shared Realm data-plane history or control-plane Seal history.

Reducer-input durable kinds MAY declare cell_family, cell_subject, lattice, bottom, and (cas_register only) initial_value. cell_family is a stable ck.component.*.v<n> URI; cell_subject is null, a payload field path, or a composite descriptor; bottom is reject or expose. initial_value declares the value the cas_register reports before any DataEvent or Control Move effect has been applied; declaring `initial_value="__unset__"` combined with `head_eq:"__unset__"` Control Move predicates implements singleton-once-set cells.

Registered exemption: protocol-singleton cells that are not written through a single event_kind are NOT indexed here. Currently the only such cell family is ck.component.notary.v1 (per-Realm notary cell, lattice=cas_register, bottom=reject): its genesis value comes from the ck.realm.create payload notary object and subsequent changes are ordinary notary-finalized Control Moves; its canonical definition lives in zh/authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 4.4. Any future cell family without a single writer kind MUST be added to this exemption list explicitly.

Lattice MUST be one of: core types or_set, mv_register, cas_register, fsm, counter, ordered_log; or extension types lww_register, rga (only declarable on cells with cell_role in {ui_affordance, content, draft, cosmetic} and only valid for receivers that implement ck.profile.collaborative_text.v1; receivers without that profile MUST fail closed with unsupported_lattice_type when an event_kind references a cell using lww_register or rga). Authorization, policy, notary, membership, and lifecycle cells MUST NOT use lww_register or rga.

State convergence is defined by CBA: DataEvent effects are locally accepted against seal_ref, Control Move effects are finalized by Seals, and per-cell Lattice join remains deterministic. Event Envelope routing fields MUST NOT be used as ordering authority.

Every active durable reducer-input event_kind MUST have a machine-readable admission source: either at least one capability action targets it (capability_action_registry.target_event_kinds), or it declares an admission class from admission_class_definitions. capability_gated events MUST list the authorizing action(s) in admission_capabilities. Enforced by lint_artifacts.py; no active durable reducer-input event may lack an admission source (fail-closed).

wire_scope_definitions.actor_private_event: Persisted actor-private/account-data event; not shared Realm history and not Realm reducer input.
wire_scope_definitions.durable_event: Valid Event Envelope kind for persisted canonical history and reducer input.
wire_scope_definitions.ephemeral_event: Transient sync/federation/app signal; MUST NOT be persisted as durable Event Envelope history.

generated_registries.description: Generated registry view for standard ck.* Event.kind values and wire scopes.
generated_registries.name: event_kinds

generated_registries.description: Generated registry view for active schema IDs and schema file locations.
generated_registries.name: schemas

generated_registries.description: Generated registry view for ck:<kind>: typed ID prefixes and storage/wire rules.
generated_registries.name: id_kinds

generated_registries.description: Generated registry view for service operation IDs across HTTP, gRPC, and MQ surfaces.
generated_registries.name: operations

generated_registries.description: Generated registry view for canonical capability action vocabulary, risk tiers, required constraints, and event_kind targets.
generated_registries.name: capability_actions

id_kinds.description: Moderation appeal ID — opaque key for the ck.component.moderation_appeal.v1 cell. Created by ck.moderation.appeal.submit; referenced by review / decision / close events. See zh/governance/content-moderation.md §5.5.

Agent interop session ID. Note the cross-surface naming: this typed ID uses the short form `agent_interop_session`, while the corresponding event kinds use the full form `ck.agent.interop_session.{start,status,result}` and capability actions use `ck.agent.interop_session.{start,cancel,stream_status,attach_artifact,read_transcript}`. The three surfaces all refer to the same session concept; downstream tooling MUST NOT assume `ck:<event-prefix>:<uuid>` mechanical derivation.
Directory-local announce ingest record ID. It is typed and UUIDv7-shaped for validator consistency, but it is scoped to the issuing Directory and is not a global federated object authority.
Audit Applet Binding ID. Created by ck.audit.applet_binding and referenced by audit session request/authorize/notice/release events.
Audit release session ID. Threads ck.audit.session.request, authorize, notice, release, and close events for one bounded historical audit window.
Audit release manifest ID. Created by ck.audit.release for a sealed historical release under an active audit binding/session.

Stable identifier for one chain of encrypted backup envelopes belonging to a single (actor_id, backup_class). A pair MAY have multiple series during rotation or migration; the active series is selected by the signed active-series record, not by server return order. Used by ck.schema.key_backup.v1.series_id and recovery flows to detect rollback. See identity/key-management.md §7.6.
Blob metadata row ID; content-addressed blobs use the special digest form

SFU-local participant handle (CKP-0010). Scope limited to `(call_id, focus_id, sfu_did)`; derived from `(realm_id, call_id, focus_id, device_id, issuer_service_did, issued_at_bucket)` by the media service token issuer. MUST NOT carry any actor-identifying material; only appears in `ck.call.state.participants[].participant_identity` and in `participant_binding`. The wire value MUST use the canonical UUIDv7-shaped `ck:rtc_participant:<uuid>` form; implementations MAY derive the random bits from the media-service token input, but the version and variant nibbles MUST satisfy the UUIDv7 pattern.
Abstract capability definition reference ID; signed grant objects use ck:grant:<uuid>.

Circle object ID — intra-Realm scoped event/message boundary. Hosts its own membership (strict subset of parent Realm.members), history visibility, delivery/query/projection boundary, and optional independent MLS group. Does NOT carry federation identity, policy server, or capability registry — those remain on the parent Realm. See zh/models/circle.md.

Device identifier (ck:device:<uuid>). A device is a typed ID scoped to an owning principal, NOT a DID and NOT an actor principal. Device keys are registered as verification methods under the owning principal DID via ck.device.authorize.
Signed capability grant object ID used by ck.schema.capability.v1 and grant/revoke references.

Stable session identifier bound by every proof transcript, backup decrypt proof and MLS Welcome replay during one recovery flow. Referenced by ck.schema.recovery_receipt.v1 and by §15 recovery proofs. See crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §15.

Space object ID — structural grouping object inside a Realm (board, list, swimlane, calendar bucket, etc.). Authorization-transparent: never carries its own membership / policy / E2EE group; resolves to the containing Realm.
Realm object ID — security / sync / auth / E2EE boundary. Always carries membership, policy, history_visibility, MLS group binding, and federation policy.

special_forms.description: Opaque sync/query cursor; not a typed-UUIDv7 object ID.
special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store as an opaque token or store server-private cursor state keyed by a raw token.

special_forms.description: Content-addressed blob reference; distinct from ck:blob:<uuid> blob metadata IDs.
special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store digest bytes/hex separately from any logical blob row ID.

special_forms.description: MLS-profile scoped reference such as KeyPackage IDs; validated by the E2EE profile, not by the generic typed-UUIDv7.
special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store profile and raw profile_id separately.

special_forms.description: Realm-scoped pseudonymous credential reference; validated by the E2EE profile. v1 core uses Realm as the boundary; Matrix-style Room terminology is only allowed in MIMI/Matrix interop modules.
special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store scope and random identifier separately when used in credential tables.
Store as a content-addressed canonical Seal hash.
Store canonical tuple fields separately when indexing cell state.

special_forms.description: Deployment-scope trust domain identifier. Scope is a lowercase opaque label (alphanumerics, dot, dash, underscore, colon; max 128 chars). Used to prevent cross-deployment / cross-sovereign replay of high-risk proofs (e.g. ck.cross_signing.reset §14.1). NOT a typed-UUIDv7 object id. See identity-did.md §3.6.
special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store the scope string as an opaque deployment-level identifier; it appears in server describe, Realm policy, and high-risk proof transcripts.

storage_rules: Protocol wire objects, canonical JSON, signatures, hashes, fixtures, logs, API DTOs, and cross-service references MUST use the full typed form ck:<kind>:<uuid> unless a special form below applies.

Storage implementations MAY store raw 16-byte UUID values (e.g. PostgreSQL `uuid` column) without the ck:<kind>: prefix when the table, column, or explicit kind field already supplies the type context.
Implementations that store raw IDs MUST restore the full typed form before computing canonical JSON, event IDs, payload hashes, detached proofs, federation payloads, sync cursors, or audit logs.
The <kind> segment is part of the signed/canonical wire value. It MUST NOT be changed, inferred differently, or stripped during verification, forwarding, backfill, or replay.

The UUID segment MUST be RFC 9562 UUID version 7 (48-bit Unix-millisecond timestamp + 4-bit version=7 + 12-bit rand_a + 2-bit variant=10b + 62-bit rand_b), serialized as the canonical 36-character lowercase hex form `xxxxxxxx-xxxx-7xxx-Nxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx` where N ∈ {8,9,a,b}.

capability_tiers.core: Base interoperable surfaces implied by claiming Cokret v1 protocol support (service discovery, identity registry, events/account aggregate).
capability_tiers.deployment_local: Deployment-specific, operator, or product-local surfaces that MUST NOT be assumed from core protocol support alone.
capability_tiers.extension: Optional interoperable surfaces that are part of the Cokret specification but require explicit discovery/profile advertisement.
capability_tiers.interop_bridge: Adapter surfaces that bridge Cokret to external protocols (MIMI Internet-Drafts, third-party Applet hosts). Implementations advertise these only when the external protocol is supported; bridge operations are not part of any core or extension profile and frequently mirror an in-spec operation via bridges_to.

operation_registry.description: Canonical operation catalog for generated service operation views and transport bindings.

generated_views.role: HTTP/OpenAPI binding shape aligned to the catalog; not a second operation namespace.
Descriptive operation map and governance notes; excerpt-only unless explicitly marked generated.

operations.notes: Issues a short-TTL, single-blob, read-only pre-signed URL whose authorization material rides in the URL itself (query string). Used as a deliberate carve-out of the no-credentials-in-URL rule (server-threat-model.md S21) so that browser primitives like /

Explicit, cumulative, monotonic to-device delivery acknowledgement (client-sync.md §10.1). Queue deletion happens only here; stream cursor advancement (account subscribe after=, device_messages from=) is read-only and MUST NOT prune the queue. Re-acking the same or an older token is a legal no-op. Unknown / expired / cross-bound tokens are rejected with invalid_param (reason invalid_ack_token) without deleting anything.
Writes requester-side ck.contact.requested fact and requester-side consent grants for requested scopes; MUST NOT write target consent or accepted fact.
Target-side accept/reject of a contact request. Accept writes target-controlled consent grants; reject writes no consent.
Holder contact projection from contact facts plus consent-derived directional scopes; account-data contact notes are local decoration only.
Holder-side contact tombstone. Default revocation is limited to contact-managed active consent dots.

Read the authenticated subject's private invite-receive policy. Returns the recommended default when no explicit override is stored; the response is never written into the target Realm durable event log.

Replace the authenticated subject's private invite-receive policy. The body MUST set subject_id equal to the session actor; the override shares the same store as ck.self.contact.tombstone(block_peer) blocked_subjects writes.
Idempotent resolver for accepted contacts. Requires accepted contact projection and direct_message consent; create=true creates canonical DM Realm, main Flow, and binding.

HTTP-specific POST/body form of ck.events.query. Semantically identical (same selector / cursor / order / filter / include_completeness parameter set, same response shape including optional range_completeness). Choose when URL length would exceed practical limits (large realms[]/actors[] arrays, complex filters object) or when query parameters would be logged inadvertently by proxies. Non-HTTP transports MUST use the canonical ck.self.events.query binding (SelfEvents/Query / self.events.query), not expose this variant as a separate gRPC or MQ operation.
Dereference a known set of event_id / event_digest references to full EventEnvelope objects. Point lookup by identifier, not a range scan — use ck.self.events.query for selector-based reads.

Long-lived per-Realm / actor event stream with optional bounded catch-up replay. `dropped` and `resync_required` control frames MAY carry `reconnect_after_ms`, a server-directed minimum delay before opening another subscription for the same caller/selector scope; early reconnects are rejected with rate_limited / Retry-After.
Federation peer Events surface describe. This endpoint describes the server-to-server peer event bindings; it is not a client self/events binding.

Federation peer frontier probe. Requires service-to-service authentication, Source/Destination service DID headers, trust-domain headers, and Realm federation_peer authorization. It returns the federation peer frontier response shape on the dedicated peer trust surface.

Federation peer pull/backfill query. Uses the same selector, cursor, order, and response semantics as ck.self.events.query, but the HTTP trust surface is peer and the caller MUST be an authorized federation peer service.
HTTP-specific POST/body form of ck.peer.events.query. Semantically identical to GET /_cokret/peer/events; use it when federation selectors or filters are too large or sensitive for query strings.

Federation peer event reference resolution for missing prev_refs / causal references. Requires authorized federation peer service authentication and applies the same reference-disclosure and history-visibility rules as peer event query.
Federation peer event push. Body is EventsSubmitFederationRequestBody and the caller MUST use service-to-service authentication with Source/Destination service DID and trust-domain headers.

Private Principal Server to Principal Server invite delivery. Requires service-to-service authentication, Destination-Service-DID equal to invite_address.recipient_service_did, a ck.invite.create event whose invitee equals invite_address.subject_id, and introduction_evidence accepted by the recipient invite_receive_policy.

Private Principal Server to Principal Server contact fact delivery. Requires service-to-service authentication, Destination-Service-DID equal to contact_address.recipient_service_did, and a signed ck.contact.* envelope the recipient projects into the target holder's contact projection without re-signing.
Federation peer snapshot manifest head for snapshot-assisted bootstrap. Requires service-to-service authentication and Realm federation_peer authorization.

Canonical broadcast ephemeral send operation for ck.schema.ephemeral_envelope.v1. Carries ck.presence, ck.typing, ck.receipt.read, and ck.call.signal; MUST NOT persist the signal as a durable Event or advance actor_seq / Realm frontier.

Media service token exchange operation (CKP-0010). Issues a short-lived (TTL <= 600s) backend_token + participant_binding for joining a focus declared in ck.realm.media_service.foci[]. Same wire across all backend types (livekit / mediasoup / janus / cokret-native); only backend_token shape is type-specific. Token issuer DID MUST be one of the Realm-authorized media service DIDs; clients reject otherwise (token_issuer_unauthorised). See zh/crypto-media/media-service-binding.md §3.

Read the currently accepted ck.schema.recovery_policy.v1 projection for the authenticated or explicitly selected principal. Returns active_policy=null when no accepted policy exists; does not publish, rotate, or revoke policy state.

Resolves an online invite locator token carried out-of-band, usually as a URL fragment in a QR/link. The locator token MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; the response is a signed principal_locator.
Canonical HTTP binding is POST /_cokret/self/policy/check. Paths carry no version segment; protocol version is negotiated via *.describe / supported_operations (see sync/api-conventions.md).
Extension read surface for reducer-maintained Flow lifecycle projection rows scoped by realm_id. This is a derived read model, not a canonical truth source.
Extension read surface for reducer-maintained Morph lifecycle projection rows scoped by realm_id. This is a derived read model, not a canonical truth source.
Extension read surface for reducer-maintained Space lifecycle projection rows scoped by realm_id. This is a derived read model, not a canonical truth source.

Optional extension read surface that materializes a View{kind=collection} projection such as board/list/table/calendar. The response is a derived read model computed from signed Events, reducer profile, View definition, and the returned frontier; it is not a canonical truth source.

Optional extension read surface for a single document Morph projection. It returns authorized document body, version, relation, comment, and cursor-presence read-model data for the addressed Morph; canonical truth remains the Morph/Relation/Message event history.

Holder-bound one-shot read of the current principal account projection. Returns principal_id, account lifecycle state, device summaries, optional ActorProfile, and signed handle-claim evidence or refs. It MUST NOT return an unsigned bare handle as authoritative identity. Naming: the trailing segment 'viewer' is intentionally outside the api-conventions.md §2.4 read-verb taxonomy; it follows the GraphQL 'viewer' convention (the authenticated subject's own projection). The target is located by the holder-bound session rather than an external id, so 'get' does not apply, and 'viewer' (subject identity projection) stays distinct from 'describe' (service capability metadata).

Holder-bound service wrapper around ck.profile.update / Actor Profile projection. Request body is a closed patch over display_name, avatar_blob_ref, and profile_fields.<key>; bio migrates to profile_fields.bio and avatar_url is not accepted on the Cokret protocol path.

Streaming push of cross-Realm account-aggregate deltas (cross-Realm frontier, to_device queue, account_data, device_lists, presence, unread / notification counts). Connection is long-lived; server pushes NDJSON frames as new data becomes available. Symmetric with ck.self.events.subscribe — both are streaming subscriptions, differing only in scope (self.events.subscribe = per-Realm event log; self.account.subscribe = account-aggregate). `dropped` and `resync_required` control frames MAY carry `reconnect_after_ms`, a server-directed minimum delay before opening another subscription for the same principal/device/filter scope; early reconnects are rejected with rate_limited / Retry-After. Replaces the prior Matrix-derived long-poll ck.account.sync; not wire-compatible with Matrix /sync.

High-assurance optional endpoint to revoke a previously issued cursor authority. Revocation hits return cursor_revoked and MUST NOT advance account subscribe position, barrier wait, or dropped recovery state. To-device queue deletion is decoupled from cursors entirely and happens only via ck.self.device_messages.ack.

registry_rules: New operation_id values MUST be added here before any OpenAPI, HTTP binding table, SDK generator, or alternative transport binding references them.
Generated views MAY change shape, grouping, or field order, but MUST NOT introduce, rename, or remove operation_id values that are absent from this catalog.
Supporting Cokret core does not imply support for every registered operation. Implementations MUST advertise supported_operations and supported_profiles explicitly.

Each surface_groups entry carries a tier (see capability_tiers); only the core tier is implied by claiming v1 protocol support. Extension, interop_bridge, and deployment_local surfaces require explicit advertisement.

Profile matrices in artifacts/profiles/conformance-profiles.json define role-level MUST/SHOULD requirements; the surface groups below define machine-readable capability families for discovery, docs, and lint.
Each operation MUST declare success_shape_kind so SDKs can determine success handling without endpoint-name hard-coding.

Operations with typed OpenAPI bodies SHOULD declare request_schema_ref and/or response_schema_ref. The referenced schema fragment is the source for generated DTO docs and MUST match the OpenAPI component referenced by the HTTP binding.

Operations that still bind OpenAPI request/response bodies to OperationRequest or OperationResult MUST declare generic_binding with request/response booleans, reason, profile_gate, and migration_plan; core-tier operations MUST NOT use generic bindings.

v1 preserves existing operation_id spellings even when an HTTP path segment uses plural nouns for collection resources. In particular, the contact lifecycle surface uses ck.self.contact.* operation_id values with /contacts/* HTTP paths; v2 may normalize naming, but v1 implementations and SDKs MUST NOT rename these operation_id values.

success_shape_kind_definitions.event_stream: Long-lived event stream rather than a single JSON success body.
success_shape_kind_definitions.inline_response: Endpoint-specific inline object schema in OpenAPI.
success_shape_kind_definitions.metadata_headers: Metadata-only success expressed through HTTP headers.
success_shape_kind_definitions.operation_result: Generic OperationResult envelope; operation row MUST carry generic_binding.
success_shape_kind_definitions.schema_resource: Response body is a canonical artifact JSON Schema resource.
success_shape_kind_definitions.service_describe: ServiceDescribe object returned by a describe endpoint.

Circle — intra-Realm scoped event/message boundary. Subset membership, independent history visibility, delivery/query/projection boundary, and optional independent MLS group. Does NOT carry federation identity or policy server. Introduced by CKP-0007; see zh/models/circle.md.
Encrypted account-data value shapes for reminders, scheduled send, snooze, and saved items.
Encrypted account-data plaintext shape for cross-device draft sync.
Encrypted account-data plaintext shape and to-device key message content for principal-private cross-device file transfer.
Profile fields for calendar-event Flows.
Payload schema for ck.rsvp.set.
Message expiry and Realm disappearing-message policy shape.
Payload schemas for shared pin events.
Privacy-preserving search index manifest, blind index query, and policy shapes.
Reference business-field schema used by the Morph type-system example. It validates the customer_risk fields.status / fields.severity payload carried inside ck.schema.morph.v1 containers.
Signed online invite locator asserting subject_id and recipient_service_did for private invite delivery.
Private service-to-service invite delivery request carrying invite_address and introduction_evidence.
Subject-private invite receive policy controlling which introduction evidence kinds may notify the holder.
Private service-to-service contact fact delivery request carrying a signed ck.contact.* envelope and contact_address for cross-Principal-Server projection.
Closed response DTO bundle for authorization query operations.
Signed holder commitment that Event bytes are available until retention_until; used by CBA Seal availability_root.
Registered schema for the embedded ck.patch.v1 field-patch wire format.
Closed request DTO bundle for realtime media service operations.
Closed request/response DTO bundle for account self-service operations: viewer, register, profile update, and session revocation.
Closed request/response DTO bundle for contact lifecycle operations and direct conversation resolver.
Closed request/response DTO bundle for Blob service operations.
Signed principal-control record selecting the active backup series for one (actor_id, backup_class).
Canonical plaintext keybag opened from a ck.schema.key_backup.v1 envelope.
Proof binding a key-backup read/decrypt action to one recovery session, requesting device, backup object, selected series, ciphertext digest, and accepted proof transcript.

Wire payload schema for the principal recovery policy. Bound to the Principal Control Realm via signed publish / rotate / share-revoke; receivers MUST reject recovery / rotate / ck.device.authorize and cross-signing-reset evidence whose proof family is not allowed by the currently accepted recovery policy. See identity/key-management.md §3.3 / §7 / §8.

Wire contract for the device recovery session state machine, including create/get session shape, proof submit/complete request and response helpers, and principal_signing recovery proof transcript. See crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §15.

Signed completion receipt for a principal recovery flow. Bound to recovery_session_id used by every proof, backup unlock, and MLS Welcome replay during the recovery. See crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §15 step 7.
Closed request/response DTO bundle for push device registration and push wakeup delivery.
Closed request/response DTO bundle for Directory discovery search, resolve, private contact discovery, handle lookup, agent selector lookup, and push webhook registration operations.
Signed DID continuity / migration proof payload
Encrypted minimal-metadata binding from Realm-scoped pairwise DID to principal DID, scoped by realm_id and trust_domain.
Realm-scoped member display/subject projection carried by ck.member.identity.update; handle lifecycle is carried by ck.schema.handle_claim.v1.
Directory response listing currently visible handle claims for a disclosed subject DID.
Builder-side candidate object for Handle resolution intent=member_add | invite (identity-handles.md §3.7); produces a Realm-scoped member_delivery_binding only after Join Policy re-validation.

Time-bounded routing hint returned by Realm discovery / resolve paths for selecting a qualified service to receive join, invite-accept, knock, or restricted-join submissions. Not an authorization grant and not a member_delivery_binding.
Closed request/response DTO bundle for MIMI provider interop operations.
Schema-registry object for applet protocol metadata snapshots. Event payloads for ck.applet.* use typed payload definitions in event-payload.schema.json.

Controller-signed package used by ck.self.applet.install preview/commit to derive ck.applet.registration and capability grants. Distribution object only; not Realm history truth and not authorization.

Closed request/response DTO bundle for ck.self.applet.ghost.provision (Applet-managed Ghost Actor provisioning by an installed bridge Applet).
Schema-registry object for agent protocol metadata snapshots. Event payloads for ck.agent.* use typed payload definitions in event-payload.schema.json.

Minimal retained verification stub bound by erasure-receipt.retained_stub_digest
