A MIMI room policy component does not match the Cokret Realm policy_root or ck.realm.policy_components state. Facade MUST reject the update until a fresh policy projection is available. See zh/extensions/mimi-interop.md §4.1.

Incoming MIMI room state uses lifecycle, membership, policy, or extension shape not supported by the declared Cokret MIMI interop profile. Facade MUST reject or require a newer profile. See zh/extensions/mimi-interop.md §4.1.

Required MIMI provider directory, key material, or groupInfo dependency is temporarily unreachable. Facade MAY retry with bounded backoff but MUST NOT accept fallback state without governance binding. See zh/extensions/mimi-interop.md §4.1.
Counterparty declared a MIMI Internet-Draft version not supported by this interop profile. Facade MUST reject instead of guessing a nearby draft shape. See zh/extensions/mimi-interop.md §4.1.

A ck.mimi.room_binding Control Move declared a payload.status value that is not a legal transition from the binding's current status (including an illegal initial status or any write after the terminal revoked state). Reducer MUST reject; the room binding status lifecycle is defined in zh/extensions/mimi-interop.md §4.2.
Invite token's expires_at has passed when claim is attempted. Internal-only reason code; the wire response MUST be the unified non-enumerable `not_found` per zh/sync/third-party-invites.md §6.1.

A late-arriving key tried to upgrade a decryption_failed event to late_recovered, but the receiver was not a member of the Realm at the original causal time T₀ (or has since been banned/removed). Client MUST NOT admit the recovered plaintext to verified timeline; audit log records this code. See zh/crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md §2.3.5.

A key backup / archive node / peer share refused to deliver late key material because, on re-running the T₀ membership + policy check before sending, the current share policy no longer permits delivery to the requesting device (distinct from late_recovery_rejected_membership, which is the receiver-side T₀ non-membership case). See zh/crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md §2.3.5.

A late-arriving key tried to recover plaintext for an event whose disappearing expiry plus grace has elapsed, or whose retention policy requires content-key destruction. Client MUST keep the expiry stub / metadata-only state. See zh/crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md §2.3.5 and zh/crypto-media/disappearing-messages.md §4.

Invite delivery to the private target failed after the delivery service exhausted the retry budget. Used as a stable invite transition reason for ck.invite state projections; see zh/models/governance-objects.md and zh/sync/third-party-invites.md §6.1.

Event Envelope prev_refs exceeds the v1 maximum of 128 entries, or duplicates entries where uniqueness is required. Receiver MUST reject with schema_violation. See zh/conformance/scalability-constraints.md.
Event Envelope refs[] exceeds the v1 maximum of 128 semantic refs. Receiver MUST reject with schema_violation. See zh/conformance/scalability-constraints.md.

A non-bootstrap ck.device.authorize event was submitted outside the principal's bound principal_control Realm, or the Realm purpose/profile/created_by does not match the device owner and issuer principal. Reducer MUST fail closed. See zh/identity/key-management.md §5.0.3.

A Move attempted to read or write a bottom=reject cell while the effective value is ⊥. Ordinary CAS writes MUST fail; recovery requires the conflict-recovery witness path. See zh/authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md §5.1 and §8.

Cross-method principal upgrade transfer_evidence.old_did_document_fetched_at is older than the maximum 168h evidence window. Receiver MUST reject instead of accepting stale did:web evidence. See zh/identity/key-management.md §5.0.5.

An agent protocol session status/result no longer matches the DID Document hash, service entry, endpoint digest, or verification method pinned at session start. Session MUST be blocked or cancelled. See zh/extensions/agent-protocol-interop.md §5.2.

A pinned agent endpoint digest was marked retired or revoked by the owner/admin endpoint state. Existing sessions MUST be blocked/cancelled and new sessions MUST re-start with a fresh pin. See zh/extensions/agent-protocol-interop.md §5.2.

An external agent protocol response failed declared schema, transcript hash, or artifact binding validation. The failure MUST be recorded via ck.agent.interop_session.status/result. See zh/extensions/agent-protocol-interop.md §12.

External applicant-facing generic join gate failure. Wire response MUST NOT reveal whether a claim was absent, revoked, issuer-unreachable, parent-membership-missing, or challenge-invalid; detailed diagnostics are audit/reviewer-only. See zh/governance/join-policy.md §5.

The effective target Realm is tombstoned, destroyed, unreachable, or not writable by the actor; default Realm resolution MUST fail closed instead of following Realm links or falling back implicitly. See zh/models/space-hierarchy.md §4.

Sub-reason for a schema_violation on ck.realm.join_policy where gates[] contains duplicate gate_id values. gate_id MUST be stable and unique within the policy so that audit refs in ck.member.state{gate_proofs[gate_id=…]} are unambiguous. Wire response uses code=schema_violation with reason_code=join_policy_duplicate_gate_id. See zh/governance/join-policy.md §3.1.
Sub-reason for schema_violation when an object's scope_circle_id references a Circle whose realm_id does not match the object's realm_id. See zh/models/circle.md §6.1.
Sub-reason for failed_precondition when scope_circle_id points at a Circle whose state is archived or tombstoned. See zh/models/circle.md §6.1.
Sub-reason for failed_precondition when ck.circle.restore targets a Circle whose current lifecycle state is not archived. See zh/models/common-fields.md §5.1 and zh/models/circle.md §9.
Sub-reason for failed_precondition when a Circle lifecycle write targets a Circle that is already tombstoned or otherwise terminal. See zh/models/common-fields.md §5.1 and zh/models/circle.md §9.

Sub-reason for failed_precondition when an object write references an effective scope whose Circle or parent Realm has been tombstoned/destroyed and cannot accept new writes. Projections may surface the same string as a non-error status marker. See zh/models/realm-and-space.md §2.6.1 and zh/models/circle.md §9.2.

Sub-reason for failed_precondition on ck.circle.member.state -> join when target actor is not yet a `join` member of the parent Realm. Circle.members ⊆ Realm.members is a hard invariant. See zh/models/circle.md §9.1.

Sub-reason for failed_precondition when ck.circle.create / ck.circle.update would set a Circle encryption setting below the parent Realm floor: either Circle.encryption_profile below the parent Realm encryption_profile / effective content_encryption_floor (E2EE Realm / e2ee_required floor requires an MLS-backed Circle), or Circle.content_encryption_floor below the effective floor max(parent Realm content_encryption_floor, Circle), or a Circle with encryption_profile=none declaring content_encryption_floor=e2ee_required (no MLS-backed effective_scope to carry ciphertext). See zh/models/circle.md §7.

Sub-reason for failed_precondition when a Realm declares content_encryption_floor=e2ee_required but a Flow / Message / Morph / Blob content write would land in a non-MLS-backed effective_scope (plaintext). The content effective_scope MUST be Realm-default MLS or Circle MLS. See zh/models/circle.md §7 (Realm.content_encryption_floor).

Sub-reason for failed_precondition when a ck.realm.policy_components or ck.circle.update would lower a scope's effective content_encryption_floor from e2ee_required back to allow_plaintext. The effective content encryption floor is a one-way ratchet (monotonically non-decreasing); tightening is allowed, lowering is rejected. See zh/models/realm-and-space.md §2.5 and zh/models/circle.md §7.

Sub-reason for failed_precondition when a ck.realm.policy_components or ck.circle.update would lower a scope's effective metadata encryption floor to a lower level (comparison order allow_plaintext < e2ee_required). The effective metadata encryption floor is a one-way ratchet (monotonically non-decreasing). See zh/models/realm-and-space.md §2.5 and zh/models/circle.md §7.

Sub-reason for failed_precondition when scope_circle_id rebind is attempted without an explicitly profile-permitted audited-high-risk path. Default reducer rejects rebinds to prevent silent historical-discussion migration. See zh/models/circle.md §6.1.

Sub-reason for failed_precondition when a Realm/Circle/Flow agent_participation ceiling write would widen (enable a bit disabled by) its parent ceiling. The deployment ⊇ Realm ⊇ Circle ⊇ Flow ceiling chain is tighten-only (monotone). See zh/models/realm-and-space.md, zh/models/circle.md, zh/authz/capabilities.md §5.4.

Sub-reason for failed_precondition when a controller's ck.self.agent.participation.set selection enables a bit the effective ceiling disables. Effective participation = effective_ceiling ∩ selection. See zh/authz/capabilities.md §5.4.

A native personal agent attempted to author ck.message.create / ck.reaction.add in a scope where its effective participation reply bit is false (no reply-enabled selection ∩ ceiling covering the scope). See zh/authz/capabilities.md §5.4 and zh/models/private-objects.md §4.1.

Sub-reason for schema_violation when actor-side submit payload illegally carries a top-level `effective_scope` field. `effective_scope` is the canonical reducer-output form (tagged {kind:realm|circle}); actors only supply `scope_circle_id` (id:circle | null). Reducer stamps the immutable tagged form on the Event envelope and materialized object cell. See zh/models/circle.md §6.2.

Sub-reason for schema_violation when actor-side submit payload carries `actor_kind`. The reducer derives actor_kind immutably from actor_id's Actor Profile after acceptance; submitters MUST NOT supply it. See zh/models/event-and-patch.md §2.1.

Sub-reason for failed_precondition when a write would expose metadata below the effective metadata_encryption_floor floor (max of parent Realm floor, Circle metadata_encryption_floor, Space child_scope_policy.metadata_encryption_floor, object profile requirement). See zh/models/circle.md §7.

ck.schema.key_backup.v1 envelope chain failed verification: a `supersedes_digest` does not match the canonical_json digest of its predecessor, or a non-genesis envelope is missing a predecessor accessible to the caller. See zh/identity/key-management.md §7.6 and zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §12 / §12.1.

A PUT /_cokret/self/keys/backups/{backup_id} request whose `series_seq` is not strictly greater than the current maximum sequence within the same (actor_id, series_id), or whose genesis envelope sets series_seq != 0. See zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §12.1.

`ck.schema.key_backup.v1.supersedes` references a backup_id that is unknown to the server, deleted, or owned by a different actor / series. Wire endpoint returns 409 Conflict; receivers MUST treat the chain as broken. See zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §12.1.

A key-backup envelope or recovery proof references a `recovery_policy.policy_id` / `policy_version` that is not the currently accepted policy for the principal. Recovery flows MUST surface this to the user as 'update recovery policy' rather than silently continuing. See zh/identity/key-management.md §7.5.4 / §7.7 and zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §15.

A recovery proof echoes a challenge value that does not exactly match the server-issued challenge for the referenced recovery_session_id. Servers MUST reject the proof before completing device recovery. See zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §15 and artifacts/schemas/recovery-session.schema.json.

A recovery-session operation (submit_proof / complete) targeted a recovery session that is already in a terminal state (`completed` / `rejected` / `expired`). Terminal recovery sessions are immutable; servers MUST reject with top-level `failed_precondition` carrying this reason_code. See zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §15 and artifacts/schemas/recovery-session.schema.json.

Recovery-session `rejection_reason_code` value: proof verification failures reached the server-side policy limit, so the session transitioned to `rejected`. Closed value set defined in artifacts/schemas/recovery-session.schema.json and zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §15.

Recovery-session `rejection_reason_code` value: an operator / admin surface explicitly rejected the session. Closed value set defined in artifacts/schemas/recovery-session.schema.json and zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §15.

Recovery-session `rejection_reason_code` value: a server-side risk policy rejected the session. Closed value set defined in artifacts/schemas/recovery-session.schema.json and zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §15.

Recovery-session `rejection_reason_code` value: the session was superseded by a newer recovery session for the same principal / device. Closed value set defined in artifacts/schemas/recovery-session.schema.json and zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §15.

A counter-lattice inc / dec op would move the cell's cumulative value past `parameters.max` (or below `parameters.min`) declared in the cell schema. The op MUST be rejected at validate_op / verify_move time with top-level `failed_precondition` carrying this reason_code; it never enters the join. See zh/authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md §5.3.5.

A ck.member.state Move requests a membership FSM transition that is not listed as legal for the member's current state. Reducers MUST reject the Move with failed_precondition. See zh/models/realm-and-space.md §2.7.

A threshold-recovery share submitted during reconstruction does not match the `share_commitment{algorithm, commitment_b64u}` declared in the active recovery policy. Coordinator MUST notify the user which holder submitted an invalid share. See zh/identity/key-management.md §7.5.4 / §8.

`ck.schema.key_backup.v1.frontier_ref.frontier_digest` does not match the current principal control stream frontier, or `ssk_generation` is below the current accepted generation. Receivers MUST refuse to use the envelope as the primary recovery source. See zh/identity/key-management.md §7.6.

A `secret_storage` backup envelope references a `self_signing_key` / `user_signing_key` whose generation was retired by a cross-signing reset, and the publish-recovery window elapsed without a successor envelope. Receivers MUST refuse it as the primary recovery source. See zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §14.2 step 7.

A key-backup envelope's auth_data verification method is bound to a self-signing generation older than the current accepted generation and outside the rotation grace window. Receivers MUST reject the envelope for recovery or read paths. See zh/identity/key-management.md §7.4.1.

A key-backup envelope signature verifies cryptographically but the signer device key cannot be linked to the current actor cross-signing trust root, or the signer is revoked, unauthorized, or generation-mismatched. Receivers MUST reject it even if the series chain and ciphertext_digest are self-consistent. See zh/identity/key-management.md §7.4.1.

Device / Key Server received a `ck.keys.backups.*` request body that does not validate as `ck.schema.key_backup.v1`. Wire backups MUST carry the dedicated key-backup envelope with `series_id` and `series_seq`; client-local secret-storage envelopes are not accepted on wire endpoints. See zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §11.

A proof transcript for recovery, cross-signing reset, device authorization, or recovery-policy rotation is not bound to `(policy_id, version, recovery_session_id)`. Receivers MUST reject. See zh/identity/key-management.md §8.1.

Receiver does not recognise `encryption.aead.aead_profile` (or sees a reserved-but-unpublished profile such as `ck.aead.hybrid_kem.*`). Receivers MUST fail closed; inferring parameters from `aead.name` alone is forbidden. See zh/identity/key-management.md §7.9.

A `recipient_method=hardware_wrapped_key` key-backup envelope, or any recovery / cross-signing proof requiring hardware attestation, lacks an `attestation` chain that the receiver can verify against the active recovery policy's `trusted_recovery_services[]`. See zh/identity/key-management.md §7.5.5.

Governance-plane resource selector wildcard (e.g. policy:*, schema:*, or a governance object:* selector) was used without the required mitigation (denied by deployment policy, or constrained with max_delegation_depth=0 plus bounded expiry plus admin approval). Receiver MUST reject.
A presigned blob URL was requested for a Realm whose policy sets direct_download_allowed=false. The service MUST deny presign and require access through the authenticated media proxy.

A presigned blob URL was requested for a Realm that requires minimal metadata or routing unlinkability. The service MUST deny presign and require an authenticated proxy, OHTTP relay, or equivalent non-bearer direct download path.

Read receipt visibility=public was combined with history_visibility=world_readable without an explicit opt-in marker. Reducer MUST reject the combination to avoid leaking actor read positions to anonymous observers.
An outbound agent-protocol handoff would emit E2EE Realm plaintext or derived content without a matching egress grant and data-class check. Session start MUST be rejected.
Retained erasure stub bytes do not match retained_stub_digest in the erasure receipt. Verifier MUST reject the receipt and treat the erasure as not completed (fail closed).

did:webvh resolution is in cache-only degraded mode and either the requested operation is outside the closed low-risk read-only set, or no sealed, controller-proof-verified cache evidence is available. Resolver MUST fail closed rather than treat unresolvable as valid.

An encrypted-attachment envelope carries a `scheme` value the receiver does not recognise. Receivers MUST fail closed rather than guess a decryption form. See zh/crypto-media/media-and-blob.md §3.2/§3.3.
Streaming-chunked AEAD attachment (`ck.blob.stream_aead.v1`): segment indices arrive out of order, skip a value, or leave a gap. Receivers MUST reject. See zh/crypto-media/media-and-blob.md §3.3.6.
Streaming-chunked AEAD attachment: a per-segment AEAD tag fails to verify. Receivers MUST reject the segment and abort the stream. See zh/crypto-media/media-and-blob.md §3.3.6.

Streaming-chunked AEAD attachment: the stream ended without a valid final segment (last_segment_flag never observed, or fewer segments than `segment_count`). Receivers MUST reject to resist truncation. See zh/crypto-media/media-and-blob.md §3.3.6.
Streaming-chunked AEAD attachment: a segment index appears more than once in the stream. Receivers MUST reject. See zh/crypto-media/media-and-blob.md §3.3.6.

Streaming-chunked AEAD attachment: a segment index is out of range, a segment length violates `segment_size`, or `segment_count` disagrees with the observed stream. Receivers MUST reject. See zh/crypto-media/media-and-blob.md §3.3.

A KeyPackage claim requested a last-resort fallback from a server that does not advertise `ck.feature.mls_last_resort_keypackage.v1`. The server MUST continue to fail closed on an empty single-use pool and MUST NOT return a `last_resort=true` package. See zh/crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md §2.6.2.
An attempt to reuse a last-resort KeyPackage outside its `intended_realm_id` Realm-scoped last-resort pool. Servers MUST reject. See zh/crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md §2.6.2.

A holder that joined groups via a last-resort KeyPackage came online but has not rotated the package and closed the forward-secrecy weakening window as required. See zh/crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md §2.6.2.

A Seal failed to discharge a FOCIL-style inclusion-list obligation: a listed, receipt-backed Control Move digest was neither included nor signed-rejected nor proven to fail batch pre-state verification within expiry_seal_count. Receivers MUST reject the entire Seal (rejected_seal). See authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 7.3 and schemas/inclusion-list.schema.json.

admission_class_definitions.capability_gated: Gated by one or more named capability actions listed in admission_capabilities. Reducer MUST verify the actor holds a matching action grant per capability-action-registry. Fail-closed.
admission_class_definitions.crypto_verifiable: Admitted by cryptographic verification of the payload against group/key state (MLS epoch, key material, franking) and its policy preconditions. Reducer MUST verify the cryptographic binding; not a user capability. Fail-closed.
admission_class_definitions.self_authored_proof: Admitted by a self-authored proof bound to the subject principal's identity (DID-bound signature / proof of possession with bounded freshness). Reducer MUST verify actor == subject and a fresh, replay-protected proof; no capability grant is consulted. Fail-closed: missing or stale proof MUST be rejected.
admission_class_definitions.service_attested: Written by a protocol service component (Auth/Gate server, Events node, applet host, agent runtime) under its service-DID attestation as part of operating the protocol. Reducer MUST verify the issuing service's authority and its binding to the subject/scope; not a user capability. Fail-closed.

event_kinds.payload: Realm official or sponsoring organization statement

Typed Realm link graph edge. link_kind declares governance / discoverability / import-export / confidential-extension semantics; it is never generic parent/child containment and never implicitly propagates membership, capabilities, history, E2EE keys, retention, or federation policy.
Realm preview / peek policy for directory card, stripped state, history stub, and plaintext history snippet projections
Enabled Realm policy components set. Payload MUST carry monotonic policy_revision; reducer rejects rollback or gaps and policy_frontier_digest MUST cover policy_revision.

Constraints on member delivery_binding: which binding_source values are admissible, which recipient services are allowed, which endorsers are required, whether DID Document fallback / unroutable membership are permitted, who may sign rebind. Governs reducer acceptance of ck.member.state{membership=join}.delivery_binding (see governance/join-policy.md §5.1).

Realm read receipt disclosure policy (disclosure / visibility / scope_overrides_allowed / allow_child_privacy_tightening_against_required); see zh/discovery/read-receipts.md §2.5 for the compliance-floor escape switch
Realm moderation policy (blocklists, allowlists, content filters)
Plaintext-visible services declaration outside E2EE boundary
Per-parent inheritance policy; one entry per source Realm
Realm tombstone lifecycle facet (terminal pointer to successor)
Realm destroy lifecycle facet (terminal decommission marker)
Circle create (intra-Realm scoped event/message boundary). Initializes independent MLS group and epoch-0 governance binding only when encryption_profile=mls_rfc9420. See zh/models/circle.md §3, §5.
Circle patch (ck.patch.v1 with path NOT containing realm_id / encryption_profile). Modifies title / summary / display / directory_visibility / join_rule / history_visibility.
Circle tombstone (terminal). Triggers lifecycle cascade per zh/models/circle.md §9.2.

Circle membership state. Uses the same membership_state enum as ck.member.state (invite/join/knock/leave/ban), scoped to a Circle. Reducer MUST first validate the target actor is a parent Realm `join` member, otherwise failed_precondition reason=circle_member_must_be_realm_member. See zh/models/circle.md §9.1.

Reducer-derived: Circle sub-seal commits opaque sub_seal_head_digest to the Realm Seal stream at the Circle's profile-defined cadence. MUST use time-based ticks + empty-batch commitment to avoid leaking activity frequency. See zh/models/circle.md §10.2.

Issuer-signed endorsement that a subject DID (typically an agent / service / hosted actor) is accountable_principal_ids the issuer for a declared scope (employment / contracted_service / agent_operator / etc.). Required to verify `Actor Profile.accountable_principal_ids[]` entries; reducer strips unverified DIDs from accountable_principal_ids. See zh/models/actor.md §3.3.1.

Notary equivocation evidence (Control Move). Payload carries signer_id plus the two conflicting Seal wire objects: same (realm_id, notary_seq) slot with different canonical bytes, or a notary_seq=k+1 Seal that does not descend from the same signer's notary_seq=k Seal (authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 7.1). Admission is verification-only: any Realm member MAY submit and the two conflicting notary signatures are the complete authorization; no capability grant is consulted and reducer MUST NOT require one. Reducer MUST re-verify both signatures and the slot rule, then add a per-signer fault record to the notary_fault cell. Once a fault record is accepted: receivers MUST reject later Seals signed by the fault signer, the two conflicting Seals and their descendants enter fork_quarantine, and Realm-wide pause applies only when no eligible signer remains.

Notary censorship evidence (Control Move). Payload carries signer_id, the signed control-plane receipt, the seal_ref of the Seal that was obliged to include / signed-reject / defer the pending Control Move, a control_event_set_root non-membership proof for the censored event digest, and the missing rejection-or-defer proof (authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 7.2). Admission is verification-only: the receipt holder MAY submit; the receipt signature plus the non-membership proof are the complete authorization. This evidence does NOT automatically disqualify the notary: reducer adds an audit fault record that MUST raise governance alarms, feeds inclusion-list / recovery obligations, and is evaluated by governance or the genesis recovery path.

Realm-scoped MemberIdentity segment replacement event. Append-only log entry that may supersede prior ck.member.identity.update events via payload.replaces[] without overloading ck.profile.update patch semantics.

Flow business-progression stage transition. Single source of truth for mutating Flow.stage / Flow.stage_changed_at; ck.flow.update patch on those paths MUST be rejected (forbidden-wire). The payload intentionally carries no reason / note / explanation field — rationale belongs in a Message on the Flow's discussion track that 'references' this event, and the event log's own actor_id / created_at is the audit source. Reducer enforces hard invariants from zh/models/common-fields.md §5.3.3: state=redacted yields failed_precondition reason=flow_already_terminal; state=archived yields flow_not_active; same-value self-transition is accepted but does NOT update stage_changed_at; reducer overwrites any wire-supplied stage_changed_at with the event's created_at. A per-Realm workflow profile MAY narrow which transitions are legal beyond these hard invariants.

Unified Flow tracks patch. payload.patch uses ck.patch.v1 against the Flow.tracks map: keys are track names (e.g. `synthesis`, `discussion`), values are patch ops that may toggle enabled, set is_primary, or modify profile / metadata on a track entry. Atomic across multiple tracks.

Flow move between Spaces (target_space_id in payload). Writes a cas_register cell keyed by (board_space_id, flow_id); the contains Relation list_space_id->flow_id is derived from cell value, not a separate truth source. Plane ruling (CBA): ck.component.flow.position.v1 defaults to sealed=true (control plane), so ck.flow.move is a Control Move carrying seal_basis; Realm schema MAY redeclare the cell family as data-plane mv_register + user-pick or per-object sequencer per authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 9.4 and models/realm-and-space.md section 3.6.

Flow reorder within Space. Writes the same cell as ck.flow.move; effect.list_space_id MUST equal head_eq.list_space_id (rank-only update). Plane ruling follows ck.flow.move: same cell family, same default sealed=true control-plane declaration (models/realm-and-space.md section 3.6).

Set or clear a per-(flow, actor) watch subscription. Writes a cas_register cell keyed by (flow_id, watcher_actor_id). Payload carries level in {mentions_only, participating, all, muted} (or null to clear, equivalent to mentions_only). Default invariant: payload.watcher_actor_id MUST equal envelope actor_id, unless writer holds ck.flow.watch.set.others. Cross-actor writes MUST carry refs[role=audit_pair] to a same-batch ck.audit.accessed event with access_kind=watch_set_others. The watches Relation (actor --watches--> flow) is a derived projection of this cell, not a separate truth source — direct ck.relation.create relation_kind=watches MUST schema_violation. See models/flow-and-message.md §8.
Space create (board / list / swimlane / calendar bucket / etc.)
Space metadata update (title, rank, kind-specific fields)

Space parent declaration. Parent is another ck:space: or null; cross-Realm parent is navigation only and never propagates Realm membership, capabilities, history, E2EE keys, retention, or federation policy.
Space archive (UI-level grouping archive; contained Flows MUST be relocated or follow archive)
Space restore (transition state archived -> active; only valid when current state == archived; tombstoned Spaces MUST NOT be restored)
Space tombstone (irreversible; contained Flows MUST be relocated before)
Message-scoped redaction; does not grant generic redaction authority
Generic redaction envelope for non-message objects/events and profile-declared content trimming

Morph schema_refs[] migration. First-class event for evolving a Morph's schema_refs[] without bypassing audit / capability gates. Carries (from_schema_refs[], to_schema_refs[], compatibility_class, migration_evidence?). Required capability ck.morph.schema_migrate (high risk tier; see capability-action-registry.json). compatibility_class = additive | breaking | transformation; core reducers MUST reject breaking/transformation unless the Realm declares ck.profile.morph.schema_migration_transformations.v1. See zh/models/morph.md §4.1 S3.

Morph business-progression stage transition. Single source of truth for mutating Morph.stage / Morph.stage_changed_at; ck.morph.update / ck.morph.schema_migrate patches on those paths MUST be rejected (forbidden-wire). The payload intentionally carries no reason / note / explanation field — rationale belongs in a Message on an associated discussion track that 'references' this event. Reducer enforces hard invariants from zh/models/common-fields.md §5.3.3: state=redacted yields failed_precondition reason=morph_already_terminal; state=archived yields morph_not_active; same-value self-transition is accepted but does NOT update stage_changed_at; reducer overwrites any wire-supplied stage_changed_at with the event's created_at.

Agent signing key authorization. Payload MUST validate as event-payload.schema.json#/$defs/agent_key_authorize_payload and bind agent_principal_id, key_id, verification_method, accountable_principal_id, agent_key_scope, audience, issued_at, expires_at, and approval_evidence.

Agent signing key revocation. Payload MUST validate as event-payload.schema.json#/$defs/agent_key_revoke_payload and bind agent_principal_id, key_id, revoked_at, and revoked_by; the revocation's control-plane basis is the Control Move envelope seal_basis, and its cutoff is the accepted Seal covering the Move.

Agent signing key rotation. Payload MUST validate as event-payload.schema.json#/$defs/agent_key_rotate_payload; key_id names the retiring key and replacement_key_id names the new key under the same accountable_principal_id with equivalent or narrower agent_key_scope.

Agent lifecycle transition to paused state (CKP-0008 §4.11). Auth Server MUST reject new agent session grants for this principal; existing tokens fail closed within the revocation freshness window. Reversible via ck.agent.resume.

Agent lifecycle transition from paused to active (CKP-0008 §4.11). Reducer MUST re-validate controller, agent, key, capability, Realm policy, and accountability_grant freshness; any failure rejects the resume.

Agent lifecycle terminal state (CKP-0008 §4.11). MUST fan-out ck.agent.key.revoke for all active agent keys, ck.capability.revoke for all active grants, and runtime endpoint revocation. Terminal — no transition out.

Agent-initiated draft proposal (CKP-0008 §4.8). Submitted by agent runtime; Principal Server materializes accepted drafts into controller-owned ck.agent.draft.v1 account-data after capability / policy / accountability / risk check. MUST NOT enter shared Realm history.
Agent-initiated action request (CKP-0008 §4.8). Carries proposed_action, target descriptor, and content digest. Awaits controller approval before generating shared event.

Controller approval of a draft / action request (CKP-0008 §4.8.1). Binds draft_id, content digest, target descriptor, proposed_action, approved payload digest, approval expiry, and single-use nonce. Publish executor MUST atomic-consume the nonce; reuse fails closed (reason=approval_already_consumed).
Controller rejection of a draft / action request (CKP-0008 §4.8.1). Draft transitions to rejected; agent runtime MUST NOT continue publish attempts.
Holder-private consent declaration: 'I consent to receive <consent_scope> from <peer>'
Revoke a previously granted consent (shares the ck.consent.grant cell; semantically a remove on the consent or_set)
Principal-scoped contact request fact. Issuer is requester; target holder must respond with accepted/rejected.
Principal-scoped contact acceptance fact. Issuer is original request target and MUST reference target-controlled consent grants.
Principal-scoped contact rejection fact. Issuer is original request target and does not write consent.
Principal-scoped contact tombstone fact. Issuer ends their own side of a contact and may revoke contact-managed consent dots.
Principal-scoped binding from unordered participant pair to canonical DM Realm and main Flow.
Realm-scoped profile override. payload.target_realm_id is the target Realm and no Space boundary is created.
Key backup active series selection for one principal and backup_class.

Push route binding for a (recipient_service_did, principal, device, push_route) tuple. Carries push_target_id, push_gateway_did, encryption_key, capabilities. Stored as actor-private state on the recipient Principal Server only; MUST NOT be replicated to Principal Servers outside the binding's recipient_service_did context.
MLS commit or Welcome processing failure diagnostic

Auditable access marker for privileged reads or privacy-sensitive paired writes. E2EE compliance release uses ck.audit.release; ck.audit.accessed remains for non-release audit pairs such as Circle metadata audit, watch_set_others, late recovery, and policy reads.

Audit Applet Binding. Declares that an audit applet/service may request staged historical release sessions for a specific Realm or Circle effective_scope. Binding is control-plane only: it does not add the applet to MLS, does not subscribe it to realtime sync, and does not grant plaintext/history keys. Bindings are non-retroactive: activation_frontier_digest / first_auditable_epoch define the earliest eligible material, and later policy changes MUST NOT expand eligibility for already encrypted messages.
Audit release session request. Must reference an active ck.audit.applet_binding and a bounded historical target range or target_refs.
Audit release session authorization by a scoped approver. Approves only the intersection of request, binding, policy, and effective_scope.
Member-visible notice for an audit release session. Circle-scoped notices are visible only to the target Circle audience and authorized moderators/admins.

Sealed audit release manifest. Records exactly which historical target_refs or sealed epochs were released, to whom, under which binding/session/notice/policy. Current active epoch release is forbidden; sealed epoch releases must reference sealed_by_commit_ref.
Close an audit release session and freeze its final release_refs.
Signed hard-erasure receipt. Attests deletion outcome and retained verification stub within an issuer-declared storage boundary; does not prove independent third-party copies disappeared.

Range-bound completeness attestation. Distinct from ck.audit.ryw_receipt (per-event read-your-writes hint) and ck.event_batch_receipt (set-bound integrity hint): this attestation asserts completeness over an explicit (from_frontier, to_frontier) + per-actor seq interval range. Issuer commits to having observed every reducer-input event in scope; witness quorum or independent seal backing is required for non-self-attested deployments. See zh/sync/operations-sync.md §4.2.
Lift a previously sealed moderation decision

Submit an appeal against an existing ck.moderation.decision. Writes the appeal cell to state=submitted. Schema: ck.schema.moderation_appeal.v1. See zh/governance/content-moderation.md §5.5 (appeal flow).
Reviewer acknowledges the appeal and transitions cell state submitted → under_review. Identifies the reviewing actor and target appeal. Schema: ck.schema.moderation_appeal.v1.

Reviewer's verdict on the appeal: uphold (decision stands) / overturn (decision reversed, emits ck.moderation.decision.lift) / modify (decision adjusted). Transitions cell state under_review → decided. Schema: ck.schema.moderation_appeal.v1.

Closes the appeal from submitted / under_review / decided via reviewer close, appellant withdrawal, or timer auto-close. Locks against re-appeal of the same target by the same appellant during the cool-off window. Schema: ck.schema.moderation_appeal.v1.

Read cursor advance event (actor-private). Writes the actor's latest read position for a given (realm_id, read_scope) tuple. Was historically named ck.read.cursor; renamed to align the event_kind, capability action, schema id and typed ID prefix on a single noun root read_cursor.

Invite create. Directed v1 invite payloads carry invitee plus invite_delivery_target and introduction_evidence_digest; raw locator tokens and invite_receive_policy state are private and MUST NOT enter the durable Realm event.

payload_schema_contract.non_critical_extension_rule: Unknown non-critical payload fields are preserved in canonical bytes and MAY be ignored by reducers. Unknown critical payload semantics MUST be declared in Event.requirements.critical_extensions and fail closed when unsupported.
payload_schema_contract.validation_rule: Every active standard ck.* event kind MUST be validated by the Event Envelope schema and one payload class selected by kind. Unknown standard kind, unmatched active kind, or payload class failure is schema_violation before reducer execution.

registry_rules: Standard ck.* effect kinds MUST appear in this registry when used by a DataEvent effect, Control Move effect, or Event Envelope payload router.

Events API, Sync durable history, Federation, and canonical reducers MUST accept only active entries with wire_scope=durable_event unless an implementation profile explicitly defines a private channel for actor_private_event.
Entries with wire_scope=ephemeral_event MUST be carried only on ephemeral channels and MUST NOT advance Seal coverage, governance state_root, or reducer state.

Entries with wire_scope=actor_private_event MAY be persisted in encrypted account data or an actor-private stream, but MUST NOT be inserted into shared Realm data-plane history or control-plane Seal history.

Reducer-input durable kinds MAY declare cell_family, cell_subject, lattice, bottom, and (cas_register only) initial_value. cell_family is a stable ck.component.*.v<n> URI; cell_subject is null, a payload field path, or a composite descriptor; bottom is reject or expose. initial_value declares the value the cas_register reports before any DataEvent or Control Move effect has been applied; declaring `initial_value="__unset__"` combined with `head_eq:"__unset__"` Control Move predicates implements singleton-once-set cells.

Registered exemption: protocol-singleton cells that are not written through a single event_kind are NOT indexed here. Currently the only such cell family is ck.component.notary.v1 (per-Realm notary cell, lattice=cas_register, bottom=reject): its genesis value comes from the ck.realm.create payload notary object and subsequent changes are ordinary notary-finalized Control Moves; its canonical definition lives in zh/authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 4.4. Any future cell family without a single writer kind MUST be added to this exemption list explicitly.

Lattice MUST be one of: core types or_set, mv_register, cas_register, fsm, counter, ordered_log; or extension types lww_register, rga (only declarable on cells with cell_role in {ui_affordance, content, draft, cosmetic} and only valid for receivers that implement ck.profile.collaborative_text.v1; receivers without that profile MUST fail closed with unsupported_lattice_type when an event_kind references a cell using lww_register or rga). Authorization, policy, notary, membership, and lifecycle cells MUST NOT use lww_register or rga.

State convergence is defined by CBA: DataEvent effects are locally accepted against seal_ref, Control Move effects are finalized by Seals, and per-cell Lattice join remains deterministic. Event Envelope routing fields MUST NOT be used as ordering authority.

Every active durable reducer-input event_kind MUST have a machine-readable admission source: either at least one capability action targets it (capability_action_registry.target_event_kinds), or it declares an admission class from admission_class_definitions. capability_gated events MUST list the authorizing action(s) in admission_capabilities. Enforced by lint_artifacts.py; no active durable reducer-input event may lack an admission source (fail-closed).

wire_scope_definitions.actor_private_event: Persisted actor-private/account-data event; not shared Realm history and not Realm reducer input.
wire_scope_definitions.durable_event: Valid Event Envelope kind for persisted canonical history and reducer input.
wire_scope_definitions.ephemeral_event: Transient sync/federation/app signal; MUST NOT be persisted as durable Event Envelope history.

registry/exporter-label-registry.json.description: Canonical registry of all normative MLS-Exporter labels in Cokret v1 (media key derivation, routing-tag HMAC keys, AEAD nonce-prefix derivation). Each label is a wire-breaking security-domain-separation parameter: implementations MUST use the exact label string and Context field shape registered here, MUST NOT derive with an empty Context, and MUST NOT migrate or reuse keys across labels without declaring a new profile. Per-entry `defined_in` points to the normative defining document. See zh/crypto-media/media-service-binding.md §8 and conformance/conformance-vectors.md §12.7.

labels.label: ck-rtc-frame-key/v1
labels.purpose: SFrame per-sender media frame key (E2EE media frames)

labels.label: cokret-reaction-routing-v1
labels.purpose: Keyed-HMAC key for the plaintext reaction routing tag in E2EE Realms (reaction_routing_hmac_v1 = HMAC-SHA256(key, utf8(canonical_emoji)); the exporter output is the HMAC key)

labels.label: cokret-mention-routing-v1
labels.purpose: Keyed-HMAC key for the opt-in mention routing sidecar tag in E2EE Realms (mention_routing_hmac_v1 = HMAC-SHA256(key, utf8(mentioned_did)); the exporter output is the HMAC key; Sync Service MUST NOT derive, receive or persist the exporter secret)

labels.context_encoding: canonical-bytes of the JSON object {"key_ref", "epoch", "device_id", "purpose", "aead_profile"} (not a bare string)
labels.label: cokret-aead-sender-nonce-prefix-v1
labels.purpose: Per-sender AEAD nonce prefix for every AEAD-bearing v1 envelope (nonce = sender_nonce_prefix || device_nonce_counter_be64); canonical derivation defined once in encoding.md, domain documents only declare their `purpose` value

allowed_context_definitions.changelog: Reference in CHANGELOG or migration documentation.
allowed_context_definitions.interop_module: Reference in interop binding documentation (e.g., MIMI / Matrix interop).
allowed_context_definitions.legacy_migration: Reference in dated migration guides describing legacy state.
allowed_context_definitions.negative_test: Reference in negative fixtures / cotest drift tests.

registry/forbidden-model-terms.json.description: Terms that MUST NOT be used in current-model prose, code identifiers, or UI copy when referring to v1 core concepts. cotest scanner greps downstream prose and source for these terms and flags occurrences outside allowed_contexts.

entries.notes: Contrix is the legacy brand name (lowercase `contrix`, wire prefixes `cx.` / `cx:`). Use Cokret / cokret / `ck.` / `ck:` in all current prose, identifiers, file names, and UI copy. See renames.json migration group brand_namespace_cx_to_ck.

Room is not the v1 core model. Use Realm (federation / identity / replication boundary), Circle (intra-Realm scoped event/message boundary; see zh/models/circle.md), Flow, or Space as applicable. 'Room' is permitted only when contrasting v1 with Matrix in interop documentation.
List-shaped containers are Spaces, not Realms. Realm remains the boundary concept; container shape (board / list / etc.) lives on Space.
Branch terminology was removed across Flow. Use track (display-only segment identifier). Variable / field names containing 'flow_branch' MUST be renamed.

Track does not carry independent membership; the entire Flow shares one effective scope (Flow.scope_circle_id). UI copy and docs MUST refer to Realm members or Circle members (per zh/models/circle.md). A Flow needing its own membership boundary MUST set scope_circle_id to point at an intra-Realm Circle; per-track membership boundaries do not exist.
entries.replacement: Realm members (or Circle members, when Flow.scope_circle_id points at a Circle)

entries.notes: Visibility is split in v1 into three independent axes: Discoverability, Join Rule, History Visibility (see spec-map 3.4). 'Room visibility' conflates them and MUST NOT be used.
entries.replacement: Realm history visibility / discoverability / join rule

entries.notes: Place was the pre-inversion container-shape model name. After the Realm/Space inversion the container model is Space (board / list / etc.) and the security boundary is Realm. 'Place' MUST NOT appear as a core model name in current normative prose, SDK identifiers, or UI copy. Existing zh prose still mentioning 'Place' MUST be migrated to 'Space (container)'.

Use 'External Collaboration Realm' (the role defined in zh/models/realm-and-space.md §2.7). The sovereign-deployment policy bundle that historically motivated the 'Controlled' prefix is now expressed as 'in sovereign deployment, External Collaboration Realm MUST satisfy …' and lives in zh/sync/sovereign-deployment.md §4 under ck.profile.sovereign_deployment.v1; it is not a Realm subtype. The infrastructure-isolation pattern 'Controlled Collaboration Enclave' is a separate, unchanged concept.

Chinese form of 'Controlled Collaboration Realm'; use 'External Collaboration Realm' per zh/models/realm-and-space.md §2.7. The strict sovereign-deployment policy previously implied by '受控' is now stated as a deployment-profile requirement on External Collaboration Realm in zh/sync/sovereign-deployment.md §4.

The bare phrase '协作 Realm' was used historically with two distinct meanings: (a) in identity / consent / profile chapters, contrasting with Principal Control Realm — replace with 'Collaboration Realm'; (b) in sovereign-deployment / architecture chapters, implicitly meaning a cross-trust-domain Realm — replace with 'External Collaboration Realm'. Bare '协作 Realm' is docs_only (kept in CHANGELOG / migration prose) because the phrase still reads naturally as a descriptive Chinese noun phrase; for new normative content, use the precise category from realm-and-space.md §2.7. Compound descriptive uses (e.g. '大型协作 Realm', '多方协作 Realm') are unaffected by this entry — they describe a Realm's scale or membership shape, not the Realm category.
entries.replacement: Collaboration Realm / Internal Collaboration Realm / External Collaboration Realm（视语境而定）

entries.notes: Legacy Contrix wire namespace prefix. Current Cokret v1 canonical event/profile names use ck.; cx. may appear only in migration notes or negative tests.
Legacy Contrix typed-ID prefix. Current Cokret v1 typed IDs use ck:; cx: may appear only in migration notes or negative tests.

Use plaintext for unencrypted user-readable material. cleartext is a legacy synonym and MUST NOT appear in current normative prose, code comments, identifiers, or UI copy except when naming historical forbidden fields in migration or negative-test contexts.

rejection_levels.compat_only: Allowed only in interop / compatibility documentation.
rejection_levels.docs_only: Removed from current normative prose; survives in CHANGELOG / glossary deprecation notes.
rejection_levels.hard_reject: MUST NOT appear in current normative prose, current SDK / service code identifiers, or current UI copy describing v1 core model.
rejection_levels.migration_only: MAY appear in clearly-marked migration documentation referencing legacy state.

allowed_context_definitions.changelog: Reference in CHANGELOG or migration documentation.
allowed_context_definitions.interop_module: Reference in an explicit interop binding (e.g., MIMI interop) where the cross-protocol mapping requires the field.
allowed_context_definitions.legacy_migration: Reference in time-bounded migration code that rewrites stored legacy bytes.
allowed_context_definitions.negative_test: Reference in negative fixtures / cotest drift tests that assert rejection.

registry/forbidden-wire-fields.json.description: Field names that MUST NOT appear on the current Cokret v1 wire in the contexts listed below. Each entry pins the context (top-level envelope, specific payload class, etc.) because a name may be legal elsewhere. cotest scanner walks Event Envelope / payload bytes and flags any occurrence outside the entry's allowed_contexts.

entries.notes: Legacy Matrix-style 'branch' top-level field on timeline / Flow events is replaced by the v1 'track' concept (a display-only timeline segment identifier). See current-model 'Track 是纯展示 / 时间线分段标识'. The string 'branch' MUST NOT appear as a top-level Event Envelope or payload field name.
Wire fields that carry one concrete Flow.tracks map key use `track_name`. The plural `tracks` map and `allowed_tracks` capability constraint remain valid collection names.

When the plaintext counterpart is `content`, the encrypted counterpart is `encrypted_content` (Flow, Message, Morph). Generic `encrypted_payload` remains valid for non-content carriers such as identity and reaction payloads.

Flow and Morph user-readable title is metadata. It MUST NOT be a top-level object wire field; in MLS / E2EE scopes it travels inside encrypted_metadata unless the Realm explicitly opts into plaintext metadata.

Flow and Morph user-readable summary is metadata. It MUST NOT be a top-level object wire field; in MLS / E2EE scopes it travels inside encrypted_metadata unless the Realm explicitly opts into plaintext metadata.
Extensible user metadata fields live under metadata.fields, or inside encrypted_metadata when the effective metadata profile requires encryption.
Room core model was removed; Realm is the v1 boundary. 'room_kind' MUST NOT appear on the wire outside an explicit MIMI / Matrix interop module.

Flow payload field 'kind' (or any analogous discriminator) MUST NOT carry the literal value 'room'. Use 'realm' / 'flow' / canonical Realm.kind values. Interop translation lives in an opt-in interop module only.

Flow payload MUST NOT carry 'discussion_space_ref'. Discussion privacy is represented by Circle-scoped Flow objects and confidential_discussion_of Relation facts; the field-level Circle identifier is 'scope_circle_id' (see schemas/flow.schema.json, zh/models/circle.md).

Single concrete protocol object identifiers use `_id`; `_ref` is reserved for causal, proof, schema/profile, content-addressed, or polymorphic reference material. The old fields parent_ref, default_realm_ref, scope_ref, default_scope_ref, retention_policy_ref, disclosure_policy_ref, rate_limit_policy_ref, and Policy-object policy_ref MUST NOT appear on current v1 wire.
entries.replacement: parent_space_id / default_realm_id / scope_circle_id / default_scope_circle_id / retention_policy_id / disclosure_policy_id / rate_limit_policy_id / policy_id

entries.notes: Capability grant constraints that contain one concrete identifier kind use `_ids`, not `_refs`. The old fields allowed_view_refs, allowed_flow_refs, allowed_circle_refs, denied_flow_refs, allowed_space_refs, denied_space_refs, realm_refs, and approval_actor_refs MUST NOT appear on current v1 wire. Polymorphic container constraints allowed_from_container_refs / allowed_to_container_refs remain `_refs` because they may identify Space, Flow, or Morph containers.
entries.replacement: allowed_view_ids / allowed_flow_ids / allowed_circle_ids / denied_flow_ids / allowed_space_ids / denied_space_ids / realm_ids / approval_actor_ids

entries.notes: The abbreviated media participant typed ID prefix was expanded to the full snake_case kind. Current v1 wire MUST use ck:rtc_participant:<uuid>; ck:rtcpart:<uuid> is rejected.
Key backup KDF params use digest_algorithm for PBKDF2/derived digest selection. The old params.hash selector is ambiguous with digest bytes and MUST NOT appear on current v1 wire.

member_delivery_binding references the policy revision Event that authorized a delivery binding, not a Policy object. The field therefore carries explicit event-reference semantics as policy_event_ref.
The child_scope_policy discriminator now names the concrete field it requires: scope_circle_id.

Range-completeness event_range, audit RYW receipt, and POST /events response MUST use 'realm_frontier'. The replication and security boundary covered by this frontier is the Realm, not an in-Realm Space container. 'space_frontier' MUST NOT appear on the current wire as a frontier object property.

Relation MUST carry rank at the top level, not nested under fields. The dual-source (top-level rank vs fields.rank) ambiguity is closed: writers MUST emit top-level rank only, and readers MUST reject fields.rank with schema_violation. See zh/models/relation.md §2.
Space MUST carry rank at the top level. Mirrors the relation_payload constraint; closes the dual-source ambiguity uniformly. See zh/models/realm-and-space.md §3.2.

Space is a container, not a security boundary. A legacy space-create / space-update payload carrying Realm-level security_class is the pre-inversion Space-as-boundary shape and MUST be rejected; migrate it to Realm payload fields.
Join policy is Realm-scoped. Space payloads MUST NOT carry join_rule; this closes the current Space container model versus removed pre-inversion payload-shape ambiguity.
entries.replacement: ck.realm.join_rule or ck.realm.policy_components join policy facet

entries.notes: History visibility is Realm-scoped. Space payloads MUST NOT carry history_visibility.
Policy server attachment is Realm-scoped. Space payloads MUST NOT carry policy_server.
Delivery binding policy is Realm-scoped. Space payloads MUST NOT carry delivery_binding_policy.

ck.message.create payload MUST NOT carry revision_root. The reducer initializes revision_root to the new message_id; only ck.message.revise (and subsequent revise events) may set revision_root, and only to the create's revision_root. See zh/models/flow-and-message.md §9.

Composite Content Block MUST use the field name `parts` (matching schemas/message.schema.json, schemas/event-payload.schema.json, schemas/flow.schema.json, and schemas/morph.schema.json). The temporary `blocks` spelling was rejected because it over-constrained the concept to document layout blocks; the canonical wire name is `parts`, and `blocks` MUST NOT appear in current content_block_composite wire. See zh/models/content-types.md §4.10.

Encrypted Envelope MUST NOT carry `cleartext_commitment`. The bare plaintext hash is dictionary-attackable offline against low-entropy plaintext; v1 E2EE producers MUST NOT emit it and receivers MUST reject any envelope that carries it (top-level `not.required` in schemas/encrypted-envelope.schema.json). Future profiles needing plaintext commitment MUST define a keyed/salted form rather than this bare hash.

Flow MUST carry stage at the top level (required field). The dual-source (top-level stage vs metadata.fields.stage) ambiguity is closed: writers MUST emit top-level stage only, and readers MUST reject metadata.fields.stage with schema_violation. Same constraint as fields.rank in relation_payload / space_payload. See zh/models/flow-and-message.md §3.2 and zh/models/common-fields.md §5.3.

Flow stage_changed_at is reducer-derived and lives at the top level. It MUST NOT be smuggled under metadata.fields.* and MUST NOT be supplied by actor on wire (reducer overwrites with the triggering ck.flow.stage.set event's created_at). See zh/models/common-fields.md §5.3.3 rule 3.

Reserved-name guard. Flow stage transitions intentionally do NOT carry a reason / note / explanation field anywhere — neither on the object, nor in the ck.flow.stage.set payload, nor under metadata.fields.*. Human-readable rationale belongs in a Message on the Flow's discussion track that 'references' the stage event; audit attribution is provided by the event log's own actor_id / created_at. The metadata.fields.stage_reason path MUST be rejected to prevent implementations from re-introducing the field through a back door.
entries.replacement: Message on the Flow's discussion track that references the ck.flow.stage.set event

entries.notes: Reserved-name sister-guard for metadata.fields.stage_reason. Closes 'stage_note' / 'stage_comment' / 'stage_explanation' style re-spellings via metadata.fields.*. Same canonical channel: a Message on the discussion track that references the ck.flow.stage.set event.
entries.replacement: Message on the Flow's discussion track that references the ck.flow.stage.set event

entries.notes: Reserved-name guard: 'lifecycle' is reserved terminology for the state axis (archive / restore / tombstone lifecycle events). It MUST NOT appear on the wire as a metadata.fields.* key on Flow. Business-progression goes through the top-level 'stage' field; physical lifecycle through 'state'. See zh/models/common-fields.md §5.
entries.replacement: stage (top-level Flow field) or state (physical lifecycle)

entries.notes: Reserved-name guard: 'progress_state' is a sister name for the stage concept and MUST NOT appear under metadata.fields.*. Implementations expressing business progression MUST use the canonical top-level 'stage' field.

Reserved-name guard: 'status' is the most direct sister spelling of the stage concept and MUST NOT appear as a metadata.fields.* key on Flow. Business progression goes through the canonical top-level 'stage' field; physical lifecycle through 'state'. Domain data mirrored from external systems MUST use a domain-named key (e.g. fields.jira_status), not bare 'status'.

Flow assignment is single-sourced by the standard assigned_to Relation. metadata.fields.assignee would create a second truth source and MUST be rejected; UI labels may say Assignee but wire writes create/tombstone assigned_to Relation edges.
Plural spelling of the Flow assignment field alias is forbidden for the same reason as metadata.fields.assignee. Multiple assignees are represented by multiple active assigned_to Relation edges.
assigned_to is already the standard Relation kind and MUST NOT be reused as a Flow metadata field.
assigned_actor_ids is a derived projection field, not Flow object state. Writers MUST NOT persist it under metadata.fields.
entries.replacement: read-only projection assigned_actor_ids derived from assigned_to Relations

entries.notes: Morph MUST carry stage at the top level (required field). Mirror of the flow_payload fields.stage constraint.
Morph stage_changed_at is reducer-derived and lives at the top level.
Reserved-name guard mirror for Morph. Stage transitions carry no reason field; rationale belongs in a discussion-track Message that references the ck.morph.stage.set event.
entries.replacement: Message on an associated discussion track that references the ck.morph.stage.set event

entries.notes: Reserved-name sister-guard for Morph fields.stage_reason. Same forbidden surface as Flow.
entries.replacement: Message on an associated discussion track that references the ck.morph.stage.set event

entries.notes: Reserved-name guard mirror for Morph: 'lifecycle' is reserved for the state axis.
Reserved-name guard mirror for Morph.

ck.flow.update payload's patch MUST NOT include path 'stage' or 'stage_changed_at'. Stage transitions are single-source: only ck.flow.stage.set may mutate these fields. The wire-level guard is the same pattern as forbidding ck.message.create from carrying revision_root — a forbidden patch path on an otherwise-shared payload class. cotest scanners MUST flag any patch op whose path matches /^stage(_changed_at)?$/. See zh/models/flow-and-message.md §3.2 reducer hard constraint 5.
ck.flow.update MUST NOT patch assignment through Flow metadata. Assignment writes create or tombstone assigned_to Relation edges.
Plural assignment metadata patch alias is forbidden; multiple assignees are multiple assigned_to Relation edges.
assigned_to is a Relation kind, not a Flow metadata patch path.
assigned_actor_ids is projection-only and MUST NOT be written through ck.flow.update.
entries.replacement: read-only projection assigned_actor_ids derived from assigned_to Relations

entries.notes: Legacy Flow fields.* patch paths are not the canonical metadata path; assignment is Relation-sourced regardless of spelling.
Legacy plural assignment patch alias is forbidden; multiple assignees are multiple assigned_to Relation edges.
assigned_to is a Relation kind, not a Flow metadata patch path.
assigned_actor_ids is projection-only and MUST NOT be written through legacy fields.* patch paths.
entries.replacement: read-only projection assigned_actor_ids derived from assigned_to Relations

entries.notes: ck.morph.update / ck.morph.schema_migrate payload's patch MUST NOT include path 'stage' or 'stage_changed_at'. Stage transitions are single-source: only ck.morph.stage.set may mutate these fields. See zh/models/common-fields.md §5.3.3 reducer hard constraint 6 and zh/models/morph.md §2.
Validity lower bounds use not_before. Current writers MUST NOT emit valid_from.
Validity upper bounds use expires_at. Current writers MUST NOT emit valid_until.
Validity upper bounds use expires_at. Current writers MUST NOT emit not_after.
Cache expiry fields use cache_expires_at.
Anonymous health frontier cache bound uses cache_expires_at.
Proof signer key material is expressed as verification_method.
Sender identity fields must carry the role and id suffix explicitly.
Sender display names in projections carry the sender_actor role prefix.

Audit Applet Binding ID. Created by ck.audit.applet_binding and referenced by audit session request/authorize/notice/release events.

Stable identifier for one chain of encrypted backup envelopes belonging to a single (actor_id, backup_class). Circle object ID — intra-Realm scoped event/message boundary. Hosts its own membership (strict subset of parent Realm.members), history visibility, delivery/query/projection boundary, and optional independent MLS group. Device identifier (ck:device:<uuid>). A device is a typed ID scoped to an owning principal, NOT a DID and NOT an actor principal. Device keys are registered as verification methods under the owning principal DID via ck.device.authorize.

Stable session identifier bound by every proof transcript, backup decrypt proof and MLS Welcome replay during one recovery flow. Referenced by ck.schema.recovery_receipt.v1 and by §15 recovery proofs. See crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §15.

Space object ID — structural grouping object inside a Realm (board, list, swimlane, calendar bucket, etc.). Authorization-transparent: never carries its own membership / policy / E2EE group; resolves to the containing Realm.
Realm object ID — security / sync / auth / E2EE boundary. Always carries membership, policy, history_visibility, MLS group binding, and federation policy.

storage_rules: Protocol wire objects, canonical JSON, signatures, hashes, fixtures, logs, API DTOs, and cross-service references MUST use the full typed form ck:<kind>:<uuid> unless a special form below applies.

Storage implementations MAY store raw 16-byte UUID values (e.g. PostgreSQL `uuid` column) without the ck:<kind>: prefix when the table, column, or explicit kind field already supplies the type context.
Implementations that store raw IDs MUST restore the full typed form before computing canonical JSON, event IDs, payload hashes, detached proofs, federation payloads, sync cursors, or audit logs.
The <kind> segment is part of the signed/canonical wire value. It MUST NOT be changed, inferred differently, or stripped during verification, forwarding, backfill, or replay.

The UUID segment MUST be RFC 9562 UUID version 7 (48-bit Unix-millisecond timestamp + 4-bit version=7 + 12-bit rand_a + 2-bit variant=10b + 62-bit rand_b), serialized as the canonical 36-character lowercase hex form `xxxxxxxx-xxxx-7xxx-Nxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx` where N ∈ {8,9,a,b}.

ciphersuites.security_note: RFC 9420 mandatory-to-implement suite; classical X25519 KEM (not post-quantum; hybrid KEM migration path reserved via ck.aead.hybrid_kem.* namespace and future hardening profile).

registry/mls-ciphersuite-registry.json.description: Canonical MLS (RFC 9420) ciphersuite vocabulary for v1 KeyPackage cipher_suites[] negotiation and server describe surfaces. Completes the algorithm-agility registry symmetry with digest-suite-registry.json and signature-alg-registry.json.
registry_rules: Schema / describe enum values for MLS ciphersuite fields MUST be generated from active rows' canonical_id.

A ciphersuite not present as an active row MUST fail closed in KeyPackage claim / group negotiation (unsupported ciphersuite); receivers MUST NOT accept unregistered suites even if the underlying MLS library supports them.

New suites (e.g. ChaCha20-Poly1305 for AES-accelerator-less devices, hybrid PQ KEM suites per the encryption-and-audit.md PQ roadmap note) enter additively as new rows with their own profile gates and conformance vectors; the registry is intentionally minimal and does not pre-register suites without an implementation plan.

registry/mls-extension-registry.json.description: Canonical registry of Cokret-defined MLS (RFC 9420) GroupContext extensions occupying the MLS private-use ExtensionType range 0xF000-0xFFFF. Maintained so SDKs and conformance tooling have a single machine-readable entry for each Cokret MLS extension codepoint, preventing collisions between future Cokret extensions in the private-use range and recording any future migration to an IANA standard codepoint.

extensions.carries: Cokret Realm/Circle governance binding inside the MLS GroupContext
extensions.migration: If a network-wide registration is ever required, request a standard codepoint via the IETF MLS extensions registry (specification-required) and declare it in a new hardening profile as a separate wire version; do not override this binding with another codepoint inside v1. Target alignment (2026-06 review): restate governance_binding against the draft-ietf-mls-extensions Safe Extension API (safe GroupContext component semantics + IANA safe labels + LeafNode safe_extensions capability signal) so its security argument can ride the framework's generic analysis; after RFC, request both the standard codepoint and a safe label, and review Cokret exporter labels (e.g. ck-rtc-frame-key/v1) against the IANA label registration discipline. If the binding proves fully expressible as a safe GroupContext component, switching the wire form is a v2-cycle decision, not a v1 change.

capability_tiers.core: Base interoperable surfaces implied by claiming Cokret v1 protocol support (service discovery, identity registry, events/account aggregate).
capability_tiers.deployment_local: Deployment-specific, operator, or product-local surfaces that MUST NOT be assumed from core protocol support alone.

capability_tiers.interop_bridge: Adapter surfaces that bridge Cokret to external protocols (MIMI Internet-Drafts, third-party Applet hosts). Implementations advertise these only when the external protocol is supported; bridge operations are not part of any core or extension profile and frequently mirror an in-spec operation via bridges_to.

Explicit, cumulative, monotonic to-device delivery acknowledgement (client-sync.md §10.1). Queue deletion happens only here; stream cursor advancement (account subscribe after=, device_messages from=) is read-only and MUST NOT prune the queue. Re-acking the same or an older token is a legal no-op. Unknown / expired / cross-bound tokens are rejected with invalid_param (reason invalid_ack_token) without deleting anything.
Writes requester-side ck.contact.requested fact and requester-side consent grants for requested scopes; MUST NOT write target consent or accepted fact.
Target-side accept/reject of a contact request. Accept writes target-controlled consent grants; reject writes no consent.
Holder contact projection from contact facts plus consent-derived directional scopes; account-data contact notes are local decoration only.
Holder-side contact tombstone. Default revocation is limited to contact-managed active consent dots.

Read the authenticated subject's private invite-receive policy. Returns the recommended default when no explicit override is stored; the response is never written into the target Realm durable event log.

Replace the authenticated subject's private invite-receive policy. The body MUST set subject_id equal to the session actor; the override shares the same store as ck.self.contact.tombstone(block_peer) blocked_subjects writes.
Idempotent resolver for accepted contacts. Requires accepted contact projection and direct_message consent; create=true creates canonical DM Realm, main Flow, and binding.

HTTP-specific POST/body form of ck.events.query. Semantically identical (same selector / cursor / order / filter / include_completeness parameter set, same response shape including optional range_completeness). Choose when URL length would exceed practical limits (large realms[]/actors[] arrays, complex filters object) or when query parameters would be logged inadvertently by proxies. Non-HTTP transports MUST use the canonical ck.self.events.query binding (SelfEvents/Query / self.events.query), not expose this variant as a separate gRPC or MQ operation.
Dereference a known set of event_id / event_digest references to full EventEnvelope objects. Point lookup by identifier, not a range scan — use ck.self.events.query for selector-based reads.

Long-lived per-Realm / actor event stream with optional bounded catch-up replay. `dropped` and `resync_required` control frames MAY carry `reconnect_after_ms`, a server-directed minimum delay before opening another subscription for the same caller/selector scope; early reconnects are rejected with rate_limited / Retry-After.
Federation peer Events surface describe. This endpoint describes the server-to-server peer event bindings; it is not a client self/events binding.

Federation peer frontier probe. Requires service-to-service authentication, Source/Destination service DID headers, trust-domain headers, and Realm federation_peer authorization. It returns the federation peer frontier response shape on the dedicated peer trust surface.

Federation peer pull/backfill query. Uses the same selector, cursor, order, and response semantics as ck.self.events.query, but the HTTP trust surface is peer and the caller MUST be an authorized federation peer service.
HTTP-specific POST/body form of ck.peer.events.query. Semantically identical to GET /_cokret/peer/events; use it when federation selectors or filters are too large or sensitive for query strings.

Federation peer event reference resolution for missing prev_refs / causal references. Requires authorized federation peer service authentication and applies the same reference-disclosure and history-visibility rules as peer event query.
Federation peer event push. Body is EventsSubmitFederationRequestBody and the caller MUST use service-to-service authentication with Source/Destination service DID and trust-domain headers.

Private Principal Server to Principal Server invite delivery. Requires service-to-service authentication, Destination-Service-DID equal to invite_address.recipient_service_did, a ck.invite.create event whose invitee equals invite_address.subject_id, and introduction_evidence accepted by the recipient invite_receive_policy.

Private Principal Server to Principal Server contact fact delivery. Requires service-to-service authentication, Destination-Service-DID equal to contact_address.recipient_service_did, and a signed ck.contact.* envelope the recipient projects into the target holder's contact projection without re-signing.
Federation peer snapshot manifest head for snapshot-assisted bootstrap. Requires service-to-service authentication and Realm federation_peer authorization.

Canonical broadcast ephemeral send operation for ck.schema.ephemeral_envelope.v1. Carries ck.presence, ck.typing, ck.receipt.read, and ck.call.signal; MUST NOT persist the signal as a durable Event or advance actor_seq / Realm frontier.

Media service token exchange operation (CKP-0010). Issues a short-lived (TTL <= 600s) backend_token + participant_binding for joining a focus declared in ck.realm.media_service.foci[]. Same wire across all backend types (livekit / mediasoup / janus / cokret-native); only backend_token shape is type-specific. Token issuer DID MUST be one of the Realm-authorized media service DIDs; clients reject otherwise (token_issuer_unauthorised). See zh/crypto-media/media-service-binding.md §3.

Read the currently accepted ck.schema.recovery_policy.v1 projection for the authenticated or explicitly selected principal. Returns active_policy=null when no accepted policy exists; does not publish, rotate, or revoke policy state.

Resolves an online invite locator token carried out-of-band, usually as a URL fragment in a QR/link. The locator token MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; the response is a signed principal_locator.
Canonical HTTP binding is POST /_cokret/self/policy/check. Paths carry no version segment; protocol version is negotiated via *.describe / supported_operations (see sync/api-conventions.md).
Extension read surface for reducer-maintained Flow lifecycle projection rows scoped by realm_id. This is a derived read model, not a canonical truth source.
Extension read surface for reducer-maintained Morph lifecycle projection rows scoped by realm_id. This is a derived read model, not a canonical truth source.
Extension read surface for reducer-maintained Space lifecycle projection rows scoped by realm_id. This is a derived read model, not a canonical truth source.

Optional extension read surface that materializes a View{kind=collection} projection such as board/list/table/calendar. The response is a derived read model computed from signed Events, reducer profile, View definition, and the returned frontier; it is not a canonical truth source.

Optional extension read surface for a single document Morph projection. It returns authorized document body, version, relation, comment, and cursor-presence read-model data for the addressed Morph; canonical truth remains the Morph/Relation/Message event history.

Holder-bound one-shot read of the current principal account projection. Returns principal_id, account lifecycle state, device summaries, optional ActorProfile, and signed handle-claim evidence or refs. It MUST NOT return an unsigned bare handle as authoritative identity. Naming: the trailing segment 'viewer' is intentionally outside the api-conventions.md §2.4 read-verb taxonomy; it follows the GraphQL 'viewer' convention (the authenticated subject's own projection). The target is located by the holder-bound session rather than an external id, so 'get' does not apply, and 'viewer' (subject identity projection) stays distinct from 'describe' (service capability metadata).

Holder-bound service wrapper around ck.profile.update / Actor Profile projection. Request body is a closed patch over display_name, avatar_blob_ref, and profile_fields.<key>; bio migrates to profile_fields.bio and avatar_url is not accepted on the Cokret protocol path.

Streaming push of cross-Realm account-aggregate deltas (cross-Realm frontier, to_device queue, account_data, device_lists, presence, unread / notification counts). Connection is long-lived; server pushes NDJSON frames as new data becomes available. Symmetric with ck.self.events.subscribe — both are streaming subscriptions, differing only in scope (self.events.subscribe = per-Realm event log; self.account.subscribe = account-aggregate). `dropped` and `resync_required` control frames MAY carry `reconnect_after_ms`, a server-directed minimum delay before opening another subscription for the same principal/device/filter scope; early reconnects are rejected with rate_limited / Retry-After. Replaces the prior Matrix-derived long-poll ck.account.sync; not wire-compatible with Matrix /sync.

High-assurance optional endpoint to revoke a previously issued cursor authority. Revocation hits return cursor_revoked and MUST NOT advance account subscribe position, barrier wait, or dropped recovery state. To-device queue deletion is decoupled from cursors entirely and happens only via ck.self.device_messages.ack.

registry_rules: New operation_id values MUST be added here before any OpenAPI, HTTP binding table, SDK generator, or alternative transport binding references them.
Generated views MAY change shape, grouping, or field order, but MUST NOT introduce, rename, or remove operation_id values that are absent from this catalog.
Supporting Cokret core does not imply support for every registered operation. Implementations MUST advertise supported_operations and supported_profiles explicitly.

Each surface_groups entry carries a tier (see capability_tiers); only the core tier is implied by claiming v1 protocol support. Extension, interop_bridge, and deployment_local surfaces require explicit advertisement.

Profile matrices in artifacts/profiles/conformance-profiles.json define role-level MUST/SHOULD requirements; the surface groups below define machine-readable capability families for discovery, docs, and lint.
