rules.endpoint_aliases: Each operation entry lists its canonical HTTP method+path alias for human navigation; alternative bindings (gRPC, MQ) inherit the same error code set.
rules.operation_coverage: Every operation_id in artifacts/registry/operation-registry.json MUST appear exactly once in operations[]. An empty operation_specific[] means the operation has no domain-specific reply shape beyond the universal failure surface.
rules.operation_specific: operation_specific[] lists the error codes that are semantically tied to this operation's domain logic (event ingest, key claim, blob upload, push gateway, directory ingest, ...). An entry may name either a top-level code from error-code-registry.json `codes` or a sub-code from its `reason_codes` section (carried under a top-level code such as failed_precondition or schema_violation). Consumers discriminate by first matching the entry against the registry's top-level `codes` set; an entry not found there is a reason_code and matches the error reply's `reason_code` field rather than its top-level `code`. Receivers SHOULD recognize and surface these codes specifically.
rules.universal_codes: Every protected operation MAY additionally return any of: unauthenticated, auth_expired, soft_logged_out, did_proof_required, invalid_signature, capability_denied, schema_violation, bad_json, bad_query, missing_param, invalid_param, rate_limited, too_large, conflict, internal_error, service_unavailable, not_implemented, unsupported_feature, unsupported_event_kind. These are the universal failure surface and are NOT repeated in each operation entry.

registry/profiles-dependency-graph.json.description: DAG view of profile inheritance / dependency / mutual-exclusion edges. Consumed by zh/conformance/conformance-profiles.md §2.1 visualization tooling. Profiles whose only relationship is to be claimable on their own (no inherits / depends_on / mutually_exclusive_with) MAY be omitted from the edges[] list; they still appear in nodes[].

edge_kinds.depends_on: A profile that depends_on another MUST be claimed alongside that target profile; absence of the target MUST cause the claimant to be treated as unsupported.
edge_kinds.inherits: A profile that inherits another transitively re-declares its required_endpoints / required_event_kinds / required_schemas / required_capability_actions. Inheritance edges are transitive and form a DAG (no cycles).
edge_kinds.mutually_exclusive_with: Profiles linked by this edge MUST NOT be claimed together; reducer / discovery MUST reject the combination (typically with reason_code conflicting_*_profiles).

vectors.description: Streaming chunked AEAD (ck.blob.stream_aead.v1) happy path: multi-segment plaintext with a short final segment is split, per-segment AEAD encrypted, segment-wise downloaded and incrementally verified, and the top-level ciphertext_digest is recomputed and matches per media-and-blob.md section 3.3.

Streaming AEAD truncation: a dropped final segment, a last segment whose flag stays 0x00, or segment_count exhausted without last_segment_flag=0x01 MUST be rejected with segment_stream_truncated and buffered plaintext discarded.
Streaming AEAD ordering: out-of-order / skipped / gapped segment_index MUST be rejected with segment_sequence_invalid; a repeated segment_index MUST be rejected with segment_replay.

Streaming AEAD scheme closure: an unknown attachment scheme MUST fail closed with unsupported_attachment_scheme (no fallback decrypt); an envelope carrying both whole-file nonce and chunked nonce_prefix/segment_* fields MUST fail blob.schema.json encrypted_attachment oneOf validation.

Federation ingress authentication-failure family (unknown peer / not authorized / target absent) returns indistinguishable responses within one timing bucket per relation.md section 4.5 sampling rules.

service_binding_ref.reducer_profile_digest is computed per federation.md section 4.1.1 from the reducer-profile-registry.json digest_input row (Cokret canonical JSON, sha256); receiver recomputes and byte-compares, rejecting the whole batch with reducer_profile_mismatch on any divergence.

New passphrase_kdf backup envelopes below the unconditional base KDF floor (Argon2id memory_kib>=65536 / iterations>=3 / parallelism>=1; PBKDF2 iterations>=600000 with allowed digest_algorithm) MUST be rejected.
Key backup retrieval requires a session-bound unlock proof (ck.schema.key_backup_unlock_proof.v1); any binding mismatch or bearer-token-only access fails closed before ciphertext is returned.

Last-resort KeyPackage (ck.feature.mls_last_resort_keypackage.v1): when the normal pool is empty, claim MAY return last_resort=true; the package is reused across multiple Welcomes within the same intended_realm_id, consume is idempotent (stays published, never keypackage_already_consumed), and each consumption emits an append-only audit record per encryption-and-audit.md section 2.6.2.

Last-resort KeyPackage forced rotation: on next online the holder MUST rotate the last-resort package (new init key, old marked rotated) and trigger an MLS self-update Commit on every group joined via it to advance the epoch and close the forward-secrecy weakening window.

Last-resort KeyPackage Realm affinity and optionality: cross-intended_realm_id reuse MUST be rejected with last_resort_realm_affinity_violation; a server not declaring the feature MUST fail closed on an empty pool and MUST NOT return a last_resort package, with explicit last-resort fallback returning last_resort_not_supported.

Appeal verdict transitions are atomic: overturn without a same-batch ck.moderation.decision.lift is rejected with appeal_overturn_missing_lift; modify requires a same-batch new decision matched by modify_decision_ref.

E2EE franking proof construction, report submission, and moderator-side verification roundtrip per content-moderation.md section 3.4; digest mismatch or minimal-disclosure violations downgrade or reject the proof.
Seal canonical bytes exclude id and notary_signature; verifier recomputes the typed id and signature payload digest from signed top-level fields only.
cas_register writes on non-initial state require an explicit CBA basis: Control Move preconditions or equivalent DataEvent causal/lattice proof; null-basis blind overwrites fail closed.
Expired policy decisions and decisions bound to an older auth/policy/membership frontier MUST be rejected on replay; receivers fail closed and re-request the policy check.
Receivers recompute the RFC 8785 JCS request_canonical_digest of the presented request body; mismatch with the signed bound_to transcript MUST reject the decision.

Sender-constrained session PoP: a write request with a valid RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signature (kid = current grant session_public_key, covering @method/@target-uri/@authority/content-digest) is accepted; a signature whose transcript mismatches the method/path/body digest fails verification and is rejected per api-conventions.md section 3.2 and service-http-binding.md section 2.5.

Under ck.profile.high_security_organization.v1 / sovereign_deployment, plain Authorization: Bearer (no Signature) on regular writes / sensitive reads MUST be rejected with unauthenticated, while the default profile accepts it as a compatibility downgrade; a PoP signature whose created/expires falls outside the replay window MUST be rejected.

Client events.query backfill with include_completeness=true detects withheld actor branches via ck.attestation.range_completeness verification; feature-less servers ignore the parameter; single_source attestation does not satisfy high-assurance realms.
Canonical JSON object key ordering follows UTF-16 code units for supplementary-plane keys.
Blind-index stale postings after revocation, visibility tightening, redaction, expiry, or epoch rotation MUST not produce unauthorized recall.
Search hit is not an authorization proof; unauthorized or unverifiable hits return non-enumerating stubs.
Receiver rejects sender_nonce_prefix collision or nonce prefix mismatch.
Receiver rejects repeated per-device AEAD nonce counter.
Receiver rejects pure random 96-bit nonce profile for v1 encrypted attachments.

reports/operation-schema-index.json.description: Generated DTO index for registered operations with request_schema_ref/response_schema_ref. JSON Schema files remain the canonical source; this report is a machine-readable summary for SDK/conformance tooling and prose drift review.

handle_claim_ref.description: Opaque reference to a signed ck.schema.handle_claim.v1 claim, such as an event ref, issuer-local receipt ref, or content-addressed artifact ref.

propertyNames.description: ck.self.account.update_profile only accepts display_name, avatar_blob_ref, and profile_fields.<key>. The bio is carried as profile_fields.bio.

schemas/account-operations.schema.json.description: Closed request and response DTOs for account self-service operations: viewer, register, profile update, and session revocation.
schemas/account-operations.schema.json.title: Cokret Account Self-Service Operation DTOs

ack_token.description: Server-issued opaque acknowledgement token, REQUIRED whenever messages[] is non-empty. Bound server-side to (principal_id, device_id, queue high-water position of this batch) and covering this batch plus all previously delivered messages. NOT a cursor: no ck:cursor: wire form, no cursor schema/TTL/purpose. The client passes it verbatim to ck.self.device_messages.ack AFTER durably persisting the batch payloads; queue deletion happens only through that explicit ack, never through stream cursor advancement (client-sync.md §10.1).

limited.description: True when this account subscribe to_device batch is truncated because the device queue exceeds the stream frame budget. When true, `next_cursor` is REQUIRED and the client MUST continue with ck.self.device_messages.get?from=<next_cursor>; the top-level account stream cursor MUST NOT be used as the to-device queue pagination cursor.

lost.description: SHOULD be set true when the server has dropped unacknowledged messages for this device (expiry or capacity) since the device's last acknowledged position. Clients SHOULD trigger key recovery paths (key backup / key re-request) and MUST NOT silently assume the queue was complete.

next_cursor.description: Read-only to-device queue continuation cursor for ck.self.device_messages.get?from=... . It is not an acknowledgement and MUST NOT delete queued messages; queue deletion happens only through `ack_token` passed to ck.self.device_messages.ack.

handle_claim_digests.description: Digests of currently visible effective ck.schema.handle_claim.v1 objects for this member in the current Realm context. MUST be omitted unless subject_id is disclosed, because stable claim digests are linkable across contexts. Absence is not proof that the member has no handle.

handle_claims.description: Optional inline signed handle claim evidence. MUST be omitted unless subject_id is disclosed, and every included claim MUST have claim.subject equal to subject_id. Services may omit this for privacy, size, or freshness; clients can backfill by subject via ck.directory.list_handles_for_subject.

handle_claims_limited.description: True when handle_claims[] is truncated or replaced by digest-only hints. Clients MUST NOT interpret missing claims as no handle.

identity_event_ids.description: Effective ck.member.identity.update event ids for this actor after replacement refs are applied.

identity_events.description: Optional inline effective ck.member.identity.update Event envelopes. When present these are the original events, not query-time re-encryption or projection rewrites. MUST be omitted unless subject_id is disclosed, because plaintext or decryptable identity events can disclose the same member subject.

member_display_state_digest.description: Digest over the effective identity event references plus the current visible handle claim digest set for this roster entry.

subject_id.description: Optional disclosed principal / holder DID for this member. Omit when subject disclosure is only available inside encrypted MemberIdentity or not authorized for the caller. Required whenever handle claim evidence or digest hints are included.

bottoms.description: Structured Bottom diagnostics for cells whose effective Lattice join resolved to ⊥ under the current CBA query basis. Each entry pins (cell, status, bottom). See zh/sync/service-surface.md §5.3.

event_states.description: Per-event protocol-state views (event_id + event_state) for reducer-input events carried by this entry. The 'bottom' detail object lives separately in 'bottoms' below — keyed by cell, not duplicated per event — so wire body is not doubled. Receivers correlate event_state=failed_bottom with the cell-level bottom diagnostic via the cells listed in bottom.cells[]. See zh/sync/service-surface.md §5.3.

event_state_reason_code.description: Optional short reason code (e.g., 'recovery_witness_missing'). For failure detail beyond the enum.

members.description: Lightweight roster hint derived from effective ck.member.state, effective ck.member.identity.update references, and currently visible handle-claim evidence. Entries MUST NOT carry display fields or naked handle strings directly; handle strings may appear only inside signed ck.schema.handle_claim.v1 objects.

members_limited.description: True when members[] is truncated and MUST NOT be treated as the complete Realm roster.

members_next_cursor.description: Optional pagination cursor for continuing member roster retrieval.

prev_cursor.description: Stream cursor pointing backward in the timeline for backfilling history before this batch.

schemas/account-subscribe-frame.schema.j.description: Single NDJSON frame on the ck.self.account.subscribe streaming channel (GET /_cokret/self/account/subscribe, Content-Type: application/x-ndjson). Each newline-delimited line is one frame object. Discriminated by the `kind` field: `delta` carries account-aggregate data (cross-Realm frontier, to_device, account_data, device_lists, presence, notifications, unread counts); the other kinds are control frames that mirror ck.self.events.subscribe (`catchup_complete`, `frontier`, `heartbeat`, `dropped`, `resync_required`, `unauthorized`). `dropped` and `resync_required` MAY carry `reconnect_after_ms` as a server-directed minimum delay before opening another account subscribe stream for the same principal/device/filter scope.

oneOf.description: Catch-up replay or initial baseline completed; no data fields are allowed.
Cursor-only frontier advancement; no data fields are allowed.
Account stream gap signal; cursor is the account catch-up start. No data fields are allowed. `reconnect_after_ms` MAY be present to enforce a server-directed reconnect holdoff.
Keepalive frame; cursor and data fields are forbidden.
Hard reset signal; cursor and data fields are forbidden. `reconnect_after_ms` MAY be present to enforce a server-directed reconnect holdoff.
Authorization-loss signal; cursor and data fields are forbidden.

account_data.description: Account-scoped private data updates on `delta` frames.

cursor.description: Stream cursor (purpose='stream'). On `delta` / `catchup_complete` / `frontier` frames it points to the position covered by this frame; pass back as `after=` on the next subscribe call to resume. REQUIRED on `dropped` frames as the account-aggregate catch-up start for `GET /account/subscribe?after=<cursor>&catchup=true`. MUST be present on `delta` / `catchup_complete` / `frontier` / `dropped`; absent on `heartbeat` / `resync_required` / `unauthorized`.

partial.description: When true on a `delta` frame, the per-Realm timelines are limited (truncated); client SHOULD backfill via ck.self.events.query for any Realm whose timeline carries `limited=true`.

priority.description: Optional server-side priority hint for the frame (UX scheduling).

realms.description: Per-Realm map on `delta` frames. Keys are `ck:realm:*`; values are that Realm's aggregate timeline/state/account-data entry. Membership lifecycle (`join` / `invite` / `knock` / `leave`) is carried by the events inside the Realm entry.

reconnect_after_ms.description: Optional server-directed minimum delay, in milliseconds, before opening another `ck.self.account.subscribe` stream for the same principal/device/filter scope. MAY appear only on `dropped` and `resync_required` frames. This is a stream reconnect hint, not a generic error retry field; it does not apply to unrelated API calls. Clients MUST wait at least this delay before reconnecting, and servers MUST reject earlier reconnect attempts with `429 rate_limited` plus `Retry-After`.

schemas/account-subscribe-frame.schema.j.title: Cokret Account Subscribe Frame

actor_kind.description: Directory / UX classification only. MUST NOT participate in authorization, reducer acceptance, capability resolution, or any wire-protocol decision: those MUST consult DID + Grant + Constraint exclusively. Implementations are free to use actor_kind for icon selection, directory filtering and presentation, but a wrong value MUST NOT widen or narrow what a principal can do. Does NOT include 'device': a device is not an actor principal and has no DID of its own; its identity is device_id (ck:device:<uuid>) plus a verification method under the owning principal DID. See zh/models/actor.md.

agent_slug.description: Projection hint for a controller-scoped selector slug backed by ck.schema.agent_selector_claim.v1. Only valid when actor_kind=agent under ck.profile.personal_agent_provisioning.v1; it is not a global handle and MUST NOT be used for authorization, attribution, or Directory discovery. The mention input token @<controller-handle>/<agent_slug> resolves to this actor's principal_id before persistence only after selector claim validation.

handle.description: Cokret canonical handle string: <localpart>:<domain>. The @ mention sigil is not part of the handle.

status.description: Public projection of the account lifecycle status values defined in zh/identity/account-lifecycle.md §3. Implementations MAY hide or coarsen this field in projection views, but the wire enum mirrors ck.account.status.

agent_slug.description: Controller-scoped native personal agent selector slug. Used only as the right-hand component of @<controller-handle>/<agent_slug>; not a global handle or authorization subject. Provisioning services that accept this field MUST issue or update a ck.schema.agent_selector_claim.v1.

opaque_local_id.description: Deployment-local short-lived account/auth artifact id. It is not a ck:<kind> protocol object id.

schemas/agent-operations.schema.json.description: Closed request and response DTOs for account pairing and native personal agent management operations.
schemas/agent-operations.schema.json.title: Cokret Account Pairing and Agent Operation DTOs

schemas/agent-selector-claim.schema.json.description: Signed claim binding a controller-scoped native personal agent selector slug to an agent principal DID. It powers @<controller-handle>/<agent_slug> compose-time resolution without making the agent carry a public handle.

agent_slug.description: Controller-scoped slug used as the right-hand side of @<controller-handle>/<agent_slug>.

audience.description: Audience binding for restricted selector disclosure, such as a Realm ID, verifier domain, or service DID.

claim_scope.description: Optional scope such as realm_id, organization_id, purpose, allowed_operations, or disclosure policy tags.

controller_subject.description: Controller principal DID that owns the selector namespace.

issuer.description: DID that signs this selector claim. It is normally controller_subject; a delegated issuer MUST be authorized by controller_subject and bound in source_refs or proof evidence.

issuer_service_did.description: Service DID that served or vouched for this selector claim when distinct from issuer.

source_refs.description: Optional refs to accountability_grant, actor profile, provisioning, delegation, or revocation evidence.

subject.description: Native personal agent principal DID selected by (controller_subject, agent_slug).

visibility.description: Disclosure boundary for selector resolution. Restricted/private claims require audience and requester policy checks before returning subject.

schemas/agent-selector-claim.schema.json.title: Cokret Agent Selector Claim

schemas/agent.schema.json.description: Schema-registry object for agent protocol metadata snapshots. Event payloads for ck.agent.* MUST use the typed payload definitions in event-payload.schema.json; this object is not a loose transport envelope and is closed at the top level except for x_* extensions.

agent_id.description: Stable agent runtime identifier. v1 uses a DID here; ck:agent:* is not a registered typed-id kind. Agent session object ids use ck:agent_interop_session:* in their own fields.

audit_binding.description: Signed audit binding emitted with the terminal *.result event so callers can prove the agent runtime executed under a specific capability grant.

detail.description: Runtime-side detail surface (intermediate progress, bridge identifier, error context, etc.).

did_document_digest.description: Canonical hash of the DID Document used for agent endpoint validation.

did_document_version.description: Method-specific DID Document version / log entry id observed during endpoint validation, when available.

endpoint_url.description: HTTPS endpoint advertised by ck.agent.endpoint events.

params.description: Caller-supplied parameters for interop_session.start. Opaque to soland — agent runtimes interpret per agent manifest.

result.description: Terminal payload for ck.agent.interop_session.result. Free-form; agents document the shape.

service_entry_digest.description: Canonical digest of the matched DID service entry, bound into interop_session.start / status / result audit evidence.

service_entry_id.description: DID service entry id matched during endpoint validation.

session_id.description: Per-invocation correlation id used by interop_session.start / .status / .result to pair request/response.

status.description: Session status for ck.agent.interop_session.status events. Same enum as agent_interop_session_status_payload.status in event-payload.schema.json — the registry-object snapshot MUST carry the canonical session state machine, not a coarse subset.

schemas/agent.schema.json.title: Cokret Agent Protocol Object

schemas/applet-edge-operations.schema.js.title: Cokret Applet Edge Operation DTOs

ghost_actor_provision_outcome.description: Response for ck.self.applet.ghost.provision. Carries the durable event refs the Principal Server minted (or re-confirmed on idempotent re-provision): the Ghost Actor ck.profile.create ref and the ck.identity.accountability_grant ref, the latter also surfaced as the authorization_ref the bridge MUST place on subsequent ghost-authored Event Envelopes.

ghost_actor_provision_request_body.description: Request body for ck.self.applet.ghost.provision. ghost_actor_id MUST fall inside the actor namespace declared by the applet_id registration; protocol / tenant / external_user_id identify the external principal being mirrored.

schemas/applet-ghost-operations.schema.j.description: Closed request/response DTOs for ck.self.applet.ghost.provision. An installed Applet service / bridge asks the Principal Server to provision (or idempotently re-validate) an Applet-managed Ghost Actor profile plus accountability grant for one external user. The server MUST re-check applet_id / service_did / realm_id / ghost namespace against the active registration before minting anything.
schemas/applet-ghost-operations.schema.j.title: Cokret Applet Ghost Actor Operation DTOs

schemas/applet-install-operations.schema.description: Closed request/response DTOs for ck.self.applet.install.preview, ck.self.applet.install, and ck.applet.revoke. The InstallPlan body itself is defined in applet-install-plan.schema.json.
schemas/applet-install-operations.schema.title: Cokret Applet Install Operation DTOs

schemas/applet-install-plan.schema.json.description: Canonical plan returned by ck.self.applet.install.preview and recomputed by ck.self.applet.install before commit. plan_digest is calculated over the canonical InstallPlan object with plan_digest omitted.
schemas/applet-install-plan.schema.json.title: Cokret Applet InstallPlan

delegation_policy.description: Delegated native-user acting request. Defaults to false; enabled MUST be explicit.

detached_proof.description: Controller-DID detached-JWS proof shape, aligned with event-envelope.schema.json#/$defs/proof (the generic non-Event signed-object proof). Non-Event objects bind their canonical payload via payload_digest; Event proofs MUST instead use event_digest and event_proof.

e2ee_policy.description: MLS join request. Defaults to false; enabled MUST be explicit.

endpoint_policy.description: Supported Applet API endpoints and their auth requirement.

ghost_policy.description: Ghost Actor support and accountability template. enabled defaults to false semantics; an explicit boolean is required.

limits.description: Service-side resource hints derived into the registration manifest.

webhook_auth.description: HTTP message signature verification seal for transaction push. key_ref is the DID URL whose key verifies the signature; accepted_algs pins the acceptable signature algorithms.

widget.description: Optional widget origin / CSP / token scope / consent declaration.

schemas/applet-package.schema.json.description: Controller-signed package used to install an Applet. The package is a distribution object, not Realm history truth and not a grant. Principal Server / authz service derives ck.applet.registration and capability grants during ck.applet.install.

package_id.description: Distribution identifier only. Not a grant subject.

proof.description: Controller DID detached proof over the canonical package or derived registration object. proof.payload_digest MUST equal package_digest (proof over canonical package) or the derived registration object digest. Empty object is invalid.

schemas/applet-package.schema.json.title: Cokret Applet Package

schemas/applet.schema.json.description: Schema-registry object for applet protocol metadata snapshots. Event payloads for ck.applet.* MUST use the typed payload definitions in event-payload.schema.json; this object is not a loose transport envelope and is closed at the top level except for x_* extensions.

applet_id.description: Stable applet identifier. MUST be either a DID or the registered typed-id form ck:applet:<uuidv7>. Arbitrary opaque strings are not valid wire identifiers; bridge-specific aliases belong in namespace / external_ref fields.

detail.description: Bridge-side detail surface (echo response payload, error context, bridge identifier, etc.). Free-form object; bridges document their own schema.

manifest.description: Applet manifest snapshot at registration time (capability requirements, supported intents, etc.).

params.description: Caller-supplied parameters for interop_session.start. Opaque to soland — bridge implementations interpret per applet manifest.

runtime_status.description: Bridge-implementation-defined runtime status for ck.applet.interop_session.status events. v1 does NOT mandate a canonical applet session state machine (unlike ck.agent.* which uses the 9-value agent_interop_session_status enum); bridges MAY restrict the set further in their applet manifest. The field name is `runtime_status` (not `status`) to keep applet object snapshots distinguishable from the canonical agent session state machine in agent.schema.json.

service_did.description: DID of the service that hosts the applet runtime (used by registration / discovery).

session_id.description: Per-invocation correlation id used by interop_session.start / .status to pair request/response.

schemas/applet.schema.json.title: Cokret Applet Protocol Object

schemas/attestation-evidence.schema.json.description: Structured remote-attestation evidence envelope for an audit applet release service under ck.profile.attested_audit.e2ee.v1. This is the wire form behind audit_assurance_class=attested_hardware: a verifier MUST be able to validate release-service measurement, attestation chain trust root, attestation key freshness, operator identity, Realm/Circle binding, and audit release policy hash without trusting prose declarations. Evidence binds the controlled output path for ck.audit.release; it does not add the applet to MLS and does not grant realtime plaintext access. See zh/crypto-media/audited-e2ee.md §6.

attestation_chain.description: Ordered attestation evidence chain: leaf attestation (signed by the enclave) → intermediate (e.g. PCK certificate, AK certificate) → root (vendor attestation root certificate). Each item is base64url-encoded DER / CBOR per platform format. Verifier MUST validate signature chain and trust the root against the Realm-declared trust root list.

attestation_key.description: The attestation public key (extracted from the leaf of attestation_chain). ck.audit.release proofs and RYW receipt validation MUST be cryptographically bound to this attested output path when audit_assurance_class=attested_hardware.

audit_policy_version_digest.description: Same definition as ck.audit.ryw_receipt.audit_policy_version_digest — fixed sha256 over canonical JSON {realm_id, trust_domain, audit_binding, release_policy, release_window_policy, activation_frontier_digest, first_auditable_epoch} at the Realm policy frontier at issued_at. Lets verifier O(1) check that the policy classification this evidence was issued under matches the current binding/session state, cannot be reused across Realms, and cannot retroactively expand eligibility for already encrypted messages. This field is intentionally not hash-agile in v1; a future algorithm change requires a new schema/profile. See encoding.md §2 (canonical JSON) and audited-e2ee.md §6.

audit_purpose.description: Why this audit applet release service may output audit material. MUST match the active binding/session purpose; mismatch → audit_purpose_mismatch.

audit_service_actor_id.description: DID of the audit release service / applet actor whose controlled output path this evidence attests. MUST match the recipient_audit_actor_id or service actor accepted by the active ck.audit.applet_binding.

measurement.description: What is actually running inside the enclave / HSM / equivalent controlled output boundary. Verifiers compare this measurement to the measurement allowed by the active audit applet binding and release policy.

code_digest.description: Hash of the audit release service binary / image / policy bundle that the enclave loads. MUST be reproducible (signed by vendor build pipeline).

policy_version.description: Release service's compiled-in policy version (e.g. semantic version or git tag). MUST appear in the Realm/Circle audit binding's allowed release-service policy versions at issued_at.

report_data.description: Optional REPORTDATA-equivalent that binds the attestation to the release service public key or output-encryption key. Lowercase hex encoding of a 32–64 byte byte-string (pattern enforces an even hex length: each byte is exactly two hex characters; total 64–128 hex characters). Receivers MUST validate this binding when present.

operator_did.description: DID of the controlling organization actually operating this enclave / HSM. This intentionally keeps the _did suffix because it is raw external DID material being compared against service_did and Realm policy, not a protocol actor_id/principal_id alias. MUST match what the Realm policy lists as the allowed audit operator. Distinct from service_did when the operating org is different from the technical service DID (e.g. service hosted by org A on behalf of org B).

family.description: Attestation family. 'software_test_only' is for conformance fixtures and MUST be rejected by deployments declaring attested_hardware assurance.

proofs.description: Detached signature(s) over the canonical evidence bytes (all fields except `proofs`), signed by operator-controlled keys distinct from the enclave attestation key. Two-key separation: the enclave attests its own measurement; the operator separately attests that this enclave is the one they intend to deploy.

realm_id.description: Realm this attestation evidence is valid for. Verifier MUST require realm_id to match the MLS Welcome / Event Envelope Realm being joined or audited; identical audit_policy_version_digest values across Realms do not make evidence portable.

revocation.description: How the verifier should check whether attestation_chain leaves / intermediates have been revoked. Required when platform supports revocation (sgx_pccs CRL, tdx PCS, etc.).

service_did.description: Operating service DID hosting the audit applet or release service. MUST match the service_did in the active ck.audit.applet_binding / ck.audit.release chain.

validity.description: Validity window of THIS evidence. Verifier MUST reject evidence outside the window. For evidence presented under audit_assurance_class=attested_hardware (ck.profile.attested_audit.e2ee.v1), the verifier MUST reject evidence whose window (expires_at - not_before) exceeds 90 days; Realm/service policy MAY cap it lower. Evidence with a longer window MUST be treated as an elevated-risk signal and rejected by profile policy rather than silently accepted.

verification_method.description: DID URL the receiving verifier uses to resolve attestation_key. MUST live under audit_service_actor_id's DID Document or a DID Document explicitly delegated by the active audit binding. Fragment characters are constrained to RFC 3986 unreserved + `:` for stable key ids. DID method-name normalized to lowercase per W3C DID 1.0.

schemas/attestation-evidence.schema.json.title: Cokret Attested Audit Release Evidence

schemas/audit-ryw-receipt.schema.json.description: Read-Your-Writes receipt issued by an Events API node, witness, or peer Principal Server confirming that a ck.audit.release or other audit envelope has reached accepted state. Required by ck.profile.attested_audit.e2ee.v1 and ck.profile.disclosed_audit.e2ee.v1 before an audit applet release service may output wrapped material or plaintext evidence (see zh/crypto-media/audited-e2ee.md §6). The audit_assurance_class field MUST match the active Audit Applet Binding; mismatch fail closed.

audit_assurance_class.description: Audit assurance class propagated from the active Audit Applet Binding. attested_hardware = ck.profile.attested_audit.e2ee.v1 (TEE/HSM/enclave controlled release required). disclosed_policy = ck.profile.disclosed_audit.e2ee.v1 (process-only disclosure, NOT cryptographically enforced). Release services MUST propagate the binding-declared value verbatim; receivers MUST fail closed when this field disagrees with the binding/policy state at the receipt's frontier.

audit_policy_version_digest.description: Canonical hash of the Realm-bound audit release policy tuple from the receipt frontier. Computed as fixed sha256 over canonical JSON {realm_id: <id>, trust_domain: <trust_domain>, audit_binding: <object>, release_policy: <object>, release_window_policy: <object>, activation_frontier_digest: <hash>, first_auditable_epoch: <n>}. Lets verifiers atomically check that the receipt's claim matches the active binding/policy at this frontier without replaying events and prevents cross-Realm reuse or retroactive expansion of identical policy text. MUST match the receipt frontier's policy state and ck.audit.release.eligibility_proof; mismatch MUST fail closed (audit_receipt_invalidated). Required field — missing receipts MUST be rejected to prevent silent policy drift. This field is intentionally not hash-agile in v1; a future algorithm change requires a new schema/profile.

recovery_reason_code.description: Optional machine-readable code, set only when this RYW receipt covers a ck.audit.accessed Event emitted via the Late Key Recovery path (see zh/crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md §2.3.5 and zh/crypto-media/audited-e2ee.md §4.1). Payload value, not an error-code-registry reason_code. Used by audit projections to distinguish late-key-triggered accesses from first-access reads. When absent, the receipt covers a normal (first-access) ck.audit.accessed Event.

trust_domain.description: Deployment trust domain for the Realm at the receipt frontier. Verifiers MUST require this to match the current receive context and the enclosing audit Event Realm context before using audit_policy_version_digest.

witness_attestation.description: Witness attestation block. The receipt's independence is externally verifiable from the witnesses[] list rather than self-claimed via a single enum. See zh/crypto-media/audited-e2ee.md §4.1 / §4.1.1.

kind.description: Attestation kind derived from witnesses[]. 'federation_witness_attested' MUST be used iff witnesses[] contains >= 2 distinct entries (distinct issuer.did AND distinct controlling_organization AND distinct verification_method) AND each issuer.did is listed by Realm policy under audit.ryw_witnesses[]. 'single_source' MUST be used iff witnesses[] contains exactly 1 entry. Any mismatch between 'kind' and the witnesses[] cardinality / distinctness / Realm policy listing MUST be rejected with audit_receipt_invalidated. The value is externally verifiable from the witness list, not a self-claim.

witnesses.description: Externally verifiable list of witnesses attesting that the audit_event_id+audit_event_digest reached accepted state. The 'kind' field MUST be derivable from this list per the rules in §4.1.1.

attested_at.description: Time at which this witness attested. Receivers MAY use the latest attested_at across witnesses as the effective receipt timestamp.

controlling_organization.description: DID of the organization that controls the witness. This value is not self-attested: verifiers MUST resolve issuer DID Document and confirm its controller / service ownership chain matches controlling_organization. For 'federation_witness_attested', all witnesses' controlling_organization values MUST be pairwise distinct and MUST NOT equal the audit actor's controlling organization.

issuer.description: Service DID of the witness that produced this receipt.

verification_method.description: DID URL of the key the witness used to sign (e.g. did:web:...#key-1). MUST be distinct from other witnesses' verification_method values for 'federation_witness_attested' to be valid.

schemas/audit-ryw-receipt.schema.json.title: Cokret Audit RYW Receipt

schemas/authz-operations.schema.json.description: Closed response DTOs for authorization query operations that need operation-specific list envelopes.
schemas/authz-operations.schema.json.title: Cokret Authorization Operation DTOs

payload_digest.description: Hash of canonical AvailabilityReceipt bytes with signature omitted.

schemas/availability-receipt.schema.json.description: Signed holder commitment that Event bytes are available until retention_expires_at. Digest membership roots do not prove byte availability; CBA models availability independently.
schemas/availability-receipt.schema.json.title: Cokret AvailabilityReceipt

content.description: The binary blob content part in multipart/form-data. This field is not JCS-canonicalized as JSON; content_digest covers the bytes.

schemas/blob-operations.schema.json.description: Closed request/response DTOs for blob service operations whose wire shape is not the full blob metadata resource.
schemas/blob-operations.schema.json.title: Cokret Blob Operation DTOs

oneOf.$comment: whole-file AEAD form: single nonce, single ciphertext_digest
streaming chunked AEAD form (STREAM / OAE2): per-segment AEAD, per-object random nonce_prefix

key_ref.$comment: MUST stay identical to encrypted-envelope.schema.json#/properties/key_ref and encryption-and-audit.md §2.3.1. Closed MLS group-binding object; not an opaque string.

group_state_ref.description: v1 MLS group state lookup hint. MUST point to accepted ck.mls.genesis / winning ck.mls.commit / equivalent group state proof. Does NOT replace MLS transcript verification.

oneOf.description: Reference to accepted ck.mls.genesis / winning ck.mls.commit event.

not.$comment: byte counts use size_bytes
content hashes use content_digest with an algorithm prefix

realm_id.description: Owning Realm for authorization, asset privacy policy enforcement, retention and GC. MAY be omitted only for global / cross-Realm service blobs (e.g. avatar previews) explicitly authorized by the Blob Service deployment policy.

schemas/bottom.schema.json.description: Structured diagnostic for cell join values that resolve to bottom (⊥). Surfaced on /account/subscribe, /events, and state query responses when a cell's effective Lattice value is undefined under the current CBA query basis. See spec/v1/zh/authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md §5.1.

cells.description: Cell ids participating in the bottom diagnostic. Multi-cell when a multi-cell Control Move atomically failed across linked cells.

details.description: Free-form structured details specific to the diagnostic kind. Producers SHOULD use stable keys per kind (e.g. invalid_transition: from/to/expected_transitions; schema_error: schema_id/violation_path). Receivers MAY display but MUST NOT use for authorization decisions.

escalated_at.description: When the cell first crossed Realm.bottom_escalation_after_ms. Absent when within the grace window. Implementations SHOULD raise an out-of-band notification to admins / recovery governance once set.

event_ids.description: Reducer-input event ids whose effects (or precondition checks) produced this bottom. Empty allowed when the cell's bottom is structural (e.g. notary cell schema_error) and not tied to a specific event.

heads.description: When kind=conflict and the cell's lattice exposes multiple candidate heads (mv_register, or_set with conflicting tag values), the candidate values. Implementations MUST NOT pick a winner from this array; it is for UI / audit only.

kind.description: Why the join produced bottom. 'conflict' = concurrent cas_register / fsm divergence on safety-critical cell. 'invalid_transition' = fsm op violates allowed_transitions. 'missing_dependency' = event ref to absent / failed prior event. 'unauthorized' = event issuer lacks capability for the op (verifier-side). 'notary_split' = multiple Seal leaves diverge on next-seal authority. 'schema_error' = lattice op or value violates declared cell schema.

seal_view.description: Seal leaves and control frontier under which this bottom was observed. Diagnostics MUST pin this so the receiver can reproduce the join without ambiguity.

state_root.description: Control-plane state_root at observation time (recompute from Seal leaves). Optional when the diagnostic is emitted before state_root is computable.

schemas/bottom.schema.json.title: Cokret Bottom Diagnostics

allOf.$comment: Lint condition (2) from capabilities.md §18.1: grants whose actions[] include moderator-role actions MUST carry a constraint with depends_on_moderation_state=true. Conditions (1) and (3) (subject condition selector referencing moderation state, constraints referencing moderation queue/cell) are reducer-side lint and not enforced here.

items.description: Canonical action vocabulary. MUST be of the form ck.<segment>.<segment>... matching capabilities.md §5. Bare names without the ck. prefix are not permitted; consult capabilities.md before introducing new action names. Wildcards within a segment are not permitted in this schema; the resource selector controls scope, not action expansion.

constraints.description: Constraints applied to this grant. Delegation control MUST be expressed via a constraint with constraint_type='delegation_control' and 'max_delegation_depth' (canonical, see capabilities.md §10). The early-draft top-level 'delegable' boolean is removed — it duplicated max_delegation_depth=0 semantics with no precedence rule. Implementations MUST reject grants carrying a top-level 'delegable' field as schema_violation. Default when no delegation_control constraint is present: not delegable (equivalent to max_delegation_depth=0).

expires_at.description: Top-level grant validity end. Authorization evaluates this together with temporal constraints: effective_expires_at = min(expires_at, every temporal.expires_at present). Delegated grants MUST not extend beyond the parent's effective_expires_at.

issued_at.description: Grant issuance time — carries the 'creation time' semantics for a Capability Grant in place of the generic created_at (models/common-fields.md §3.2). Retention / audit / ordering queries MUST use issued_at / expires_at / revoked_at rather than falling back to created_at.

not_before.description: Top-level grant validity start. Authorization evaluates this together with temporal constraints: effective_not_before = max(not_before, every temporal.not_before present).

updated_at.description: Reducer-derived timestamp for the most recent grant lifecycle update. Ordinary grant body fields remain immutable; revocation still uses revoked_by/revoked_at.

updated_by.description: Reducer-derived actor that produced the most recent grant lifecycle update. Ordinary grant body fields remain immutable; revocation still uses revoked_by/revoked_at.

color_token.description: Color token from the spec-controlled palette. Clients MUST map token -> theme color (light/dark/high-contrast) consistently across devices; clients MUST NOT reassign tokens.

short_name.description: Human-facing short name. Unique per (realm_id, short_name) case-insensitive — reducer-enforced.

schemas/circle.schema.json.description: Circle — intra-Realm scoped event/message boundary. Hosts its own membership (strict subset of parent Realm.members), history visibility, and delivery/query/projection boundary. It may be plaintext delivery-only or MLS-backed depending on encryption_profile and parent Realm policy floor. It does NOT carry federation identity, policy server, or capability registry — those remain on the parent Realm. Circle is NOT a principal Group; principal-set capability narrowing belongs on Group / capability constraint / resource selector. See spec/v1/zh/models/circle.md.

agent_participation.description: Optional agent participation ceiling for this Circle: the maximum native personal agent behavior permitted in this scope. When omitted, inherits the parent Realm ceiling. Each bit MAY only tighten, never widen, the parent ceiling (reducer rejects a widening write with agent_participation_ceiling_widen); it is further tightened by any inner Flow ceiling. See zh/models/circle.md field table.

content_encryption_floor.description: Optional Circle-local content encryption floor. When omitted, the Circle inherits the parent Realm's content_encryption_floor. Effective floor = max(parent Realm content_encryption_floor, this field). May only tighten, never widen, the parent Realm floor, and the effective floor is a one-way ratchet: once e2ee_required has been accepted it MUST NOT be lowered back to allow_plaintext (reducer rejects with content_encryption_floor_downgrade). e2ee_required is only meaningful when encryption_profile='mls_rfc9420'; a Circle with encryption_profile='none' MUST keep allow_plaintext. See zh/models/circle.md §7.

directory_visibility.description: Who may see this Circle exists as a directory entry. 'members' means only Circle members see its title/display/member_count. 'realm_members' exposes directory metadata only and does NOT grant event or history access.

encryption_profile.description: Circle content encryption profile. create-locked. 'none' means plaintext delivery/query/projection isolation only and is allowed only when the parent Realm policy floor allows plaintext. 'mls_rfc9420' means the Circle owns an independent MLS group and MUST NOT derive its keys from the Realm-default MLS group.

history_visibility.description: Circle's own history visibility. Effective visibility MUST NOT be wider than the parent Realm's policy floor. See zh/authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md §6.

join_rule.description: How an actor becomes a Circle member. 'open' lets any active Realm member self-join. 'request' requires profile-defined application/approval. 'invite' requires Circle admin add or invite.

metadata_encryption_floor.description: Optional Circle-local metadata encryption floor (binary, symmetric with content_encryption_floor: allow_plaintext | e2ee_required). When omitted, the Circle inherits parent Realm's metadata_encryption_floor. May only tighten, never widen, parent Realm floor; the effective floor is a one-way ratchet (reducer rejects a lowering write with metadata_encryption_floor_downgrade).

mls_group_ref.description: Reducer-derived reference to the independent MLS group bound to (realm_id, circle_id). Present only when encryption_profile='mls_rfc9420'. Populated by ck.circle.create reducer; not actor-supplied on wire.

realm_id.description: Parent Realm. create-locked; Circle never re-binds to another Realm.

schemas/circle.schema.json.title: Cokret Circle

schemas/common-ids.schema.json.description: Shared typed-ID pattern $defs referenced cross-file by multiple object schemas so a single id-form change propagates without inline drift. Defs-only: not an object or event schema. See zh/models/common-fields.md §6 and artifacts/registry/id-kind-registry.json for the authoritative ID kind registry.
schemas/common-ids.schema.json.title: Cokret Common Typed-ID Definitions

effective_scopes.description: Optional shorthand. When present, MUST equal bidirectional_scopes.

invite_consent_grant_ref.description: Optional. Event ref of the peer-issued ck.consent.grant (scope invite or any) granting the holder the right to send Realm/Flow invites to this peer. Present only when granted_to_me includes invite or any. Used by the holder as consent_grant introduction evidence to invite this contact into a Realm without a locator URL.

peer_service_did.description: Optional. Principal Server service DID hosting the peer, when known (e.g. learned from a cross-Principal-Server contact delivery). Lets the holder address responses/invites to the peer's home server. Omitted for same-Principal-Server contacts.

message.description: Optional free-text greeting carried into contact_requested_payload.message. NFC-normalized per canonical encoding rules.

recipient_service_did.description: Optional cross-Principal-Server addressing (see contact-and-direct-conversation.md §4.1). When target is hosted on a different Principal Server, the requester MUST supply the target home service DID so the issuer-side server federates the signed ck.contact.requested fact via ck.peer.contacts.submit. Omit for same-server requests.

requester_service_did.description: Optional cross-Principal-Server addressing (see contact-and-direct-conversation.md §4.1). When the original requester is hosted on a different Principal Server, the responder supplies the requester home service DID so the accept / reject fact is federated back via ck.peer.contacts.submit. Omit for same-server responses.

block_peer.description: When true, additionally add the peer DID to the holder invite_receive_policy.blocked_subjects, so future invite delivery from this peer is dropped and disclosed opaquely. Models a hard block ("拉黑") on top of contact tombstone.

full_peer_revoke.description: When true, UI/admin explicitly requested revocation beyond contact-managed grant dots.

peer_service_did.description: Optional cross-Principal-Server addressing (see contact-and-direct-conversation.md §4.1). When contact (the peer) is hosted on a different Principal Server, the holder supplies the peer home service DID so the issuer-side server federates the signed ck.contact.tombstoned fact via ck.peer.contacts.submit. Omit for same-server tombstones; when absent the issuer falls back to the peer recorded peer_service_did on the stored contact row.

schemas/contact-operations.schema.json.description: Closed request/response DTOs for contact lifecycle operations and direct conversation resolver.
schemas/contact-operations.schema.json.title: Cokret Contact and Direct Conversation Operation DTOs

alg.description: JOSE-style algorithm identifier; MUST be present in the protocol algorithm registry.

kid.description: Verification method identifier within the principal's DID document or key log.

signature.description: base64url-encoded signature over the canonical 'ck-cross-signing-bind-v1\n' + canonical_json input, including trust_domain. See device-lifecycle.md §5.1.

verification_method.description: PSK kid that signed this subordinate key's canonical signing input.

schemas/cross-signing-publish.schema.jso.description: Payload content for ck.cross_signing.publish (schema_id ck.schema.cross_signing_publish.v1). Publishes the (PSK -> {SSK, USK}) binding to the principal control stream. Each subordinate key MUST carry a binding signature produced by PSK over a canonical signing input that includes trust_domain — see device-lifecycle.md §5.1.

expected_previous_generation.description: CAS precondition for the current accepted cross-signing generation. Initial publish uses 0. Reducers MUST accept only when this equals the current accepted generation and generation == expected_previous_generation + 1.

generation.description: Monotonically increasing publish generation. Each ck.cross_signing.reset MUST increment by 1. Receivers MUST reject publishes whose generation is <= the currently accepted generation.

trust_domain.description: Deployment-scope trust domain identifier. MUST match the receiver's current trust_domain and enters the PSK binding transcript so a publish from deployment A cannot be replayed into deployment B.

schemas/cross-signing-publish.schema.jso.title: Cokret Cross-Signing Publish

device_quorum_proof.description: Device-quorum proof. The schema enforces only the minimum wire shape (threshold>=1, signatures.minItems=1). Cryptographic and quorum verification are normative in zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §14.4: (a) every signature MUST verify against the public key of an authorized, non-revoked device in the principal's current device set at issued_at, over the §14.1 canonical input; (b) signatures MUST be deduplicated by device_id; (c) the count of valid, deduplicated signatures MUST be >= threshold; (d) threshold MUST equal the current `recovery_policy.device_quorum.threshold` (or equivalent published quorum policy) at issued_at — a smaller threshold supplied by the issuer MUST be rejected as `failed_precondition` reason=`cross_signing_reset_quorum_below_policy`. Receivers MUST reject the reset if any of (a)-(d) fails.

signatures.description: minItems=1 is the schema floor only; reducer-side verification requires deduplicated valid signatures count >= threshold per description rule (c).

threshold.description: The quorum threshold the issuer claims to satisfy. MUST equal the principal's currently published recovery_policy device-quorum threshold; receivers MUST cross-check (see description rule (d)).

did_url.description: DID URL with required key fragment. Fragment characters constrained to RFC 3986 unreserved + `:` for stable key ids. DID method-name normalized to lowercase per W3C DID 1.0.

principal_signing_proof.description: Principal-control-key proof. The schema only encodes wire shape; key-class verification is normative in zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §14.4. `verification_method` MUST be a principal-grade DID-control verification method (zh/identity/key-management.md §3.2 — e.g. `did:webvh:...#ck_principal_signing_v1` or the DID method's equivalent control key), and MUST NOT be the self_signing_key or user_signing_key being retired by this reset.

verification_method.description: Principal-grade control-key verification method. MUST NOT reference the SSK/USK being reset (§14.4 rule (a)).

recovery_unlock_proof.description: Recovery-key unlock proof. The cryptographic strength comes entirely from `signature` — possession of the recovery private key is proven by verifying `signature` over the §14.1 canonical input under the public key bound to `recovery_secret_ref` in the DID Document recovery section / `recovery_policy`. `unlock_commitment` is a wire-integrity / debug binding only: it is a deterministic public hash that the receiver re-computes from material already in the event. See zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §14.4: (a) recovery_secret_ref MUST resolve to a recovery key entry that was authoritative at issued_at; (b) signature MUST verify against that entry's public key; (c) unlock_commitment MUST equal SHA-256(utf8('ck-cross-signing-reset-unlock-binding-v1\n') || recovery_secret_ref || unlock_binding_input_bytes), where unlock_binding_input_bytes is the §14.1 canonical input with proof_body excluding both signature fields and unlock_commitment. Receivers MUST reject the reset if any of (a)-(c) fails.

recovery_secret_ref.description: Stable identifier of the recovery key entry inside the principal's DID Document recovery section or `recovery_policy` (e.g. `did:webvh:...#recovery-1` or a recovery share id). MUST match an entry that was authoritative at issued_at.

recovery_session_id.description: Recovery session id from the §15 device recovery state machine (step 2). Carried inside the recovery_unlock proof body so it enters the §14.1 canonical transcript via proof_body, giving the proof a self-contained freshness binding that does not depend on external recovery state. Receivers MUST reject a recovery_unlock reset whose recovery_session_id does not match an active recovery session for principal_id at issued_at. See zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §14.1 / §15.

unlock_commitment.description: Deterministic wire-integrity hash bound to (recovery_secret_ref, reset content). Receiver-computable from public material; does NOT prove possession of the recovery secret — `signature` does. See §14.4 rule (c) for the exact derivation and the self-reference exclusion.

attestation_ref.description: Optional attestation object for service_did. If present, receivers MUST resolve it in the same trust_domain as the reset payload and reject cross-domain attestations as cross_signing_reset_recovery_service_attestation_domain_mismatch.

schemas/cross-signing-reset.schema.json.description: Payload content for ck.cross_signing.reset (schema_id ck.schema.cross_signing_reset.v1). High-risk operation that retires the current (SSK, USK) generation and requires one of four kinds of proof — see device-lifecycle.md §14. A successor ck.cross_signing.publish MUST follow within 24h.

new_generation.description: Generation that the successor ck.cross_signing.publish will use; MUST equal previous_generation + 1.

previous_generation.description: The generation being retired; MUST equal the currently accepted publish generation.

reset_event_id.description: Typed event_id of the Event Envelope carrying this reset payload. MUST equal the enclosing Event.event_id. Binding it into proof transcript prevents wrapping the same proof bytes into a different Event shell. Mismatch MUST be rejected as reset_event_id_mismatch.

trust_domain.description: Deployment-scope trust domain identifier. Enters every proof's canonical transcript so the same proof bytes cannot be replayed from deployment A into deployment B (different trust_domain → different transcript → signature verification fails as invalid_signature). Receivers MUST check this matches their own trust_domain before doing any signature work, returning cross_domain_replay_rejected otherwise. See zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §14.1 and zh/identity/identity-did.md §3.6.

schemas/cross-signing-reset.schema.json.title: Cokret Cross-Signing Reset

schemas/cursor.schema.json.description:
Single opaque cursor type. Used as both stream continuation token (incremental sync, list pagination — 'after', 'before', 'prev_cursor', 'next_cursor') and barrier token (read-your-writes wait — 'X-Cokret-Wait-For'). Wire form is always ck:cursor:<base64url(canonical_json)>. Clients MUST treat the wire form as opaque; only the issuing server reads the inner structure.

Integrity contract (normative, see client-sync.md §12 and encoding.md §10): v1 core uses the stateful opaque-handle form only — body is {v, purpose, t, x, h} where 'h' is an unguessable server-side handle that the issuing server resolves to the bound (principal_id, device_id, service_id, filter_digest, purpose, positions, target?, expiry) tuple. Server-side handle lookup IS the integrity check; there is no inline transcript binding to verify on the client side. Servers MUST reject unknown / expired / cross-binding handles with cursor_integrity_invalid.

^_[A-Za-z0-9_]*$.description: Server-private auxiliary fields (e.g. `_compress` / `_kid` flags). Names MUST start with underscore. In v1 core there is no `_mac` / `_sig` integrity field — handle lookup IS the integrity check — so the underscore namespace is private to the issuing server. `_mac` and `_sig` themselves are explicitly excluded by the top-level `not` clause: a cursor body carrying either MUST be rejected (encoding.md §8.3).

h.description: Server-side opaque handle. The issuing server MUST bind this handle to (principal_id, device_id, service_id, filter_digest, purpose, positions, target?, expiry) and MUST be able to revoke it. The handle MUST be unguessable (≥ 128 bits entropy after base64url decoding); minLength=22 enforces that floor mechanically (base64url packs 6 bits per character so 128/6 ≈ 21.33 → at least 22 chars of the [A-Za-z0-9_-] alphabet). Servers MUST reject any unknown / expired / cross-binding handle with `cursor_integrity_invalid`. Handle lookup IS the integrity check — there is no MAC or signature to verify inline. This is the moral equivalent of Matrix `next_batch` / MSC4186 `pos` and satisfies the integrity contract without crypto. Servers SHOULD keep the handle → binding map durable across process restarts (see client-sync.md §12.1): a memory-only table is still integrity-correct (unknown handles fail closed) but turns every restart into a fleet-wide forced full resync. For production-grade deployment profiles (small_team / organization / high_security_organization / sovereign_deployment / sovereign_enclave / isolated_sovereign_network) this durability plus TTL GC is a MUST per client-sync.md §12.1; only personal_node keeps it at SHOULD.

purpose.description: Cursor purpose. 'stream' = continuation cursor for incremental sync / list pagination. Used as 'after' on /account/subscribe, 'before' / 'after' on ck.self.events.query and ck.peer.events.query (including its service-to-service federation pull form GET /_cokret/peer/events?before=<cursor>), and as response 'prev_cursor' (older direction) / 'next_cursor' (newer direction). prev_cursor / next_cursor carry absolute directional meaning regardless of how the request was issued — see api-conventions.md §7.0. 'barrier' = read-your-writes / wait-for-event cursor (use in X-Cokret-Wait-For header to block until local frontier covers target.event_id). The handle binding (resolved server-side) carries positions for 'stream' or target for 'barrier'; the wire body does not.

x.description: Expiration timestamp (Unix ms). MUST be in the future when the cursor is issued. TTL upper bounds (cursor lifetime = x - t_ms): barrier cursors MUST have TTL ≤ 3,600,000 ms (1 hour); stream cursors MUST have TTL ≤ 604,800,000 ms (7 days). Issuing a cursor exceeding these caps is a producer error; receivers MUST reject with `invalid_param`. Reasoning: barrier cursors only gate read-your-writes wait latency and become meaningless once the global frontier has long covered the target event. Stream cursors lose causal alignment value over weeks of activity.

schemas/cursor.schema.json.title: Cokret Cursor

schemas/delivery-binding-stale.schema.js.description: Canonical error body for the delivery_binding_stale federation signal. A receiver that has accepted a member delivery-binding rebind handover returns this when a sender still delivers under the pre-handover binding. Carries new_recipient_service_did, handover_frontier, and a verifiable handover_proof binding the accepted ck.member.state{membership=join} rebind Move. High-risk redirect: senders MUST cross-verify handover_frontier via a non-destination witness and validate handover_proof (reachability, seal-frontier finalization, allowed_recipient_services membership, trust-domain guard) before following. See zh/sync/federation.md §4.1 and registry/error-code-registry.json (delivery_binding_stale / delivery_binding_handover_proof_invalid).

handover_frontier.description: Handover frontier F that triggered the rebind. MUST equal handover_proof.frontier.

handover_proof.description: Verifiable proof binding the accepted ck.member.state{membership=join} rebind Move that produced the new binding.

actor_id.description: Rebind target principal; MUST equal target_principal_id.

witness.description: Event digest / state witness / inclusion proof of the rebind Move. Sender MUST verify reachability in the Realm Event graph and policy, and that the Move is seal-frontier finalized.

new_recipient_service_did.description: Target Principal Server service DID after rebind. MUST be within the current effective allowed_recipient_services / delivery binding policy allow set.

schemas/delivery-binding-stale.schema.js.title: Cokret Delivery Binding Stale Error Body

challenge_signature.description: Fresh requesting-device proof bound to pairing_code, new_device_pubkey, gate_audience, and request_canonical_digest; later submitted to ck.gate.account.device_pair.

device_metadata.description: User-facing requesting-device hints. Receivers MUST treat this as display metadata and bind the parts shown to the user into the verification transcript.

gate_audience.description: Auth Server audience/origin expected to consume the paired proof.

new_device_pubkey.description: Public key material for the requesting device when purpose=same_principal_device_authorization. The kid SHOULD equal the requesting device id and the object is later consumed by ck.gate.account.device_pair.

pairing_code.description: Short user-visible code bound into a same-principal device authorization transcript.

purpose.description: Optional verification purpose. Omitted means generic device key verification. same_principal_device_authorization is used when a fresh device asks already authorized devices of the same principal to approve device authorization.

request_canonical_digest.description: Digest of the canonical request material bound into the pairing proof.

secret_request_content.description: ck.secret.request to-device content (device-lifecycle.md §10.7). A newly authorized device asks an existing authorized device to hand over an account-scope secret over HPKE. Carries no secret material itself.

from_device.description: Requesting (new) device; MUST equal envelope sender_device_id.

recipient_hpke_public_key.description: base64url X25519 HPKE public key the requesting device controls and the responder seals to. SHOULD be the device hpke_key or the ephemeral key already established by the bound SAS verification transcript.

request_id.description: Caller-generated random correlation id; MUST NOT be reused after the request is answered or cancelled.

secret_id.description: Opaque identifier of the requested secret, e.g. yougen_mls_account_secret.

secret_send_content.description: ck.secret.send to-device content (device-lifecycle.md §10.7). The existing authorized device returns the requested secret HPKE-sealed to the requester's recipient_hpke_public_key. The plaintext is never visible to the queue service.

ciphertext.description: base64url HPKE AEAD ciphertext over the secret plaintext. The HPKE AAD is the RFC 8785 JCS canonical JSON of {kind, sender_principal_id, sender_device_id, recipient_principal_id, recipient_device_id, expires_at_unix} where expires_at_unix is expires_at normalized to integer Unix seconds (device-lifecycle.md §10.7); both sides reconstruct it from the DeviceMessageEnvelope. Freshness for sent_at (server-assigned) is bound by the one-time request_id authenticated inside the sealed plaintext.

from_device.description: Authorizing (existing) device; MUST equal envelope sender_device_id and MUST be a non-revoked device of the recipient principal.

request_id.description: Correlates to the pending ck.secret.request; MUST equal the request_id authenticated inside the sealed plaintext. Receivers MUST drop sends that do not match a locally pending request_id.

device_proof.description: Optional per-device transport proof block. Schema-open extension point keyed by device-lifecycle.md §5.2 cross-signing binding (typical sub-fields: cross_signing_binding, sender_device_key_fingerprint, signature_over_content_digest). MUST NOT replace MLS authentication of the enclosing envelope; included only when an additional out-of-band per-device transport binding is required (e.g. SAS verification, dehydrated-device proofs). Receivers MUST treat unknown sub-fields as opaque and MUST NOT trust device_proof in isolation.

recipient_principal_id.description: Recipient Principal DID. Same naming rationale as sender_principal_id — device messages are not Realm-scoped, so Actor identity is not used. Pair with recipient_device_id for targeted device delivery.

sender_principal_id.description: Sender Principal DID. Intentionally NOT named sender_actor_id: device messages are out-of-band per-device transport envelopes that travel principal-to-principal outside any Realm context, so the Realm-scoped Actor identity used by message.schema.json / event-payload.schema.json does not apply here. Pair with sender_device_id for cross-signing binding.

unsigned.description: Optional non-authenticated metadata block (transport-layer hints only). Receivers MUST NOT trust any field here for authorization, ordering, or cryptographic verification. Typical sub-fields: progress (delivery progress hint), error_context (transport-layer error diagnostics), retry_after_ms. By convention this block is excluded from the signed transcript of the enclosing transport envelope and is dropped on persist.

schemas/did-continuity-proof.schema.json.description: Payload profile for ck.did.proof continuity transitions, including cross-method did:web -> did:webvh upgrades.

audience.description: Optional list of intended verifier scopes (e.g. Realm IDs, registry service DIDs, or trust-domain identifiers) that this continuity proof is bound to. When present, verifiers outside the listed audiences MUST reject the proof to prevent cross-protocol / cross-Realm replay of an account migration claim. When absent, the proof is broadcast-style and verifiers fall back to checking signature_chain + transfer_evidence only. See zh/identity/identity-did.md §4.2.

payload_digest.description: Hash of utf8('ck-did-continuity-proof-v1\n') || canonical_json(proof object with signature_chain[].signature omitted).

principal_id.description: DID of the principal that produced this signature-chain link. The signing key is named by verification_method; this is the responsibility subject.

verification_method.description: DID URL of the signing key. Fragment is REQUIRED. DID method-name normalized to lowercase per W3C DID 1.0.

schemas/did-continuity-proof.schema.json.title: Cokret DID Continuity Proof

head_event_digest.description: Self digest of this entry: canonical_digest of the entry with `proofs` and `head_event_digest` removed (canonical JSON per encoding.md §2, wire hash form per §3.1). The next accepted entry's prev_event_digest and identity receipts both reference this value. Normative byte-level definition: zh/sync/service-surface.md §3.1.3.

operation.description: Normalized operation kind. The DID method-specific raw operation object is carried in operation_body; this field is the reducer/verifier discriminator.

operation_body.description: DID method-specific raw operation object. This is not a generic JSON Patch; validation dispatches by DID method and operation kind.

prev_event_digest.description: Hash of the previous accepted key-log entry. Required for seq>0 and forbidden for seq=0.

proofs.description: Controller proofs over this entry. payload_digest = canonical_digest(entry without `proofs`); the detached JWS signs the canonical binding object {payload_digest, did, verification_method, created_at, domain?, audience?} defined in zh/sync/service-surface.md §3.1.3. verification_method MUST be a controller key authorized for this operation at the previous accepted entry's state; the registry host MUST NOT substitute its own key.

seq.description: Monotonic DID method log sequence for this DID. seq=0 is the inception entry and MUST NOT carry prev_event_digest; every seq>0 entry MUST carry prev_event_digest equal to the previous accepted entry's head_event_digest.

controller_subject.description: Controller principal DID resolved from controller_handle and verified against the selector claim.

subject.description: Native personal agent principal DID selected by (controller_subject, agent_slug).

controller_handle.description: Canonical controller handle string without the @ sigil.

invite_consent_handoff_stub.description: Minimal invite/consent handoff stub allowed beside PSI match bits. It declares state or next-step guidance only; it MUST NOT carry a contact request token, reachability proof, profile, membership, or read grant.

state_digest.description: If present, MUST be salted per requester/session or replaced by an audience-bound opaque token per consent-model.md §6.2.

schemas/directory-operations.schema.json.description: Closed request/response DTOs for Directory discovery search, resolve, private contact discovery, handle lookup, agent selector lookup, and push webhook registration operations.
schemas/directory-operations.schema.json.title: Cokret Directory Operation DTOs

schemas/draft-sync.schema.json.description: Encrypted account-data plaintext shape for ck.profile.draft_sync.v1.
schemas/draft-sync.schema.json.title: Cokret Draft Sync Account Data

aad_visibility_event_id.description: Normative discriminator for event id visibility in aad. hidden forbids aad.event_id and aad.event_ref_digest; routing_digest requires aad.event_ref_digest and forbids aad.event_id; opaque_id requires aad.event_id and forbids aad.event_ref_digest.

key_ref.description: MLS group binding hints. Closed object: privacy-sensitive AAD must not be smuggled through here. Forbidden in v1: ratchet_tree, leaf_node, group_info (these MUST NOT be replicated per-message).

group_state_ref.description: v1 MLS group state lookup hint. MUST point to accepted ck.mls.genesis / winning ck.mls.commit / equivalent group state proof. Does NOT replace MLS transcript verification. See encryption-and-audit.md §4. Ratchet tree material MUST NOT be carried in the per-message envelope; group state changes flow through ck.mls.genesis / Welcome / Commit events.

oneOf.description: Reference to accepted ck.mls.genesis / winning ck.mls.commit event.

call_id.description: Typed call/session identifier (ck:call:<uuidv7>) scoped to the Realm. Unified with ice-config-response and media-operations so cross-channel join cross-checks key on the same form.

seq.description: Monotonic per-(realm_id, call_id, actor_id, device_id) sequence. Receivers MUST reject replay or rollback.

schemas/ephemeral-envelope.schema.json.description: Wire shape for broadcast ephemeral signals — ck.presence, ck.typing, ck.receipt.read, ck.call.signal. These signals have wire_scope=ephemeral_event in event-kind-registry.json: they MUST NOT carry CBA reducer fields, MUST NOT advance Seal coverage, governance state_root or actor_seq, MUST NOT enter reducer state, and MUST NOT be submitted via ck.events.submit. They are carried on dedicated ephemeral channels (sync subscribe live stream, presence/typing fanout, call signaling channel) and are dropped at TTL. Point-to-point to-device signals (ck.key.verification.*) use device-message.schema.json instead — they have a sender+recipient pair and do not match this broadcast shape. See zh/sync/operations-sync.md §2.3 (wire-scope reject rule) and zh/crypto-media/webrtc-signaling.md §5 (ephemeral channel transport).

actor_id.description: Signaling actor. MUST be a member of the Realm (ck.member.state cell join != ban/leave/remove at receive time) for the broadcast to be admitted by other clients; receivers drop signals from non-members without surfacing them.

device_id.description: Originating device. Optional but RECOMMENDED so receivers can dedupe per-device typing/presence signals.

expires_at.description: Server / client MUST drop the signal at or after this time. Per-kind soft caps (recommended): presence ≤ 60s, typing ≤ 15s, receipt.read ≤ 30s, call.signal ≤ 30s. Signals with expires_at > sent_at + 5 minutes MUST be dropped by receivers (`invalid_param`).

kind.description: Ephemeral signal kind. MUST be one of the four broadcast ephemeral kinds; ck.key.verification.* point-to-point flows MUST use device-message.schema.json instead.

payload.description: Kind-specific signal payload. Schema per kind is defined by the producing module (e.g. zh/crypto-media/webrtc-signaling.md for ck.call.signal, zh/discovery/read-receipts.md for ck.receipt.read). Payload MUST NOT carry mutable governance state — that belongs in a durable event.

proof.description: Optional detached signature over canonical envelope bytes (per RFC 8785 JCS, excluding `proof` itself). Required for ck.call.signal; RECOMMENDED for ck.receipt.read so receivers can verify origin without trusting relay. presence / typing MAY omit proof for cost reasons; receivers MUST NOT promote unsigned signals to durable state.

realm_id.description: Realm whose ephemeral channel carries this signal. Authorization to broadcast a signal on a Realm channel is governed by the same membership / capability rules as the corresponding durable kinds.

sent_at.description: Wall-clock send time. Diagnostic only — ephemeral signals do not participate in HLC ordering.

schemas/ephemeral-envelope.schema.json.title: Cokret Ephemeral Broadcast Envelope

event_digest.description: Digest of the original Event envelope or durable object metadata, when the erased subject was event-backed.

retained_digests.description: Event digest / object payload digests retained for signature verification. MUST NOT be a bare digest of erased low-entropy plaintext.

schemas/erasure-receipt.schema.json.description: Signed attestation that an issuer completed, partially completed, or blocked a hard-erasure request within a declared storage boundary. It proves the issuer's deletion action and retained verification stub, not disappearance of independent third-party copies.

erasure_scope.description: Boundary in which deletion was attempted. This MUST be narrow enough for an auditor to tell which service/storage class made the claim.

fanout_status.description: Cross-Principal-Server erasure receipt fanout aggregate status tracked by the issuing server (models/realm-and-space.md §2.6.2). 'pending' = peers still within erasure_propagation_window_ms and not all acknowledged; 'complete' = every peer that ever held this Realm's content returned a receipt; 'incomplete' = at least one peer failed to acknowledge within erasure_propagation_window_ms. The issuing server MUST surface 'incomplete' to audit/UI and MUST NOT silently swallow it. Absent on receipts that do not drive fanout tracking.
