For 'wide synthesis + narrow discussion' scenarios use two Flows linked by a confidential_discussion_of Relation (circle.md §7.2).

stage.description: Optional Flow business-progression stage. Orthogonal to top-level 'state' (physical lifecycle): archive does NOT change stage; stage=done does NOT auto-archive. ck.flow.create MAY omit stage; when present it must be one of the protocol-level enum values and has no protocol-level default. The only wire path that mutates stage after creation is the dedicated ck.flow.stage.set event; ck.flow.update patches on stage / stage_changed_at MUST be rejected (schema_violation, single-source). Stage transitions intentionally do NOT carry a reason / note field — the ck.flow.stage.set event log is the audit source, and human-readable explanations belong in a Message on the discussion track that references the event. A per-Realm workflow profile MAY narrow which transitions are legal beyond the core reducer hard invariants (terminal state freeze, non-active reject) defined in models/common-fields.md §5.3.3. See models/flow-and-message.md §3.2 for full semantics and models/common-fields.md §5.3 for the protocol-level enum / bucket mapping.

stage_changed_at.description: Reducer-derived timestamp of the most recent stage transition. MUST NOT appear without stage. MUST be ignored when present on wire; reducer overwrites with the triggering ck.flow.stage.set event's created_at. Same-value self-transitions (stage value unchanged) MUST NOT update this field.

state.description: Flow lifecycle state. 'active' is the default. Reducer enforces transitions per common-fields.md §5.1: ck.flow.archive MUST come from 'active' (else failed_precondition reason=flow_not_active); ck.flow.restore MUST come from 'archived' (else flow_not_archived); terminal state is reached only via a ck.redaction event targeting the flow (MUST come from {'active','archived'} else flow_already_terminal). Same-state self-transitions MUST fail. 'redacted' is the irreversible terminal.

state_changed_at.description: Reducer-derived timestamp of the most recent state transition. MUST be set when state != 'active'; MUST be the created_at of the corresponding ck.flow.archive / ck.flow.restore / ck.redaction Event. Aligns with Space.state_changed_at and the common-fields rule in models/common-fields.md §3.

tracks.description: Active Flow tracks, keyed by track name. Tracks are pure section pointers (synthesis vs discussion timeline) — they do NOT carry independent membership / permissions / history visibility / E2EE. The entire Flow shares a single effective scope determined by Flow.scope_circle_id (see models/circle.md); there is no per-track security boundary. At most one track entry may explicitly set is_primary=true; when none does, the reducer derives the primary track by the deterministic rules in models/flow-and-message.md §4.5. The map MUST contain at least one entry; track names are validated by propertyNames.

schemas/grant-constraint.schema.json.$comment: Property ordering is grouped by constraint family to match capabilities.md §6 (the human-readable family map): discriminator/meta, then temporal, field_access, type_restriction, scope_limitation, delegation_control, quota, claim_based, confidentiality, then the moderation cache-invalidation hint. Canonical JSON re-sorts keys lexicographically so this ordering is presentation-only and does not affect the wire (see C13-07).

allOf.$comment: constraint-schema.md §2.2 / §2.3: claim_based, confidentiality and quota families have NO valid no-subtype form — every row in the §2.3 evaluation_class table carries a subtype (claim/approval/accountability; encryption/visibility; rate/resource). Without this gate a {"constraint_type":"claim_based","effect":"allow"} with no subtype passes schema validation, letting weak implementations cache an external (claim-revocation) constraint on the grant_local fast path (see C05-03 fail-open). temporal is intentionally excluded: a temporal constraint with no subtype is the valid ordinary time-window form.

allowed_circle_ids.description: Limits Circle-scoped capability actions to the listed Circle ids. Used by ck.circle.manage / ck.circle.member.manage style grants; unconstrained Realm-wide Circle management grants are not a normal permission shape.

allowed_data_classes.description: Data classification labels this grant may read, export, transform, or send to external endpoints.

allowed_endpoints.description: Allowed outbound endpoint origins or deployment-approved endpoint patterns for applet / agent / connector operations.

allowed_space_kinds.description: Allowed Space kinds (e.g. 'board', 'list', or profile-registered kinds like 'swimlane', 'calendar_bucket'). Reducer/profile MUST validate kind value.

applies_to_actions.description: Optional restriction of a temporal constraint to specific capability actions (e.g. ['ck.message.revise.own', 'ck.message.redact.own']).

blob_presign_max_ttl_seconds.description: Maximum TTL, in seconds, that this grant permits for ck.blob.presign. The service must clamp requested max_age_seconds to the smaller of this value and deployment policy.

blob_presign_scope.description: Scope limiter for ck.self.blob.presign grants: allowed purposes plus optional blob/realm restrictions.

condition.description: Conditional predicate for field_access and similar constraints. The `kind` value is a registered named condition from constraint-schema.md §4.1; unknown kinds MUST fail closed. Implementations MUST NOT introduce ad hoc string DSL predicates.

constraint_id.description: Optional stable identifier of this constraint within the grant; used for diagnostics and overrides.

constraint_type.description: Constraint family discriminator. v1 collapses what were 15 types into 8 by absorbing narrowly-scoped types into their conceptual parent: edit_window → temporal; container_move → scope_limitation; rate_limiting + resource_limit → quota; approval_workflow + accountability + device_session → claim_based (with subtype); encryption_requirement + visibility_control → confidentiality (with subtype). Use the optional 'subtype' field to indicate the original specialization where evaluation logic differs.

depends_on_moderation_state.description: Cache-invalidation hint: when true, this grant's authorization decisions depend on the ck.component.moderation_state.v1 cell (see policy-server.md §7.1 and capabilities.md §18.1) and the grant's cache entry MUST be invalidated when that cell changes. Default false: ordinary grants (ck.flow.update / ck.message.create / org membership grants) do NOT take a cache hit on every moderation decision. v1 capabilities.md §18.1 lists three conditions where MUST be explicitly true (moderator-role grants, condition-selector subjects referencing moderation state, constraints referencing moderation queue / cell). Schema-side enforcement of condition (2) is in capability-grant.schema.json via if/then on actions[]; conditions (1) and (3) are reducer-side lint. Cache invalidation hint outside the eight constraint families; it does not participate in allow/deny evaluation and is documented in capabilities.md §6 / constraint-schema.md.

evaluation_class.description: Cacheability/dependency hint for the authorization evaluator. stateless = pure function of (constraint, op, now); grant_local = depends on the grant object only; realm_state = depends on Realm frontier (membership, policy_version, etc.); external = depends on data outside the Realm causal frontier (claim revocation status, rate-limit history counts, async approval). Each constraint_type has a canonical evaluation_class declared in constraint-schema.md §2.3; implementations MAY tighten (e.g. grant_local → stateless) but MUST NOT loosen (e.g. external as stateless). Auth evaluators SHOULD use this hint to gate fast-path caching.

expires_after.description: ISO 8601 duration; used by approval_workflow constraint instead of expires_after_ms.

max_artifact_bytes.description: Maximum artifact size in bytes for applet / agent / export operations.

recurrence.description: Recurrence rule for temporal constraints. Used by constraint-schema.md §3.1.

requires_claims.description: Conditional claim requirements. resource-selector-grammar.md §3.3 caps this array at 32 entries as a normative DoS guard; the schema enforces maxItems:32 so condition-selector grants cannot smuggle in unbounded claim objects.

subject_matches_actor.description: If true, the credential subject DID MUST match the actor DID.

value_constraints.description: Per-field equality / membership constraints on credential claims.

subtype.description: Optional discriminator within a constraint_type. Standard values: claim_based.{claim,approval,accountability,device_session}; quota.{rate,resource}; confidentiality.{encryption,visibility}; temporal.{window,edit_window,redact_window,session}. Implementations MAY require subtype for these families and fail closed on unknown values.

schemas/grant-constraint.schema.json.title: Cokret Grant Constraint

audience.description: Audience binding for the claim. For handle claims used to build a Realm delivery_binding, audience is the target Realm ID, the inviting service DID, or another verifier domain the proofs explicitly bind to. Verifier MUST reject claims whose audience does not match the current invocation context.

claim_kind.description: Protocol-level kind of holder/principal handle claim. v1 intentionally does not allow the earlier draft service_handle value: service-readable names or resource labels need their own service/resource schema, while organization-assigned user/principal handles use organization_handle.

claim_scope.description: Optional claim_scope such as organization_id, realm_id, purpose, or allowed operations.

handle.description: Cokret canonical handle string: <localpart>:<domain>. The @ mention sigil and acct: alias are not part of this field. This pattern is intentionally ASCII-only: it validates the post-IDNA canonical form, where <domain> is the A-label (punycode, xn-- prefix) and <localpart> is the lowercase restricted-ASCII canonical form. Unicode NFC normalization and UTS#39 confusable / script-mixing homograph detection (see zh/identity/identity-handles.md §17) MUST be applied to the U-label BEFORE IDNA conversion; they are not (and cannot be) re-enforced by this ASCII pattern.

handle_aliases.description: Interop aliases such as RFC 7565 acct:. Aliases are never canonical; verifiers MUST normalize to handle before cache lookup, proof comparison, or delivery_binding construction.

issuer_service_did.description: Service DID that signed, served, or vouched for this handle claim when distinct from issuer.

member_delivery_binding.description: Single source for the Principal Server service DID and delivery parameters this handle claim offers to the membership builder. Top-level delivery shortcuts are forbidden; use member_delivery_binding.recipient_service_did, member_delivery_binding.service_acceptance_ref, and member_delivery_binding.policy_event_ref.

schema.description: Canonical schema discriminator. Aligned with schema-registry.json; lets validators / contract-catalog consumers disambiguate this claim from other DID-bearing envelopes.

subject.description: Holder/principal DID for a user/principal handle. This is the stable DID the handle resolves to; it is not a Realm actor_id, server-local account_id, administrative identifier, service DID, or generic resource id.

visibility.description: Default disclosure boundary for this handle claim.

credential.description: TURN ephemeral credential password (HMAC-SHA256 of username with per-tenant turn shared secret in REST-style).

urls.description: STUN/TURN server URL(s). Schemes: stun:, stuns:, turn:, turns:.

username.description: TURN ephemeral credential username. v1: <expiry-unix>:<per-call-pseudonym>. MUST NOT contain principal DID, handle, email, or any cross-call stable identifier.

kid.description: Verification method id, typically <media_service_did>#<key-id>. Bare DID is accepted (resolves to the controller's current key); DID URLs with key fragment are RECOMMENDED. Pattern normalized to canonical DID form; the previous `(#.+)?$` was redundant under greedy `[^\s]+`.

sig.description: base64url-encoded detached signature over canonical response bytes.

schemas/ice-config-response.schema.json.description: Result shape for the WebRTC media service ICE config endpoint. Used by ck.profile.webrtc_media.v1; see crypto-media/webrtc-signaling.md §4.

actor_id.description: Actor that may use this ICE configuration. Bound into the signature.

bucket_seconds.description: TURN pseudonym bucket size in seconds. v1 fixes the default and interoperable value at 300s; clients SHOULD refresh before crossing the next bucket.

call_id.description: Echo of the request call id. Bound into the signature to prevent cross-call replay.

device_id.description: Device that may use this ICE configuration. Bound into the signature.

expires_at.description: Convenience field equal to issued_at + ttl_seconds. MUST match within signature validation.

force_turn.description: When true, clients MUST disable host/srflx ICE candidates and only relay through TURN. Used by high-privacy Realms to prevent IP leakage.

ice_servers.description: STUN / TURN server entries the client may use during this call.

issued_at.description: Server-issued timestamp (RFC 3339 UTC). Bound into the ICE config signature.

issued_at_bucket.description: Coarse UTC bucket start used for TURN pseudonym derivation. MUST equal floor(issued_at / bucket_seconds) * bucket_seconds. Bound into the signature so TURN usernames cannot be correlated across buckets by rewriting metadata.

next_retry_at.description: Set when the response is a soft failure (e.g. turn_credential_expired). Clients MUST NOT retry before this time.

realm_id.description: Echo of the request Realm id. Bound into the signature to prevent cross-Realm replay.

refresh_lead_seconds.description: Minimum lead time before ttl expiry at which the client SHOULD initiate refresh. refresh_lead_seconds MUST be strictly less than ttl_seconds (servers MUST NOT issue refresh_lead_seconds >= ttl_seconds, otherwise the client would judge the credential stale at issuance and storm refresh). Defaults SHOULD be ttl_seconds / 4. The recommended floor (60s) applies only when ttl_seconds is large enough that floor < ttl_seconds still holds; for small ttl (e.g. the 60s minimum) the server MUST shrink refresh_lead_seconds below ttl_seconds (see webrtc-signaling.md §4.2). Required so all clients refresh at consistent cadence and servers can plan secret rotation grace windows.

signature.description: Detached signature by the media service DID over the canonical bytes of this response (excluding `signature`).

ttl_seconds.description: Validity window for the issued credentials in seconds. Clients MUST refresh before this expires; servers SHOULD pick a value <= 1 hour for normal calls.

schemas/ice-config-response.schema.json.title: Cokret Media ICE Config Result

schemas/identity-link.schema.json.description: Encrypted application-message or MLS private-extension payload that binds a Realm-scoped pairwise DID to the real principal DID for ck.profile.mls.minimal_metadata_realm.v1. The binding is scoped to both realm_id and trust_domain so the same pairwise mapping cannot be replayed across deployments. This object is never written to public Realm history unless a separate disclosure policy explicitly permits it.

flow_id.description: Optional application-message context marker for the Flow carrying the identity link. It does not create independent membership or key scope; key scope is determined by effective_scope.

mls_group_id.description: Optional MLS group identifier (base64url RFC 9420 GroupID) for diagnostic / cross-implementation correlation. NOT used by the reducer for authorization — authoritative MLS group state lives in ck.mls.genesis / ck.mls.commit events. Provided here so audit projections can quickly correlate an identity-link with its MLS group without replaying the full epoch chain.

pairwise_did.description: Realm-scoped pairwise DID used in Event.actor_id and MLS leaf credential. The v1 boundary is the Realm, not a Matrix-style Room.

principal_id.description: Real principal DID that controls or has disclosed the pairwise DID.

payload_digest.description: Hash of canonical input bytes: utf8('ck-identity-link-v1\n') || canonical_json(identity-link object with proof.signature omitted). The signed object includes trust_domain.

verification_method.description: DID URL of a key controlled by principal_id or by a disclosure proof accepted by Realm policy. Fragment is REQUIRED (this is a DID URL, not a bare DID). DID method-name normalized to lowercase per W3C DID 1.0.

track_name.description: Optional display-track context marker for application routing. Track names do not create independent membership, policy, or MLS key scope.

trust_domain.description: Deployment-scope trust domain. Receiver MUST require this value to match the current Realm / service trust_domain before accepting a pairwise DID -> principal DID mapping.

schemas/identity-link.schema.json.title: Cokret Minimal-Metadata Identity Link

audience.description: Optional audience binding (verifier DID, service DID, or domain). When present, verifiers MUST reject the receipt outside that audience context to prevent cross-protocol reuse.

schema.description: Canonical schema discriminator. Aligned with schema-registry.json; lets validators distinguish identity registry receipts from other receipt envelopes (e.g. audit-ryw-receipt, event-batch-receipt).

witness_role.description: Issuer's role in the DID registry consensus group. Required so verifiers can apply role-specific freshness / quorum rules; an absent role would force the verifier to guess writer vs replica semantics.

payload_digest.description: Hash of canonical InclusionList bytes with signature omitted.

schemas/inclusion-list.schema.json.description: FOCIL-style control-plane inclusion list. A non-proposer notary signer lists pending Control Move digests that passed its local verification; the next Seal MUST include, signed-reject, or prove batch pre-state verification failure for every listed digest, otherwise receivers MUST reject that Seal (authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 7.3). single_did notary profiles cannot provide this mechanism. The list is an accountability object, not a Seal: it never advances governance state by itself.

event_digests.description: Canonical ascending list of pending Control Move event digests that passed the issuer's local verification and hold a valid receipt.

expiry_seal_count.description: Number of subsequent Seals within which the obligation must be discharged. Default deployment value is 1 (the next Seal).

list_seq.description: Per-signer monotonic inclusion-list sequence. Two different canonical lists from the same signer with the same (realm_id, list_seq) constitute equivocation evidence under the section 7.1 slot rule.

signer_id.description: Notary signer issuing the list. MUST be an eligible non-proposer signer of the Realm's multi-signer notary profile at issue time.

schemas/inclusion-list.schema.json.title: Cokret InclusionList

consent_grant_ref.description: Event ref of the invitee-issued ck.consent.grant (scope invite or any) that authorizes the inviter to send Realm/Flow invites. High-trust evidence: it is material the invitee actively issued to the inviter, equivalent in trust to a locator_ref.

consent_id.description: Optional consent cell id locating the holder consent cell, to speed up receiver verification of the active grant dot.

recipient_service_did.description: Principal Server service DID that accepts invite delivery for subject_id.

recipient_service_type.description: v1 only allows Principal Server invite delivery. Omit by default; if present, the value MUST be principal_server.

subject_id.description: Principal DID of the invite recipient. v1 core defaults principal DIDs to did:webvh; did:web is only valid for principal identity when an explicit deployment profile or resolver policy allows it.

disclosed_outcome.description: Optional graded-disclosure result. Present ONLY when the subject invite_receive_policy disclosure level for this introduction trust tier is 'outcome'. Omitted (opaque) for low-trust tiers and always omitted for blocked_subjects hits. delivered: invite reached the holder surface awaiting acceptance; blocked: rejected by block list or policy; quarantined: held for review.

status.description: Generic receive status. It MUST NOT reveal whether subject_id exists or whether policy quarantined/dropped the invite unless receiver policy explicitly allows disclosure via disclosed_outcome.

recipient_service_type.description: v1 only allows Principal Server invite delivery. Omit by default; if present, the value MUST be principal_server.

schemas/invite-delivery-request.schema.j.description: Private service-to-service request used by an inviter-side Principal Server to deliver a Realm invite to the invitee-side Principal Server. The request carries an explicit invite address and introduction evidence; raw locator tokens are never written into durable Realm events.

invite_event.description: The ck.invite.create EventEnvelope or equivalent accepted event view being delivered.

schemas/invite-delivery-request.schema.j.title: Cokret Invite Delivery Request

disclosure_level.description: opaque: only a generic accepted-for-processing status is returned, indistinguishable across exists/not-exists/policy outcomes. outcome: the real delivered/blocked/quarantined result is disclosed to the inviter.

high_trust.description: Disclosure level for the high-trust introduction tier: consent_grant, locator_ref, shared_realm. Default outcome.

low_trust.description: Disclosure level for the low-trust introduction tier: same_principal_server, explicit_address, and missing/non-compliant evidence. Default opaque.

schemas/invite-receive-policy.schema.jso.description: Subject-private policy used by a Principal Server to decide which invite delivery introduction evidence may notify the holder. This policy is not written into the target Realm durable event log.

allowed_introduction_kinds.description: Allowlist of introduction evidence kinds that may reach holder notification or review.

blocked_subjects.description: Per-subject block list (peer principal DIDs). Invite delivery whose inviter is in this list MUST be dropped, and disclosure MUST be forced to opaque regardless of the disclosure policy, to avoid leaking the block via a side channel.

disclosure.description: Graded disclosure policy. Controls whether the invite delivery outcome reveals a real result (delivered/blocked/quarantined) to the inviter, by introduction trust tier. Omitted means the default: high_trust=outcome, low_trust=opaque.

explicit_address_behavior.description: Default behavior for explicit_address evidence. Deployments SHOULD default to quarantine or drop, not notify.

subject_id.description: Principal DID whose private invite receive policy this object configures. v1 core defaults principal DIDs to did:webvh; did:web is only valid for principal identity when an explicit deployment profile or resolver policy allows it.

unknown_invites.description: Behavior for delivery requests without compliant introduction_evidence.

schemas/invite-receive-policy.schema.jso.title: Cokret Invite Receive Policy

third_party_invite.description: Wire-level 3PID/OOB invite binding. No plaintext email/phone/SMS code is allowed here. `oob_code_kind` distinguishes offline high-entropy token validation from server-side lookup short-code validation.

display_name_hint.description: Non-identifying UI hint only; MUST NOT contain plaintext 3PID.

lookup_table_ref.description: Opaque verification-service lookup table reference for short-code mode. The raw short code MUST NOT appear on wire.

oob_code_kind.description: offline_token means the out-of-band code is itself >=128-bit entropy and validated against token_commitment. lookup means the human-readable code is only an index into a server-private lookup table protected by rate limits and pepper/HMAC storage.

pepper_id.description: Server-private pepper generation identifier for lookup mode; the pepper value itself is never on wire.

token_commitment.description: Salted commitment to a high-entropy invite token. Required for offline_token mode.

token_entropy_bits.description: Required for offline_token mode. Entropy estimate excluding separators.

token_salt_id.description: Opaque handle for the verification service's private salt record. The salt value itself MUST NOT appear on wire.

verification_public_key.description: Ephemeral public key or DID verification method used by the verification service to sign claim results.

introduction_evidence_digest.description: Digest of private invite delivery introduction_evidence. Raw locator tokens and receive-policy state MUST NOT appear in durable Realm events.

invite_delivery_target.description: Public durable target for private invite delivery. invitee is the subject; this object carries only the recipient Principal Server service DID.

updated_by.description: Reducer-derived actor that produced the most recent invite state update.

schemas/key-backup-active-series.schema..description: Signed principal-control record selecting the canonical backup series for one (actor_id, backup_class). This closes the rollback gap when multiple series exist after compromise rotation or migration. Receivers MUST verify this record before choosing a series from list results.

signature.description: base64url signature over canonical_json(record without auth_data.signature).

ssk_generation.description: Accepted ck.cross_signing.publish.generation used to authorize this active-series selection.

frontier_ref.description: Principal control stream frontier under which active_series_id was selected.

previous_series_ids.description: Retained old series used only for read-old-data or erasure transition. MUST NOT be treated as a primary recovery source.

schemas/key-backup-active-series.schema..title: Cokret Key Backup Active Series Record

secret_b64u.description: base64url(no padding) encoded secret bytes. The item_type and metadata define how receivers import the bytes.

schemas/key-backup-plaintext.schema.json.description: Canonical plaintext carried inside ck.schema.key_backup.v1 ciphertext after AEAD/HPKE open. The public envelope contents[] is only an index; this keybag is the import truth source.
schemas/key-backup-plaintext.schema.json.title: Cokret Key Backup Plaintext Keybag

schemas/key-backup-unlock-proof.schema.j.description: Proof presented before a recovery flow downloads or unlocks a key-backup envelope. It binds a backup read/decrypt action to one recovery_session_id, requesting device, backup object, selected series, ciphertext digest, and the proof transcript accepted by the recovery session.

signature.description: base64url signature over canonical_json(unlock proof without auth_data.signature).

verification_method.description: DID URL for either the accepted requesting device key after authorization, or the recovery-session proof key before did_recovery unlock.

challenge.description: Optional echo of the recovery-session challenge; when present it MUST match the session snapshot.

proof_digest.description: Digest of the canonical recovery proof transcript that moved the session to verified.

schemas/key-backup-unlock-proof.schema.j.title: Cokret Key Backup Unlock Proof

then.description: mls_history backups MUST use secret_storage_key or recovery_public_key (key-management.md §7.5.2 / §7.5.3 and device-lifecycle.md §12); passphrase_kdf, threshold_recovery, hardware_wrapped_key, and the removed device_snapshot_secret are rejected. recovery_policy_ref MAY appear as a signed hint, but is not required for mls_history.

did_recovery backups MUST use recovery_public_key (key-management.md §5.0.1 first-backup gate), MUST carry recovery_policy_ref matching the active recovery policy, and MUST cover that field in auth_data.signed_fields. passphrase_kdf and secret_storage_key are forbidden for did_recovery; threshold_recovery and hardware_wrapped_key are recovery policy / proof-layer factors, not key-backup recipient methods.

signature.description: base64url-encoded signature over canonical_json(envelope without auth_data.signature).

signature_algorithm.description: Raw signature algorithm name; MUST be a value generated from an active signature-alg-registry row (Ed25519 / ES256 / ML-DSA-65). EdDSA is the proof_alg label, not a raw signature_algorithm value. ML-DSA-65 is gated behind the PQ migration profile.

signed_fields.description: Names of envelope fields covered by the signature; MUST include backup_id, actor_id, backup_class, backup_version, series_id, series_seq, supersedes, encryption, contents, ciphertext_digest, and when present supersedes_digest, frontier_ref, recovery_policy_ref, and (hardening profile) ssk_generation.

ssk_generation.description: Accepted ck.cross_signing.publish.generation of the self-signing key generation that authorized the device signing this backup. Hardening profiles require receivers to reject envelopes whose generation is below the current accepted generation outside the rotation grace window.

verification_method.description: DID URL identifying the device signing key.

aead_profile.description: Optional AEAD profile id that binds algorithm version, nonce length, tag length, key length, and AAD construction. Receivers that do not support the profile MUST fail closed instead of inferring semantics from name alone.

enc.description: base64url HPKE KEM encapsulated key. Required for recipient_method=recovery_public_key (HPKE base mode, DHKEM(X25519,HKDF-SHA256)); absent for the symmetric methods.

nonce.description: base64url AEAD nonce. Required for the symmetric methods (passphrase_kdf / secret_storage_key). For recipient_method=passphrase_kdf this MUST equal HMAC-SHA256(HKDF(derived_key, info='cokret-key-backup-aead-nonce-v1'), canonical_json({backup_id, actor_id, device_id, backup_class, backup_version, created_at, aead.name, aead.aead_profile?, aead.nonce_salt}))[0:N_AEAD]; receivers recompute and reject mismatches. Absent for recovery_public_key (HPKE derives its nonce internally).

nonce_salt.description: Producer-generated base64url random salt (at least 128 bits before encoding) included in the passphrase_kdf nonce derivation transcript. Required when recipient_method=passphrase_kdf; not secret, signed as envelope metadata, and prevents nonce reuse from duplicate business metadata tuples.

frontier_ref.description: Optional reference to the principal control stream frontier at envelope creation time. Improves rollback detection by sealing the envelope to a verifiable control-stream position.

mixed_secret_storage.description: True only for the personal_node exception where one encrypted backup envelope contains both identity-signing material and E2EE / MLS history material. Non-personal deployment profiles MUST reject this flag. When true and recipient_method=passphrase_kdf, the stricter Argon2id floor below applies.

recovery_policy_ref.description: Required for backup_class=did_recovery and optional as a signed recovery-flow hint for other backup classes. Binds the backup envelope to the active recovery policy version under which it was produced. Receivers MUST compare this tuple to the currently accepted recovery policy before using a did_recovery envelope; when present on other classes, mismatch fails as recovery_policy_mismatch but the field does not replace active-series, frontier, Realm/MLS authorization, or device-state checks. This is intentionally separate from frontier_ref and ssk_generation: it binds the recovery authorization surface, not only the device trust generation or control-stream position.

series_id.description: Stable identifier for one immutable chain of backup envelopes belonging to a single (actor_id, backup_class). A pair MAY have multiple series during compromise rotation or migration; active series selection is outside this envelope and MUST come from the signed active-series record in identity/key-management.md §7.6. Receivers use (actor_id, backup_class, series_id) to detect server-side rollback / withholding within the selected series.

series_seq.description: 0-based, strictly monotonically increasing sequence number within (actor_id, series_id). Genesis envelope of a series MUST set 0. Receivers MUST reject envelopes whose sequence does not strictly exceed the previously accepted sequence in the same series.

supersedes.description: backup_id of the immediate predecessor in the same series_id. MUST be null for series_seq=0; MUST be non-null and reference an existing predecessor for series_seq>0.

supersedes_digest.description: Required when supersedes is non-null. Hash of the canonical_json of the predecessor envelope (excluding auth_data.signature). Receivers MUST recompute and reject mismatches as `series_chain_broken`.

heads.description: Exposed head digests for multi-value cells. Mutually exclusive with value_digest.

last_covered_event.description: event_digest of the latest DataEvent the notary observed for this cell within the Seal window.

value_digest.description: Digest of the canonical single join value. Mutually exclusive with heads.

schemas/key-view-proof.schema.json.description: Inclusion proof for one KeyView record against a Seal's data_view_root (authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md sections 6.4 and 10). data_view_root is the RFC 6962 Merkle root over canonical KeyView leaves sorted by cell_id; this proof lets a light client verify 'this Seal observed and committed this local join result for this cell' without global state. The proof is observational: absence of a KeyView never invalidates a DataEvent, and verifiers MUST NOT treat it as finality.

audit_path.description: RFC 6962 Merkle audit path from the canonical KeyView leaf to data_view_root. Leaf input is H(0x00 || canonical_json(key_view)); interior nodes are H(0x01 || left || right).

data_view_root.description: MUST equal the data_view_root field of the referenced Seal; the verifier checks the Seal signature separately.

schemas/key-view-proof.schema.json.title: Cokret KeyViewProof

last_resort.description: When true, this claim record returns a reusable last-resort KeyPackage (RFC 9420 Section 10) because the single-use pool was empty. The package may be reused within the same intended_realm_id and is not transitioned to consumed; the holder MUST rotate it and trigger group updates on next online. Optional capability gated by ck.feature.mls_last_resort_keypackage.v1. See encryption-and-audit.md section 2.6.2.

key_package.description: Base64url encoding of the canonical MLS KeyPackage bytes.

last_resort.description: When true, this entry is a reusable last-resort KeyPackage (RFC 9420 Section 10). It is not consumed single-use; it cycles between published and claimed until rotated, expired, or revoked. Optional capability gated by ck.feature.mls_last_resort_keypackage.v1. See encryption-and-audit.md section 2.6.2.

object_ref.description: Opaque content-addressed or service-scoped reference. Hash-shaped refs MUST use keypackage_digest for digest bytes.

schemas/keypackage-operations.schema.jso.description: Closed request and response DTOs for ck.keys.keypackages.{upload,claim,consume,revoke}. Individual OpenAPI components reference the $defs entries in this bundle.
schemas/keypackage-operations.schema.jso.title: Cokret MLS KeyPackage Operation DTOs

keys_backups_unlock_request_body.description: Request body for ck.self.keys.backups.unlock. The unlock proof MUST validate as ck.schema.key_backup_unlock_proof.v1 and MUST be verified against the recovery session, caller, requesting device key, active-series record, and target envelope before the full ciphertext is returned (key-management.md §7.7.1 / §7.8). The path backup_id and proof.backup_id MUST match.

schemas/keys-operations.schema.json.description: Closed request and response DTOs for ck.keys.{upload,query,claim} and ck.keys.backups.{put,list,delete}. Individual OpenAPI components reference the $defs entries in this bundle.
schemas/keys-operations.schema.json.title: Cokret Device Key Operation DTOs

schemas/list-handles-for-subject-respons.description: Result body for ck.directory.list_handles_for_subject. It lists currently visible handle claims for a disclosed holder/principal subject DID in the caller's context. Every claim in claims[] MUST have claim.subject byte-for-byte equal to this response subject.

as_of.description: As-of timestamp used to build the visible claim set and primary handle selection.

claims.description: Current context-visible signed handle claims. Each item MUST have subject equal to the top-level subject; mismatches MUST be dropped or fail the response closed.

primary_handle.description: Optional canonical primary handle selected from claims[] by identity-handles.md section 3.2.1 for the same context/as_of. The @ mention sigil is not part of this field.

subject.description: Holder/principal DID used as the reverse lookup key. This is not a Realm actor_id.

schemas/list-handles-for-subject-respons.title: Cokret Directory Subject Handle List

not.$comment: byte counts use size_bytes

thumbnails.description: Bound thumbnail / preview descriptors. Producers SHOULD prefer this over preview_blob_ref for private or E2EE media.

schemas/media-operations.schema.json.description: Closed request DTOs for realtime media service operations. ck.self.media.ice_config responses use ice-config-response.schema.json.
schemas/media-operations.schema.json.title: Cokret Realtime Media Operation DTOs

schemas/member-delivery-binding-candidat.description: Builder-side candidate object that ferries Handle resolution output (intent=member_add | invite) or a trusted-issuer-signed equivalent into the Realm member_add / invite pipeline. Produces a Realm-scoped member_delivery_binding only after the reducer independently re-validates against Join Policy. See identity-handles.md §3.7.

audience.description: Target Realm ID or inviting service DID. Verifier MUST reject candidates whose audience does not match the current invocation context.

claim_digest.description: sha256 digest over JCS(semantic_projection(upstream handle claim)) per zh/identity/identity-handles.md ?3.2.1; it is not a digest over the whole upstream handle claim object.

expires_at.description: RFC 3339 UTC timestamp. Expired candidates MUST NOT enter the builder.

handle.description: Cokret canonical handle string: <localpart>:<domain>. acct: aliases and @ mention spelling are rejected here.

handle_aliases.description: Optional interop aliases (RFC 7565 acct:). Never used for cache keys, signature transcripts, or delivery_binding materialisation.

intent.description: Builder entry point. Advisory for audit / telemetry; reducer behaviour does not branch on this field.

issued_at.description: RFC 3339 UTC timestamp marking when the issuer signed the candidate. Required: paired with expires_at to give verifiers a replay-protection window and to detect retro-dated candidates. issued_at MUST be <= expires_at.

issuer_service_did.description: Service DID that signed the candidate (Directory service DID, Principal Server service DID, or Organization service DID).

binding_source.description: MUST NOT be did_document_default — handle-resolved candidates and DID Document fallback are independent materialisation paths.

proofs.description: At least one proof binding handle, subject_id, member_delivery_binding.recipient_service_did, audience, issuer_service_did, issued_at, expires_at and (when present) claim_digest. issued_at MUST be inside the signed transcript so an MITM cannot widen the replay-protection window by rewriting it; verifiers MUST reject proofs whose canonical transcript omits issued_at.

source_refs.description: Event references at the issuer / Directory / Organization that back this candidate; clients SHOULD re-verify against the truth source.

subject_id.description: Principal DID of the addressee. Materialised as payload.actor_id / cell subject in ck.member.state{membership=join}.

schemas/member-delivery-binding-candidat.title: Cokret Member Delivery Binding Candidate

schemas/member-identity.schema.json.description: Realm-scoped, actor-scoped full member_identity segment. It is carried by ck.member.identity.update in plaintext or inside encrypted-envelope.schema.json. Replacement events that name segment=member_identity MUST carry this complete object. This object discloses subject_id and display_profile for Realm UI projection; handle lifecycle is intentionally excluded and is governed only by ck.schema.handle_claim.v1 issuer claims. Mention / reply / quote / actor attribution MUST use subject_id (the principal DID), never a handle string.

actor_id.description: Effective member actor DID in this Realm. MAY be a Realm-scoped pairwise DID.

payload_digest.description: sha256 over RFC 8785 JCS canonical JSON of this MemberIdentity object with the top-level proof field excluded. The signature MUST cover the same canonical bytes.

subject_id.description: Principal DID or disclosed holder DID represented by actor_id for display purposes. Authorization and audit continue to use the Event actor and member state.

schemas/member-identity.schema.json.title: Cokret Member Identity

schemas/message.schema.json.$comment: Top-level uses unevaluatedProperties (not additionalProperties) because the top-level oneOf branches contribute evaluated properties; additionalProperties at the top level would not see those and could wrongly reject legitimate oneOf-branch fields (JSON Schema additionalProperties/oneOf pitfall).

agent_slug.description: Controller-scoped native personal agent selector slug used by @<controller-handle>/<agent_slug>. Not a global handle or authorization subject.

not.$comment: Mirror of event-payload.schema.json $defs.content_block: reject discriminator field `type` (canonical: `kind`), composite child array name `blocks` (canonical: `parts`), and byte-count field `size` (canonical: `size_bytes`). Keeps materialized Message and Event payload schemas in lockstep so that the materialized Message.content cannot smuggle through wire-forbidden field names.

controller_subject_id.description: Audit metadata for @<controller-handle>/<agent_slug> inputs. MUST NOT replace subject_id for routing, authorization, or attribution.

subject_id.description: Authoritative mention target principal DID. For native personal agent selectors this is the agent principal DID, not the controller DID.

message_metadata.description: Extensible user-readable Message metadata. In MLS / E2EE realms this object is encrypted as encrypted_metadata unless the Realm explicitly opts into plaintext metadata.

not.$comment: Reducer-owned fields stay top-level and MUST NOT be mirrored inside metadata.

metadata_fields.description: Profile-defined Message metadata fields. Reducer-owned lifecycle and revision fields are forbidden here to avoid dual sources of truth.

anyOf.$comment: forbidden encrypted content carrier; canonical name is encrypted_content
forbidden track key; canonical name is track_name
forbidden Message extension metadata; canonical path is metadata.fields or encrypted_metadata

effective_scope.description: Reducer-stamped immutable effective scope of this Message, materialized from the scope_circle_id effective at create time (models/circle.md §6.1-§6.2). kind='realm' for Realm-default scope; kind='circle' when the message's Flow was Circle-scoped at write time. Immutable: a later Flow scope rebind MUST NOT reinterpret already-written messages — each message retains its write-time effective_scope and old-scope history/key eligibility. MUST NOT appear in actor-supplied submit payload (reducer-managed, reason=effective_scope_reducer_managed); the reducer stamps it on accept.

encrypted_content.description: Encrypted envelope whose plaintext is the Message ContentBlock.

encrypted_metadata.description: Encrypted envelope whose plaintext is a message_metadata object.

redaction_ref.description: Required when state=redacted; references the ck.message.redact event that produced this state. MUST be absent for other states.

revision_root.description: First revision in this message's edit chain. The first revision MUST have revision_root == id. Maintained by ck.message.revise reducer.

state.description: Top-level lifecycle state for messages. Messages do not have a separate deleted/tombstone state; retention or moderation removal uses ck.message.redact and state=redacted so the message slot and audit metadata remain stable.

state_changed_at.description: Reducer-derived timestamp of the most recent state transition. MUST be set when state != 'active'; MUST be the created_at of the corresponding ck.message.redact Event. Aligns with the common-fields rule in models/common-fields.md §3.

track_name.description: Flow track key for this Message. v1 Message objects are restricted to the Flow discussion track. Profiles that need another timeline kind MUST register a separate object/event profile instead of overloading Message.track_name.

updated_by.description: Reducer-derived actor that produced the most recent materialized message update, such as ck.message.revise or ck.message.redact.

schemas/message.schema.json.title: Cokret Message

schemas/mimi-interop.schema.json.$comment: Intentionally relaxed interop-extension surface: this profile tracks evolving IETF MIMI Internet-Drafts (see zh/extensions/mimi-interop.md §1), so additionalProperties is left open at the top level and on the mimi/binding_scope/payload subtrees to forward-carry draft fields without a breaking schema bump. Known fields are pinned; unknown draft fields are tolerated rather than rejected. The proof object below gives a minimal required core so the openness is limited to known extension subtrees and does not mask a missing signature. Unknown fields anywhere on this surface are security-inert (see zh/extensions/mimi-interop.md §9.2): receivers MUST ignore them for all security decisions and MUST NOT let them affect authorization, identity binding, policy_root, MLS epoch/group state, routing, or any signature/digest transcript.

room_binding.description: MIMI room binding effect payload. In CBA/Lattice state, the cell subject is payload.mimi_room_uri for ck.component.mimi.room_binding.v1.

status.description: Room binding lifecycle status. Initial status MUST be proposed or accepted; legal transitions are proposed->accepted, proposed->revoked, accepted->migrating, accepted->revoked, migrating->accepted (verified migration proof), migrating->revoked. revoked is the only terminal state; illegal transitions are rejected with mimi_room_binding_status_transition_invalid. Normative state machine: zh/extensions/mimi-interop.md §4.2.

schemas/mimi-interop.schema.json.description: Provider directory, room binding, and content mapping receipt objects for ck.profile.mimi_interop.v1.
schemas/mimi-interop.schema.json.title: Cokret MIMI Interoperability

schemas/mimi-operations.schema.json.description: Closed request/response DTOs for MIMI provider interop operation bindings.
schemas/mimi-operations.schema.json.title: Cokret MIMI Operation DTOs

close_payload.description: ck.moderation.appeal.close — closes the appeal from submitted/under_review/decided. Reviewer close and timer auto-close use the review capability; appellant withdrawal is authorized by closer == appellant while state is submitted or under_review. Locks against re-appealing the same (decision_ref, appellant) pair within the policy cool-off window; new appeals after the cool-off are allowed via a fresh appeal_id.

auto_closed.description: true iff the close was triggered by a timer (submitted/review inactivity timeout or decided + Realm.appeal_window_ms <= now); false iff explicitly closed by an authorized actor.

close_reason.description: Machine-readable close cause. appellant_withdrawn is valid only when closer is the appellant and the appeal is still submitted or under_review; timer_expired requires auto_closed=true.

closer.description: Actor or service closing the appeal. If auto_closed=true, reducer MUST require closer to be a timer service DID listed in Realm policy and MUST enforce closed_at >= decided_at + appeal_window_ms.

decision_payload.description: ck.moderation.appeal.decision — reviewer's verdict. Transitions cell state under_review → decided. Verdict semantics: uphold = original decision stands, no further action; overturn = original decision reversed, this event MUST be paired in the same ordered submit batch or equivalent control transaction with a ck.moderation.decision.lift event whose target equals decision_ref (reducer rejects with appeal_overturn_missing_lift otherwise); modify = original decision adjusted (parameters revised), modify_decision_ref MUST point to a new ck.moderation.decision event in the same batch that supersedes the original.

modify_decision_ref.description: Required iff verdict=modify. Points to the replacement ck.moderation.decision event in the same ordered submit batch or equivalent control transaction.

reason_text_ref.description: Reference to the verdict rationale. MUST be present for audit trail; visibility follows evidence_visibility on the submit event.

decision_ref.description: Reference to the ck.moderation.decision event being appealed.

evidence_visibility.description: Who may decrypt / read the appeal evidence narrative. Default per Realm policy; SHOULD be reviewers_only for sensitive disputes. The visibility tag MUST enter projection / redaction decisions; it does NOT change wire encryption of the envelope, only the plaintext audience for evidence fields.

review_payload.description: ck.moderation.appeal.review — reviewer takes the appeal under review. Transitions cell state submitted → under_review. Reviewer MUST hold ck.moderation.appeal.review capability; the same actor MUST NOT review their own moderation decision (separation of duties enforced by reducer).

submit_payload.description: ck.moderation.appeal.submit — opens the appeal. Writes appeal cell (state=submitted). MUST be issued by an appellant who is the original moderation target's controller (member appealing their own ban / message removal) or by an authorized advocate listed in Realm policy. appellant MUST hold ck.moderation.appeal.submit capability.

appellant.description: Actor lodging the appeal. MUST be the original moderation target's controller or an authorized advocate.

evidence_refs.description: Optional supporting evidence (blob refs, prior message ids, witness DIDs).

reason_text_ref.description: Reference (typically blob_ref or in-line short string) to the appeal narrative / supporting argument. For E2EE Realms this is an encrypted reference.

target_ref.description: The original moderation target (message, flow, member, blob, etc.) — same typed-id form as the appealed decision's target.

schemas/moderation-appeal.schema.json.description: Payload shapes for the four ck.moderation.appeal.* event kinds (submit / review / decision / close) that close the moderation appeal loop. Each kind writes the ck.component.moderation_appeal.v1 cell on a deterministic state machine: (none) → submitted → under_review → decided → closed, with close also allowed from submitted/under_review for appellant withdrawal or timer auto-close. The decided state additionally records the verdict (uphold / overturn / modify); overturn MUST be paired in the same ordered submit batch or equivalent control transaction with a ck.moderation.decision.lift event referencing the original decision. All payloads carry realm_id and reducers MUST require it to equal the enclosing Event.realm_id and the appealed decision's Realm. See zh/governance/content-moderation.md §5.5 (appeal flow). Capability: ck.moderation.appeal.submit (any member, low risk) for submit; ck.moderation.appeal.review (moderator) for review/decision/manual reviewer close; appellant withdrawal is authorized by closer == appellant.
schemas/moderation-appeal.schema.json.title: Cokret Moderation Appeal

status.description: Authoritative moderation queue-item lifecycle. v1 is intentionally minimal: 'submitted' = report accepted and awaiting handling; 'resolved' = handling complete (terminal). The disposition (action taken vs no violation) lives on the separate ck.moderation.decision event; the appeal loop lives in the independent ck.moderation.appeal.* subsystem (§5.5). Additional intermediate states MAY be introduced in a later revision if a workflow phase needs them. See governance/content-moderation.md §3.3.

replay_nonce.description: Opaque anti-replay nonce generated by the receiving service and covered by the franking proof signature.

routing_metadata_digest.description: Digest of canonical event routing metadata covered by the receiving service.

mls_group_id_digest.description: Digest of the MLS group id; raw group ids MUST NOT appear in franking proofs.

signature.description: Receiving service signature over the canonical franking proof transcript.

effective_scope.description: Governance boundary for this report. When absent, the report is Realm-default. Circle-scoped targets MUST resolve to the target Circle and route only to scoped moderators/admins.

franking_proof.description: Optional franking proof metadata block. Mirrors the franking_proof object spec'd in zh/governance/content-moderation.md §3.4. It proves service receipt of ciphertext metadata; it does not prove plaintext authorship and does not grant moderators any MLS epoch/exporter secret.

status.description: Non-authoritative status mirror for client / UI convenience. The authoritative moderation lifecycle (submitted → resolved) lives on the moderation-queue-item produced by the reducer (see schemas/moderation-queue-item.schema.json + governance/content-moderation.md §3.3). Reducers MUST NOT read this field for routing or state-machine decisions; if present on submit it MUST be either absent or 'submitted'.

schemas/morph-customer-risk.schema.json.$comment: Logical schema id is ck.schema.morph.customer_risk.v1 (dotted, used in schema_refs[]); the artifact file name uses hyphens (morph-customer-risk.schema.json). Do not derive the id from the file name.
schemas/morph-customer-risk.schema.json.description: Reference business-field schema for the morph.md customer_risk example. It constrains the fields object carried by a ck.schema.morph.v1 container.
schemas/morph-customer-risk.schema.json.title: Cokret Morph Customer Risk Example

not.$comment: Reject discriminator field `type`, composite child array name `blocks`, and byte-count field `size`; canonical content blocks use `kind`, composite children use `parts`, and byte counts use `size_bytes`.

morph_metadata.description: Extensible user-readable Morph metadata. Morph business fields stay in the top-level fields object; metadata carries display-oriented fields such as title and summary. In MLS / E2EE realms this object is encrypted as encrypted_metadata unless the Realm explicitly opts into plaintext metadata.

not.$comment: Reducer-owned fields and Morph business fields stay top-level and MUST NOT be mirrored inside metadata.

anyOf.$comment: forbidden Morph top-level metadata; canonical path is metadata.title or encrypted_metadata
forbidden Morph top-level metadata; canonical path is metadata.summary or encrypted_metadata
forbidden encrypted content carrier; canonical name is encrypted_content

encrypted_content.description: Encrypted envelope whose plaintext is a ContentBlock for Morph content.

encrypted_metadata.description: Encrypted envelope whose plaintext is a morph_metadata object. Required instead of plaintext metadata when the effective metadata_encryption_floor is e2ee_required.

schema_refs.description: Authoritative schema set for Morph fields and transition validation. Reducers MUST validate fields against exactly these refs; morph_type and facets are not a replacement for schema_refs.

scope_circle_id.description: Optional reference to an intra-Realm Circle that defines this Morph's effective scope. Omitted means Realm-default scope. Reducer enforces scope_circle_id.realm_id == Morph.realm_id and stamps immutable effective_scope onto emitted events.

stage.description: Morph business-progression stage. Orthogonal to top-level 'state' (physical lifecycle). Required on ck.morph.create (no protocol-level default). The only wire path that mutates stage is the dedicated ck.morph.stage.set event; ck.morph.update / ck.morph.schema_migrate patches on stage / stage_changed_at MUST be rejected (schema_violation, single-source). Stage transitions intentionally do NOT carry a reason / note field — the ck.morph.stage.set event log is the audit source; human-readable explanations belong in a Message on an associated discussion track that references the event. See models/common-fields.md §5.3 for full semantics.

stage_changed_at.description: Reducer-derived timestamp of the most recent stage transition. MUST be ignored when present on wire; reducer overwrites with the triggering ck.morph.stage.set event's created_at. Same-value self-transitions MUST NOT update this field.

state.description: Morph lifecycle state. 'active' is the default. Reducer enforces transitions per common-fields.md §5.1: ck.morph.archive MUST come from 'active' (else failed_precondition reason=morph_not_active); ck.morph.restore MUST come from 'archived' (else morph_not_archived); ck.redaction targeting the morph MUST come from {'active','archived'} (else morph_already_terminal). Same-state self-transitions MUST fail. 'redacted' is the irreversible terminal.

state_changed_at.description: Reducer-derived timestamp of the most recent state transition. MUST be set when state != 'active'; MUST be the created_at of the corresponding ck.morph.archive / ck.morph.restore / redaction Event. Aligns with Space.state_changed_at and the common-fields rule in models/common-fields.md §3.

not.$comment: Flow track keys use track_name on current wire.

flow_id.description: Optional Flow context for routing the notification.

preview.description: Render summary. Under E2EE / redaction / history-limited scopes this MUST be empty or an authorized redacted digest; sender/reducer-enforced. A notification projection MUST NOT widen the plaintext visibility of the source Message. See models/private-objects.md §3.4.

source_ref.description: Optional canonical-object reference for clients that want to render the notification target without resolving source_event_id. Reducers MUST treat source_event_id as authoritative; source_ref is a render-only hint.

track_name.description: Optional Flow track key on the source Flow.

oneOf.$comment: Direct value form: equivalent to {"$op":"set","value":<value>}. Any JSON value EXCEPT a JSON object containing a $op discriminator may use this form.
Explicit op object form. $op is required; value is required for set/add/remove; value MUST be absent for unset.

schemas/patch.schema.json.description: Canonical field-patch format embedded in event payloads (typically at payload.patch) for non-create updates. This is a registered schema id (ck.schema.patch.v1) describing the structural form of a patch map; the embedded format identifier 'ck.patch.v1' remains the in-prose name for the same wire shape. Implementations MUST resolve ck.patch.v1 references in spec prose to this schema artifact. Grammar, parser responsibilities, selector semantics, redactable-field protection and reducer-managed-field protection are defined normatively in zh/models/event-and-patch.md §4.

propertyNames.$comment: Patch path syntax. Snake_case identifier, optional dot-separated segments, optional stable-key selectors (`field[<key>=<canonical-json-string>]`) and backtick-quoted literals for non-snake_case keys. Full ABNF in zh/models/event-and-patch.md §4.2.1. Maximum length 1024 bytes, maximum nesting depth 16 segments — exceeding either MUST yield reason_code patch_path_invalid.

schemas/patch.schema.json.title: Cokret Field Patch (ck.schema.patch.v1)

recipient_service_did.description: Principal Server service DID that hosts subject_id and accepts contact delivery for it.

recipient_service_type.description: v1 only allows Principal Server contact delivery. Omit by default; if present, the value MUST be principal_server.

subject_id.description: Principal DID of the contact fact recipient (the request target, or the original requester for an accept/reject travelling back). The recipient Principal Server projects the fact into this holder's contact projection.

disclosed_outcome.description: Optional graded-disclosure result, present only when the subject's receive policy disclosure level for this trust tier is 'outcome' and the subject did not block the issuer. Omitted (opaque) otherwise.

status.description: Generic receive status. It MUST NOT reveal whether subject_id exists or whether the holder's receive policy suppressed the fact, beyond the optional disclosed_outcome graded disclosure that mirrors ck.peer.invites.submit.

schemas/peer-contact-delivery-request.sc.description: Private service-to-service request used by an issuer-side Principal Server to deliver a signed contact fact (ck.contact.requested / ck.contact.accepted / ck.contact.rejected / ck.contact.tombstoned) to the target holder's Principal Server. The recipient projects the original signed envelope into the target holder's contact projection (pending_incoming / accepted / rejected / tombstoned); it MUST NOT re-sign the fact as its own. Contact facts are principal-scoped and cross-Realm, so this carrier is the federation delivery path for the contact fact log, separate from invite delivery.

contact_event.description: The issuer-signed contact fact EventEnvelope being delivered with its original signature, so the recipient can verify and project it without re-signing.

fact_kind.description: The contact fact kind carried by contact_event. MUST equal contact_event.kind.

schemas/peer-contact-delivery-request.sc.title: Cokret Peer Contact Delivery Request

schemas/personal-productivity.schema.jso.description: Plaintext shapes that MUST be encrypted before writing ck.profile.personal_productivity.v1 account-data values.
schemas/personal-productivity.schema.jso.title: Cokret Personal Productivity Account Data

domain_name.description: Lowercase DNS A-label domain. Matching semantics are label-boundary based and defined by governance/content-moderation.md.

policy_rule.description: Closed policy rule. Extension rules must carry an explicit schema_ref/profile_ref instead of adding undeclared fields to the signed policy body.

server_selector.description: Selector for federation server policy rules. Domain rules match normalized DNS labels only; service_did exact rules take precedence in policy evaluation.

proof.description: Detached proof over canonical_json(principal_locator_without_proofs). proof.payload_digest MUST equal that canonical payload digest.

locator_token.description: Opaque base64url locator token with at least 128 bits of entropy. It SHOULD be a server-side handle and MUST NOT plaintext-encode subject_id, recipient_service_did, expiry, policy state, or other invitee-identifying material. It MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string.

schemas/principal-locator.schema.json.description: Signed online locator returned from a holder-controlled Principal Server locator ref. It asserts the invite address used for private invite delivery; it is not a Realm membership grant and not a member_delivery_binding.

delivery_modes.description: Invite-delivery capability hints only; join-time member_delivery_binding is still materialized by Realm policy.

display_hint.description: UI-only display hint. It is not identity authority and MUST NOT be used for authorization.

expires_at.description: Time after which the locator MUST NOT be used to initiate invite delivery.

locator_ref_digest.description: Digest of the private locator ref material. The raw locator token MUST NOT appear in durable Realm events.

proofs.description: At minimum contains recipient_service_acceptance. High-assurance deployments SHOULD also require subject_locator_authorization.

recipient_service_did.description: Principal Server service DID that accepts invite delivery for subject_id.

recipient_service_type.description: v1 only allows Principal Server invite delivery. Omit by default; if present, the value MUST be principal_server.

subject_id.description: Principal DID of the invite recipient. v1 core defaults principal DIDs to did:webvh; did:web is only valid for principal identity when an explicit deployment profile or resolver policy allows it.

schemas/principal-locator.schema.json.title: Cokret Principal Locator

evaluation_locus_unresolved.description: Set true when the client has been woken but server-side rule matching is not yet resolved (E2EE client-side rule fallback). Pure local-evaluation signal; carries no metadata. See push-notifications.md §4.5.

push_hint.description: Sanitized hint sentinel. When the value is "l10n_key" the actual localization key MUST be carried in push_hint_l10n_key (this enum value is a form selector, not a literal display token). See push-notifications.md §5.1 / §4.5.

push_hint_l10n_key.description: Localization key value, only present (and required) when push_hint == "l10n_key". MUST be an l10n key token, never plaintext body or any identifying metadata.

badge.description: Coarse unread indicator. Under blind_wakeup it MUST NOT carry a plaintext absolute unread count (activity side channel); only a boolean presence flag or a policy-declared bucket string is allowed. See push-notifications.md §5.1.

push_target_id.description: Pairwise pseudonym for one (recipient_service_did, principal, device, push_route) tuple. It MUST NOT be a DID, DID URL, Realm id, Flow id, Message id, Event id, or stable cross-Realm correlation key.

registration_id.description: Push gateway local registration id. It is not a registered ck:<kind> protocol object id.

evaluation_locus_unresolved.description: Set true when the client has been woken but server-side rule matching is not yet resolved. See push-notifications.md §4.5.

push_hint.description: Sanitized hint sentinel. When the value is "l10n_key" the actual localization key MUST be carried in push_hint_l10n_key (this enum value is a form selector, not a literal display token). See push-notifications.md §5.1 / §4.5.

push_hint_l10n_key.description: Localization key value, only present (and required) when push_hint == "l10n_key".

schemas/push-operations.schema.json.description: Closed request and response DTOs for ck.edge.push.register_device, ck.edge.push.unregister_device, and ck.push.notify.
schemas/push-operations.schema.json.title: Cokret Push Gateway Operation DTOs

key_view_ref.description: Optional root/proof reference for the data-plane KeyView used by this projection.

context_ref.description: Optional timeline / renderer context object reference. This is not a Seal.

schemas/query.schema.json.description: Canonical wire schema for client query / projection and search request bodies and their reusable building blocks (filters, sort, relation query). The OpenAPI document references these $defs so there is a single source of truth. Human-readable semantics: zh/conformance/query-schema.md. facet_name / view_renderer are copies of the shared OpenAPI enums (kept local so this file is self-contained); the authoritative facet / renderer enums also live in the OpenAPI components and MUST stay in lockstep.
schemas/query.schema.json.title: Cokret Query / Search Request Shapes

schemas/range-completeness-attestation.s.description: A range-bound completeness attestation. Event kind: ck.attestation.range_completeness (active in event-kind-registry; the event kind itself carries NO .v1 suffix). Payload schema id: ck.schema.range_completeness_attestation.v1 (schemas keep the .v1 versioning). The attestation asserts that the issuer (and any witnesses) have observed every reducer-input event in a declared range — (from_frontier, to_frontier) bounded by explicit per-actor seq intervals — where each frontier is a Realm-scoped frontier (property name realm_frontier; the security/replication boundary for completeness in v1 is the Realm, not an in-Realm Space container). Distinct from ck.event_batch_receipt (set-bound integrity over an arbitrary chosen subset) and ck.audit.ryw_receipt (per-event RYW hint). Used when verifiers need a completeness claim — i.e., 'no event has been silently withheld from this range' — not just 'the events given are unmodified'. Standalone single-issuer attestations are NOT sufficient for sovereign / multi-writer trust models; deployments requiring strong completeness MUST use a witness_attestation block following the ck.audit.ryw_receipt model (zh/crypto-media/audited-e2ee.md §4.1.1).

count.description: Number of reducer-input events in scope. MUST match the number of leaves used to compute root.

actor_seq_ranges.description: Per-actor seq intervals attested. Silent forks frequently appear as a missing slice in a single actor's seq sequence while the global frontier still advances monotonically — explicit per-actor ranges close that gap. MUST cover every actor that produced reducer-input events in (from_frontier, to_frontier].

from_seq_exclusive.description: Per-actor seq lower bound (exclusive). -1 means 'from actor genesis'.

to_seq_inclusive.description: Per-actor seq upper bound (inclusive). Issuer asserts completeness of every actor_seq in the half-open interval (from_seq_exclusive, to_seq_inclusive].

from_frontier.description: Lower bound of the range (exclusive). The attestation covers events causally after this frontier.

observed_at.description: When the issuer finished observing the scope and computed the attestation.

root.description: Canonical Merkle root over the sorted set of (actor_id, actor_seq, event_id, event_digest) tuples for every reducer-input event in scope. Digest algorithm agility per Realm.digest_algorithm.

schema.description: Payload schema id (versioned). The owning Event kind in event-kind-registry.json is ck.attestation.range_completeness (NO .v1 suffix on the event kind).

kind.description: Same semantics as ck.audit.ryw_receipt.witness_attestation: 'federation_witness_attested' requires witnesses[].length >= 2 with pairwise-distinct issuer/controlling_organization/verification_method, each listed by Realm policy in audit.range_completeness_witnesses[]. 'single_source' is the honest declaration for self-attested deployments. Mismatch between kind and witnesses[] cardinality / distinctness / policy listing MUST be rejected. Receivers SHOULD treat single_source attestations as advisory only and not as a sovereign-grade completeness proof.

schemas/range-completeness-attestation.s.title: Cokret Range-bound Completeness Attestation

schemas/read-cursor.schema.json.description: Actor-private multi-device read cursor. Stored in encrypted account data or actor-private stream; NEVER published into a shared Realm Event history. Bound to (actor_id, realm_id, read_scope, position, HLC, device_id) per zh/discovery/read-receipts.md §6.6 so that concurrent updates from multiple devices converge by HLC max.

device_id.description: Originating device. Required for multi-device convergence: when two devices race on the same (actor_id, realm_id, read_scope) the receiver picks the entry with greater HLC; device_id provides a deterministic actor_id-scoped tiebreaker when HLCs are equal.

kind.description: Read-scope object kind per zh/models/private-objects.md §2.2. Track-scoped read cursors use kind='flow' plus track_name. Thread cursors use kind='thread' with ref = the thread root message id (zh/discovery/read-receipts.md §5); thread is a projection selector over the reply sub-timeline, not a first-class protocol object. Shares the read-scope discriminator family with read-receipt.schema.json; each schema declares its own supported subset.

ref.description: Required when kind is circle, space, flow, or thread; omitted for kind='realm'. Thread read scopes reference the root message.

track_name.description: Required when kind='flow' AND the cursor scopes a single track (e.g. 'discussion', 'synthesis', or any profile-registered track name). Track names MUST match the Flow's registered tracks; unknown tracks MUST be rejected with schema_violation.

schemas/read-cursor.schema.json.title: Cokret Read Cursor

schemas/read-receipt.schema.json.description: Public/shared read receipt for Flow timeline UI hint. NOT canonical truth, NOT a multi-device cursor (see read-cursor.schema.json for that). MUST NOT generate push notifications. Privacy is governed by Realm policy: Realms MAY allow public, members-only, or actor-private receipt sharing.

event_id.description: ID of the most recent Event the actor has read. Causality implies all causal predecessors are also read.

hlc.description: Optional. HLC of the read position; required when Sync Service must compare receipts under merge / debounce rules across devices for the same actor.

kind.description: Read-scope discriminator from the same family as read-cursor.schema.json; each schema declares its own supported subset (receipt additionally supports view/message/morph; cursor additionally supports circle/space). kind='thread' selects the reply sub-timeline rooted at a message (zh/discovery/read-receipts.md §5); thread is a projection selector, not a first-class protocol object.

ref.description: Required when kind is anything other than 'realm'. Thread read scopes reference the root message.

track_name.description: Required when kind='flow' and the receipt scopes a single track.

track_scope.description: Only valid when kind='flow'. Use track_scope='all' for an entire Flow regardless of track.

schemas/read-receipt.schema.json.title: Cokret Read Receipt

schemas/realm-join-candidate.schema.json.description: Time-bounded routing hint for submitting Realm join, invite-accept, knock, or restricted-join material through a qualified Realm service. This object is not membership authorization and is distinct from member_delivery_binding.

as_of.description: Time when the issuer observed or refreshed this candidate.

endpoint.description: Optional endpoint hint. Callers MUST re-resolve the service DID document before transport and MUST NOT treat this field as authority.

expires_at.description: Time after which clients MUST NOT use this candidate without re-resolving the Realm.

frontier_ref.description: Optional digest of the candidate service's advertised Realm frontier at as_of; used only to detect stale hints.

join_methods.description: Join-side flows this candidate claims to support for this requester and Realm.

operations.description: Endpoint-callable operation ids available at this candidate. Join-side routing requires ck.events.submit.

priority.description: Lower values are preferred. Ties are broken deterministically by service_did.

proofs.description: Optional proof set binding realm_id, service_did, role, operations, join_methods, as_of, and expires_at. Required when the candidate is carried outside a freshly resolved Directory response.

realm_id.description: Realm this candidate is bound to. Verifiers MUST reject a candidate used for any other Realm.

role.description: Routing role within the Realm candidate set. This is a hint for ordering and diagnostics, not an authorization grant.

service_did.description: Service DID that can receive or relay join-side submissions for this Realm.

service_type.description: Service class. principal_server is the normal candidate; sync_node and notary are allowed only when Realm policy authorizes them to receive join-side submissions.

source.description: Where this routing hint came from. Receivers still validate against current Realm policy and service DID documents.

source_refs.description: Realm or directory source events that justify this candidate, such as discovery, service-binding, or sync endpoint state.

schemas/realm-join-candidate.schema.json.title: Cokret Realm Join Candidate

allOf.$comment: Security-root roles are always control-plane.
sealed=true is the explicit data-to-control opt-in.
initial_value is only defined for cas_register (see event-auth-state-resolution.md §5.3.3). Other lattices reject the field.

sentinel_writers is the companion of initial_value; it only makes sense on a cas_register cell that has declared initial_value. Reject declarations on other lattices, and reject declarations on cas_register cells that lack initial_value (since there is no sentinel to authorise writing back).

cell_role.description: Semantic role declared by Realm schema. authorization_root / policy_root / notary_root / membership / lifecycle MUST NOT use lattice types lww_register or rga (enforced by allOf below). ui_affordance / content / draft / cosmetic MAY use lww_register or rga.

initial_value.description: Optional cell schema initial value (cas_register only). When defined, the cas_register `join` algorithm initialises `current` to this value (rather than null) before applying any Move. Combined with a `head_eq: <initial_value>` predicate on the first set Move, this implements singleton-once-set cells via the empty sentinel pattern. See event-auth-state-resolution.md §5.3.3.

plane.description: CBA plane for this cell family. authorization_root / policy_root / notary_root / membership / lifecycle MUST be control. Ordinary content / draft / cosmetic cells SHOULD be data unless sealed=true.

sealed.description: Opt-in control-plane finality for an otherwise data-like cell family. When true, plane MUST be control.

sentinel_writers.description: Optional companion to `initial_value` (cas_register only). When `initial_value` is declared, set ops whose effect equals the sentinel are rejected by default (initial_value_reserved). Listing event_kinds here permits those event_kinds to write the sentinel back — typically the cleanup event_kind in a singleton-once-set / explicit-reset workflow. Capability authorization remains a separate independent check. See event-auth-state-resolution.md §5.3.3.

allOf.$comment: single_did notary profiles must declare an explicit recovery notary path at Realm create time. Distinct controlling organization is semantic/reducer validation because JSON Schema cannot compare DID-controller derivations across resolver evidence.

Threshold notary committees must declare their equivocation culprit-attribution mode at Realm create time. The arithmetic rule (quorum_intersection iff 2*threshold > members.length) is reducer/conformance validation; see notary.forensic_attribution $comment.

Principal control Realms are ordinary ck.schema.realm.v1 objects, but the profile discriminator must be closed at schema level: fields.purpose and schema_refs must appear together, the Realm MUST be MLS-backed, and both encryption floors MUST be pinned to e2ee_required (key-management §4.1 / §5.0.1, realm-and-space §2.8.1). There is no plaintext-floor PCR in v1.
The inverse guard prevents a profile-tagged Realm from omitting the machine-readable purpose discriminator, and pins the encryption floors symmetrically with the forward guard.

not.$comment: forbidden Realm authorship field; canonical name is created_by
